ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S1.text: Few creations of big technology capture the imagination like giant dams.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 很少有大型科技作品能像巨型水坝那样激发人们的想象力。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S2.text: Perhaps it is humankind's long suffering at the mercy of flood and drought that makes the idea of forcing the waters to do our bidding so fascinating.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 也许正是人类长期遭受洪水和干旱的折磨，才使得强迫水域听从我们的命令的想法如此令人着迷。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S3.text: But to be fascinated is also, sometimes, to be blind.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 但有时候，着迷也意味着盲目。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S4.text: Several giant dam projects threaten to do more harm than good.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 几个巨型水坝项目可能弊大于利。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S5.text: The lesson from dams is that big is not always beautiful.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 大坝的教训是，大并不总是美丽的。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S6.text: It doesn't help that building a big, powerful dam has become a symbol of achievement for nations and people striving to assert themselves.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S6.translation: 建造一座强大的大坝已成为努力维护自己的国家和人民成就的象征，这无济于事。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S7.text: Egypt's leadership in the Arab world was cemented by the Aswan High Dam.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P1-S7.translation: 阿斯旺大坝巩固了埃及在阿拉伯世界的领导地位。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S1.text: Turkey's bid for First World status includes the giant Ataturk Dam.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 土耳其对第一世界地位的争夺包括巨型阿塔图尔克大坝。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S2.text: But big dams tend not to work as intended.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 但大坝往往无法按预期发挥作用。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S3.text: The Aswan Dam, for example, stopped the Nile flooding but deprived Egypt of the fertile silt that floods left—all in return for a giant reservoir of disease which is now so full of silt that it barely generates electricity.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S3.translation: 例如，阿斯旺大坝阻止了尼罗河的洪水，但剥夺了埃及洪水留下的肥沃淤泥——所有这些都换来了一个巨大的疾病库，现在这个库已经充满了淤泥，几乎无法发电。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S4.text: And yet, the myth of controlling the waters persists.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S4.translation: 然而，控制水域的神话依然存在。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S5.text: This week, in the heart of civilized Europe, Slovaks and Hungarians stopped just short of sending in the troops in their contention over a dam on the Danube.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: 本周，在文明欧洲的中心，斯洛伐克人和匈牙利人差点就派出军队来争夺多瑙河上的一座大坝。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S6.text: The huge complex will probably have all the usual problems of big dams.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S6.translation: 这个巨大的综合体可能会遇到大型水坝的所有常见问题。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S7.text: But Slovakia is bidding for independence from the Czechs, and now needs a dam to prove itself.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P2-S7.translation: 但斯洛伐克正在争取从捷克独立，现在需要一座大坝来证明自己。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S1.text: Meanwhile, in India, the World Bank has given the go-ahead to the even more wrong-headed Narmada Dam.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 与此同时，在印度，世界银行批准了更加错误的讷尔默达大坝建设。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S2.text: And the bank has done this even though its advisors say the dam will cause hardship for the powerless and environmental destruction.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 尽管该银行的顾问表示，大坝会给弱势群体带来困难，而且还会造成环境破坏，但该银行还是这么做了。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S3.text: The benefits are for the powerful, but they are far from guaranteed.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 强者会得到好处，但远不能保证。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S4.text: Proper, scientific study of the impacts of dams and of the cost and benefits of controlling water can help to resolve these conflicts.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: 对水坝的影响以及控制水的成本和效益进行适当的科学研究有助于解决这些冲突。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S5.text: Hydroelectric power and flood control and irrigation are possible without building monster dams.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: 无需建造巨型水坝即可实现水力发电、防洪和灌溉。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S6.text: But when you are dealing with myths, it is hard to be either proper or scientific.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 但当你处理神话时，很难做到正确或科学。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S7.text: It is time that the world learned the lessons of Aswan.
ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S7.translation: 现在是世界吸取阿斯旺教训的时候了。

ky-en1-1998-r-t1#P3-S8.text: You don't need a dam to be saved.

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S1.text: Well, no gain without pain, they say.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 他们说，没有痛苦就没有收获。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S2.text: But what about pain without gain?
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 但如果没有收获又如何呢？

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S3.text: Everywhere you go in America, you hear tales of corporate revival. What is harder to establish is whether the productivity revolution that businessmen assume they are presiding over is for real. The official statistics are mildly discouraging.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 无论你走到美国的哪个地方，你都会听到企业复兴的故事。更难确定的是，商界人士认为他们正在主导的生产力革命是否是真实的。官方统计数据有些令人沮丧。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S4.text: They show that, if you lump manufacturing and services together, productivity has grown on average by 1.2% since 1987.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 他们表明，如果将制造业和服务业放在一起，自 1987 年以来，生产率平均增长了 1.2%。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S5.text: That is somewhat faster than the average during the previous decade.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S5.translation: 这比过去十年的平均水平要快一些。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S6.text: And since 1991, productivity has increased by about 2% a year, which is more than twice the 1978-87 average.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P1-S6.translation: 自 1991 年以来，生产率每年增长约 2%，是 1978-87 年平均水平的两倍多。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S1.text: The trouble is that part of the recent acceleration is due to the usual rebound that occurs at this point in a business cycle, and so is not conclusive evidence of a revival in the underlying trend.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 问题在于，最近的加速部分是由于商业周期中此时出现的通常反弹，因此并不是基本趋势复苏的决定性证据。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S2.text: There is, as Robert Rubin, the treasury secretary, says, a "disjunction" between the mass of business anecdotes that points to a leap in productivity and the picture reflected by the statistics.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 正如财政部长罗伯特·鲁宾所说，大量指向生产力飞跃的商业轶事与统计数据反映的情况之间存在“脱节”。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S3.text: Some of this can be easily explained.

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S4.text: New ways of organizing the workplace—all that re-engineering and downsizing—are only one contribution to the overall productivity of an economy, which is driven by many other factors such as joint investment in equipment and machinery, new technology, and investment in education and training.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 组织工作场所的新方式——所有的重新设计和裁员——只是对经济整体生产力的贡献之一，而整体生产力的推动因素包括对设备和机械的联合投资、新技术以及对教育和培训的投资等许多其他因素。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S5.text: Moreover, most of the changes that companies make are intended to keep them profitable, and this need not always mean increasing productivity: switching to new markets or improving quality can matter just as much.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S5.translation: 此外，公司做出的大多数改变都是为了保持盈利，这并不总是意味着提高生产力：转向新市场或提高质量同样重要。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S6.text: Two other explanations are more speculative.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P2-S6.translation: 另外两种解释更具推测性。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S1.text: First, some of the business restructuring of recent years may have been ineptly done.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 首先，近年来的一些业务重组可能做得不够好。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S2.text: Second, even if it was well done, it may have spread much less widely than people suppose.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 其次，即使做得很好，它的传播范围也可能远没有人们想象的那么广。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S3.text: Leonard Schlesinger, a Harvard academic and former chief executive of Au Bong Pain, a rapidly growing chain of bakery cafes, says that much "re-engineering" has been crude.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S3.translation: 哈佛大学学者、快速发展的面包咖啡馆连锁店 Au Bong Pain 的前首席执行官伦纳德·施莱辛格 (Leonard Schlesinger) 表示，很多“重新设计”都很粗糙。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S4.text: In many cases, he believes, the loss of revenue has been greater than the reductions in cost.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S4.translation: 他认为，在许多情况下，收入损失大于成本降低。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S5.text: His colleague, Michael Beer, says that far too many companies have applied re-engineering in a mechanistic fashion, chopping out costs without giving sufficient thought to long-term profitability.
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S5.translation: 他的同事迈克尔·比尔（Michael Beer）表示，太多公司以机械的方式进行再设计，削减成本，而没有充分考虑长期盈利能力。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S6.translation: BBDO 的 Al Rosenshine 就比较直率了。

ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S7.text: He dismisses a lot of the work of re-engineering consultants as mere rubbish—"the worst sort of ambulance chasing."
ky-en1-1998-r-t2#P3-S7.translation: 他认为重建顾问的许多工作只是垃圾——“最糟糕的救护车追逐”。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S1.text: Science has long had an uneasy relationship with other aspects of culture.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 长期以来，科学与文化的其他方面都存在着不稳定的关系。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S2.text: Think of Galileo's 17th-century trial for his rebelling belief before the Catholic Church or poet William Blake's harsh remarks against the mechanistic worldview of Isaac Newton.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 想想 17 世纪伽利略因其反叛信仰而在天主教会面前接受的审判，或者诗人威廉·布莱克对艾萨克·牛顿机械论世界观的严厉言论。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S3.text: The schism between science and the humanities has, if anything, deepened in this century.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 如果说科学与人文之间的分歧有什么不同的话，那就是本世纪加深了。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S4.text: Until recently, the scientific community was so powerful that it could afford to ignore its critics—but no longer.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 直到最近，科学界还非常强大，以至于可以忽视批评者——但现在不能了。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S5.text: As funding for science has declined, scientists have attacked "anti-science" in several books, notably Higher Superstition, by Paul R.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S5.translation: 随着科学经费的减少，科学家们在几本书中攻击了“反科学”，特别是保罗·R·肯尼迪（Paul R.

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S6.text: Gross, a biologist at the University of Virginia, and Norman Levitt, a mathematician at Rutgers University; and The Demon-Haunted World, by Carl Sagan of Cornell University.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P1-S6.translation: 弗吉尼亚大学生物学家格罗斯和罗格斯大学数学家诺曼·莱维特；以及康奈尔大学卡尔·萨根的《恶魔出没的世界》。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S1.text: Defenders of science have also voiced their concerns at meetings such as "The Flight from Science and Reason," held in New York City in 1995, and "Science in the Age of (Mis) information," which assembled last June near Buffalo.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 科学捍卫者也在 1995 年于纽约市举行的“逃离科学与理性”会议和去年 6 月在布法罗附近举行的“信息时代的科学”会议上表达了他们的担忧。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S2.text: Anti-science clearly means different things to different people.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 反科学显然对不同的人意味着不同的事情。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S3.text: Gross and Levitt find fault primarily with sociologists, philosophers and other academics who have questioned science's objectivity.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 格罗斯和莱维特主要批评社会学家、哲学家和其他质疑科学客观性的学者。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S4.text: Sagan is more concerned with those who believe in ghosts, creationism and other phenomena that contradict the scientific worldview.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 萨根更关心那些相信鬼魂、神创论和其他与科学世界观相矛盾的现象的人。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S5.text: A survey of news stories in 1996 reveals that the anti-science tag has been attached to many other groups as well, from authorities who advocated the elimination of the last remaining stocks of smallpox virus to Republicans who advocated decreased funding for basic research.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S5.translation: 对 1996 年新闻报道的调查显示，许多其他群体也被贴上了反科学的标签，从主张消灭最后剩余天花病毒的当局到主张减少基础研究经费的共和党人。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S6.text: Few would dispute that the term applies to the Unabomber, whose manifesto, published in 1995, scorns science and longs for return to a pre-technological utopia.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P2-S6.translation: 很少有人会质疑这个词适用于“大学轰炸机”，该组织于 1995 年发表的宣言蔑视科学，渴望回到前技术时代的乌托邦。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S1.text: But surely that does not mean environmentalists concerned about uncontrolled industrial growth are anti-science, as an essay in US News & World Report last May seemed to suggest.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 但这当然并不意味着担心不受控制的工业增长的环保主义者是反科学的，正如去年五月《美国新闻与世界报道》上的一篇文章所暗示的那样。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S2.text: The environmentalists, inevitably, respond to such critics.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 环保主义者不可避免地会对这些批评做出回应。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S3.text: The true enemies of science, argues Paul Ehrlich of Stanford University, a pioneer of environmental studies, are those who question the evidence supporting global warming, the depletion of the ozone layer and other consequences of industrial growth.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 环境研究先驱、斯坦福大学的保罗·埃利希认为，科学的真正敌人是那些质疑支持全球变暖、臭氧层消耗和工业增长的其他后果的证据的人。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S4.text: Indeed, some observers fear that the anti-science epithet is in danger of becoming meaningless.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 事实上，一些观察家担心反科学的绰号有变得毫无意义的危险。

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S5.text: "The term 'anti-science' can lump together too many, quite different things," notes Harvard University philosopher Gerald Holton in his 1993 work Science and Anti-Science.
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 哈佛大学哲学家杰拉尔德·霍尔顿 (Gerald Holton) 在其 1993 年的著作《科学与反科学》中指出：“‘反科学’这个词可以将太多、完全不同的事物混为一谈。”

ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S6.text: "They have in common only one thing that they tend to annoy or threaten those who regard themselves as more enlightened."
ky-en1-1998-r-t3#P3-S6.translation: “他们的共同点只有一件事，那就是他们倾向于惹恼或威胁那些自认为更开明的人。”

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S1.text: Emerging from the 1980 census is the picture of a nation developing more and more regional competition, as population growth in the Northeast and Midwest reaches a near standstill.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 1980 年的人口普查显示，随着东北部和中西部的人口增长几近停滞，国家的区域竞争日益激烈。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S2.text: This development—and its strong implications for US politics and economy in years ahead—has enthroned the South as America's most densely populated region for the first time in the history of the nation's head counting.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 这一发展及其对未来几年美国政治和经济的强烈影响使南方在美国人口统计史上首次成为美国人口最稠密的地区。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S3.text: Altogether, the US population rose in the 1970s by 23.2 million people—numerically the third-largest growth ever recorded in a single decade.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 20 世纪 70 年代，美国人口总共增加了 2320 万人，这是有记录以来十年内第三大增长。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S4.text: Even so, that gain adds up to only 11.4 percent, lowest in American annual records except for the Depression years.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S4.translation: 即便如此，这一增幅加起来也只有 11.4%，是除大萧条时期之外美国年度记录中最低的。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S5.text: Americans have been migrating south and west in larger numbers since World War II, and the pattern still prevails.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S5.translation: 自第二次世界大战以来，大量美国人向南部和西部移民，而且这种模式仍然盛行。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S6.text: Three sun-belt states—Florida, Texas and California—together had nearly 10 million more people in 1980 than a decade earlier.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P1-S6.translation: 佛罗里达州、德克萨斯州和加利福尼亚州这三个阳光地带州 1980 年的人口比十年前增加了近 1000 万。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S1.text: Among large cities, San Diego moved from 14th to 8th and San Antonio from 15th to 10th -- with Cleveland and Washington.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 在大城市中，圣地亚哥从第 14 位上升到第 8 位，圣安东尼奥从第 15 位上升到第 10 位——与克利夫兰和华盛顿一起。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S2.text: C., dropping out of the top 10.

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S3.text: Not all that shift can be attributed to the movement out of the snow belt, census officials say.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: 人口普查官员表示，并非所有的变化都可以归因于雪带的迁移。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S4.text: Nonstop waves of immigrants played a role, too—and so did bigger crops of babies as yesterday's "baby boom" generation reached its child bearing years.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 源源不断的移民浪潮也发挥了作用，随着昨天的“婴儿潮”一代到达生育年龄，婴儿数量的增加也发挥了作用。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S5.text: Moreover, demographers see the continuing shift south and west as joined by a related but newer phenomenon: More and more, Americans apparently are looking not just for places with more jobs but with fewer people, too.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S5.translation: 此外，人口统计学家认为，向南和向西的持续转移伴随着一个相关但更新的现象：越来越多的美国人显然不仅在寻找就业机会更多的地方，而且还在寻找人口更少的地方。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S6.text: Some instances: ■ Regionally, the Rocky Mountain states reported the most rapid growth rate—37.1 percent since 1970 in a vast area with only 5 percent of the US population. ■ Among states, Nevada and Arizona grew fastest of all: 63.5 and 53.1 percent respectively.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P2-S6.translation: 一些实例： ■ 从地区来看，落基山脉各州的增长率最高，自 1970 年以来增长率为 37.1%，而该地区幅员辽阔，人口仅占美国人口的 5%。 ■ 在各州中，内华达州和亚利桑那州增长最快：分别为 63.5% 和 53.1%。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S1.text: Except for Florida and Texas, the top 10 in rate of growth is composed of Western states with 7.5 million people—about 9 per square mile.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 除佛罗里达州和得克萨斯州外，增长率排名前 10 位的都是拥有 750 万人口的西部州，即每平方英里约 9 人。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S2.text: The flight from overcrowdedness affects the migration from snow belt to more bearable climates.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 逃离过度拥挤会影响从雪带向气候更适宜的迁移。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S3.text: Nowhere do 1980 census statistics dramatize more the American search for spacious living than in the Far West.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S3.translation: 1980 年的人口普查统计数据最能体现美国人对宽敞生活的追求，而远西部地区则最为突出。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S4.text: There, California added 3.7 million to its population in the 1970s, more than any other state.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S4.translation: 20 世纪 70 年代，加利福尼亚州的人口增加了 370 万，比任何其他州都多。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S5.text: In that decade, however, large numbers also migrated from California, mostly to other parts of the West.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S5.translation: 然而，在那十年里，也有大量人口从加利福尼亚州迁徙到西部其他地区。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S6.text: Often they chose—and still are choosing—somewhat colder climates such as Oregon, Idaho and Alaska in order to escape smog, crime and other plagues of urbanization in the Golden State.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S6.translation: 他们经常选择——并且仍然选择——气候稍冷的俄勒冈州、爱达荷州和阿拉斯加，以逃避金州的雾霾、犯罪和其他城市化瘟疫。

ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S7.text: As a result, California's growth rate dropped during the 1970s, to 18.5 percent—little more than two thirds the 1960s' growth figure and considerably below that of other Western states.
ky-en1-1998-r-t4#P3-S7.translation: 结果，加利福尼亚州的增长率在 20 世纪 70 年代下降至 18.5%，仅略高于 1960 年代增长率的三分之二，并且大大低于其他西部州。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S1.text: Scattered around the globe are more than 100 small regions of isolated volcanic activity known to geologists as hot spots.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S1.translation: 全球分布着 100 多个孤立的火山活动小区域，被地质学家称为热点。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S2.text: Unlike most of the world's volcanoes, they are not always found at the boundaries of the great drifting plates that make up the earth's surface; on the contrary, many of them lie deep in the interior of a plate.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S2.translation: 与世界上大多数火山不同，它们并不总是位于构成地球表面的巨大漂移板块的边界处；相反，它们中的许多都位于盘子的内部深处。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S3.text: Most of the hot spots move only slowly, and in some cases the movement of the plates past them has left trails of dead volcanoes.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S3.translation: 大多数热点移动缓慢，在某些情况下，经过它们的板块运动会留下死火山的痕迹。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S4.text: The hot spots and their volcanic trails are milestones that mark the passage of the plates.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S4.translation: 热点及其火山轨迹是标志着板块移动的里程碑。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S5.text: That the plates are moving is now beyond dispute.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P1-S5.translation: 板块正在移动，这一点现在已无可争议。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S1.text: Africa and South America, for example, are moving away from each other as new material is injected into the sea floor between them.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S1.translation: 例如，随着新物质被注入非洲和南美洲之间的海底，非洲和南美洲正在彼此远离。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S2.text: The complementary coastlines and certain geological features that seem to span the ocean are reminders of where the two continents were once joined.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S2.translation: 互补的海岸线和某些似乎跨越海洋的地质特征提醒人们，这两个大陆曾经是连接在一起的。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S3.text: The relative motion of the plates carrying these continents has been constructed in detail, but the motion of one plate with respect to another cannot readily be translated into motion with respect to the earth's interior.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S3.translation: 承载这些大陆的板块的相对运动已经被详细构建，但是一个板块相对于另一个板块的运动不能轻易地转化为相对于地球内部的运动。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S4.text: It is not possible to determine whether both continents are moving in opposite directions or whether one continent is stationary and the other is drifting away from it.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S4.translation: 无法确定两个大陆是否朝相反方向移动，或者一个大陆是否静止而另一个大陆正在远离它。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S5.text: Hot spots, anchored in the deeper layers of the earth, provide the measuring instruments needed to resolve the question.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P2-S5.translation: 位于地球深层的热点提供了解决该问题所需的测量仪器。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S1.text: From an analysis of the hot-spot population it appears that the African plate is stationary and that it has not moved during the past 30 million years.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S1.translation: 从对热点人口的分析来看，非洲板块似乎是静止的，并且在过去 3000 万年里没有移动。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S2.text: The significance of hot spots is not confined to their role as a frame of reference.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S2.translation: 热点的重要性不仅限于其作为参考框架的作用。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S3.text: It now appears that they also have an important influence on the geophysical processes that propel the plates across the globe.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S3.translation: 现在看来，它们对推动板块穿越全球的地球物理过程也有重要影响。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S4.text: When a continental plate comes to rest over a hot spot, the material rising from deeper layers creates a broad dome.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S4.translation: 当大陆板块停在热点上方时，从深层升起的物质会形成一个宽阔的圆顶。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S5.text: As the dome grows, it develops deep fissures (cracks); in at least a few cases the continent may break entirely along some of these fissures, so that the hot spot initiates the formation of a new ocean.
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S5.translation: 随着圆顶的生长，它会出现很深的裂缝（裂缝）；至少在某些情况下，大陆可能会沿着其中一些裂缝完全破裂，从而使热点开始形成新的海洋。

ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S6.text: Thus, just as earlier theories have explained the mobility of the continents, so hot spots may explain their mutability (inconstancy).
ky-en1-1998-r-t5#P3-S6.translation: 因此，正如早期的理论解释了大陆的流动性一样，热点也可以解释它们的可变性（不稳定）。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S1.text: It's a rough world out there.

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S2.text: Step outside and you could break a leg slipping on your doormat.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 走出去，你可能会因为在门垫上滑倒而摔断腿。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S3.text: Light up the stove and you could burn down the house.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 点燃炉子，你可能会烧毁房子。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S4.text: Luckily, if the doormat or stove failed to warn of a coming disaster, a successful lawsuit might compensate you for your troubles.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 幸运的是，如果门垫或炉子未能警告即将到来的灾难，一场成功的诉讼可能会弥补你的麻烦。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S5.text: Or so the thinking has gone since the early 1980s, when juries began holding more companies liable for their customers' misfortunes.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 至少自 20 世纪 80 年代初以来，这种想法就已经消失了，当时陪审团开始要求更多的公司为其客户的不幸承担责任。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S6.text: Feeling threatened, companies responded by writing ever-longer warning labels, trying to anticipate every possible accident.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P1-S6.translation: 由于感到受到威胁，公司的反应是写出越来越长的警告标签，试图预测每一次可能发生的事故。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S1.text: Today, stepladders carry labels several inches long that warn, among other things, that you might—surprise!—fall off.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 如今，梯子上贴有几英寸长的标签，除其他外，还警告您可能会（令人惊讶！）跌落。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S2.text: The label on a child's Batman cape cautions that the toy "does not enable the user to fly".
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 儿童蝙蝠侠斗篷上的标签警告说，该玩具“不能让使用者飞翔”。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S3.text: While warnings are often appropriate and necessary—the dangers of drug interactions, for example—and many are required by state or federal regulations, it isn't clear that they actually protect the manufacturers and sellers from liability if a customer is injured.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S3.translation: 虽然警告通常是适当和必要的（例如药物相互作用的危险），而且许多警告是州或联邦法规所要求的，但尚不清楚它们是否真的可以保护制造商和销售商在顾客受伤时免于承担责任。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S4.text: About 50 percent of the companies lose when injured customers take them to court.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S4.translation: 大约 50% 的公司因受伤的客户将其告上法庭而蒙受损失。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S5.text: Now the tide appears to be turning.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: 现在潮流似乎正在转变。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S6.text: As personal injury claims continue as before, some courts are beginning to side with defendants, especially in cases where a warning label probably wouldn't have changed anything.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P2-S6.translation: 随着人身伤害索赔一如既往地继续，一些法院开始站在被告一边，特别是在警告标签可能不会改变任何事情的情况下。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S1.text: In May, Julie Nimmons, president of Schutt Sports in Illinois, successfully fought a lawsuit involving a football player who was paralyzed in a game while wearing a Schutt helmet.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 今年5月，伊利诺伊州Schutt Sports公司总裁朱莉·尼蒙斯(Julie Nimmons)成功打赢了一起诉讼，该诉讼涉及一名戴着Schutt头盔在比赛中瘫痪的橄榄球运动员。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S2.text: "We're really sorry he has become paralyzed, but helmets aren't designed to prevent those kinds of injuries, " says Nimmons.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 尼蒙斯说：“我们对他瘫痪感到非常遗憾，但头盔的设计目的并不是为了防止此类伤害。”

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S3.text: The jury agreed that the nature of the game, not the helmet, was the reason for the athlete's injury.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 陪审团一致认为，比赛的性质，而不是头盔，是运动员受伤的原因。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S4.text: At the same time, the American Law Institute—a group of judges, lawyers, and academics whose recommendations carry substantial weight—issued new guidelines for tort law stating that companies need not warn customers of obvious dangers or bombard them with a lengthy list of possible ones.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: 与此同时，美国法律研究所（由法官、律师和学者组成的团体，其建议具有重大影响力）发布了新的侵权法指南，指出公司无需警告客户明显的危险或用一长串可能的危险清单轰炸他们。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S5.text: "Important information can get buried in a sea of trivialities, " says a law professor at Cornell Law School who helped draft the new guidelines.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: “重要的信息可能会被淹没在琐碎的海洋中，”帮助起草新指南的康奈尔法学院的一位法学教授说。

ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S6.text: If the moderate end of the legal community has its way, the information on products might actually be provided for the benefit of customers and not as protection against legal liability.
ky-en1-1999-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 如果法律界的温和派能够得逞，那么产品信息实际上可能是为了客户的利益而提供的，而不是为了避免法律责任。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S1.text: In the first year or so of Web business, most of the action has revolved around efforts to tap the consumer market.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 在网络业务的第一年左右，大部分行动都围绕着开拓消费者市场的努力。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S2.text: More recently, as the Web proved to be more than a fashion, companies have started to buy and sell products and services with one another.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 最近，随着网络被证明不仅仅是一种时尚，公司开始相互买卖产品和服务。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S3.text: Such business-to-business sales make sense because business people typically know what product they're looking for.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 这种企业对企业的销售是有意义的，因为商人通常知道他们正在寻找什么产品。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S4.text: Nonetheless, many companies still hesitate to use the Web because of doubts about its reliability.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 尽管如此，许多公司仍然犹豫是否使用网络，因为对其可靠性存疑。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S5.text: "Businesses need to feel they can trust the pathway between them and the supplier," says senior analyst Blane Erwin of Forrester Research.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S5.translation: “企业需要感觉到他们可以信任他们与供应商之间的途径，”Forrester Research 的高级分析师 Blane Erwin 说。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S6.text: Some companies are limiting the risk by conducting online transactions only with established business partners who are given access to the company's private intranet.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P1-S6.translation: 一些公司通过仅与有权访问公司私人内部网的既定业务合作伙伴进行在线交易来限制风险。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S1.text: Another major shift in the model for Internet commerce concerns the technology available for marketing.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 互联网商务模式的另一个重大转变涉及可用于营销的技术。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Until recently, Internet marketing activities have focused on strategies to "pull" customers into sites.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 直到最近，互联网营销活动的重点仍然是“吸引”客户进入网站的策略。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S3.text: In the past year, however, software companies have developed tools that allow companies to "push" information directly out to consumers, transmitting marketing messages directly to targeted customers.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S3.translation: 然而，在过去的一年里，软件公司开发了一些工具，使公司能够将信息直接“推送”给消费者，将营销信息直接传递给目标客户。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S4.text: Most notably, the Pointcast Network uses a screen saver to deliver a continually updated stream of news and advertisements to subscribers' computer monitors.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 最值得注意的是，Pointcast Network 使用屏幕保护程序向订户的计算机显示器提供持续更新的新闻和广告流。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S5.text: Subscribers can customize the information they want to receive and proceed directly to a company's Web site.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S5.translation: 订阅者可以定制他们想要接收的信息并直接访问公司的网站。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S6.text: Companies such as Virtual Vineyards are already starting to use similar technologies to push messages to customers about special sales, product offerings, or other events.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P2-S6.translation: Virtual Vineyards 等公司已经开始使用类似的技术向客户推送有关特价销售、产品供应或其他活动的信息。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S1.text: But push technology has earned the contempt of many Web users.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 但推送技术却遭到了许多网络用户的蔑视。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S2.text: Online culture thinks highly of the notion that the information flowing onto the screen comes there by specific request.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 网络文化高度重视屏幕上流动的信息是根据特定请求出现的这一概念。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S3.text: Once commercial promotion begins to fill the screen uninvited, the distinction between the Web and television fades.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S3.translation: 一旦商业促销开始不请自来地占据屏幕，网络和电视之间的区别就会消失。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S4.text: That's a prospect that horrifies Net purists.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S4.translation: 这种前景令网络纯粹主义者感到恐惧。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S5.text: But it is hardly inevitable that companies on the Web will need to resort to push strategies to make money.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S5.translation: 但网络公司不可避免地需要采取推送策略来赚钱。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S6.text: The examples of Virtual Vineyards, Amazon.com, and other pioneers show that a Web site selling the right kind of products with the right mix of interactivity, hospitality, and security will attract online customers.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S6.translation: Virtual Vineyards、Amazon.com 和其他先驱者的例子表明，销售正确类型的产品并具有适当的交互性、热情好客和安全性组合的网站将吸引在线客户。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S7.text: And the cost of computing power continues to free fall, which is a good sign for any enterprise setting up shop in silicon.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S7.translation: 计算能力的成本继续直线下降，这对于任何在芯片领域开设商店的企业来说都是一个好兆头。

ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S8.text: People looking back 5 or 10 years from now may well wonder why so few companies took the online plunge.
ky-en1-1999-r-t2#P3-S8.translation: 5年或10年后回顾过去，人们很可能想知道为什么很少有公司涉足在线业务。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S1.text: An invisible border divides those arguing for computers in the classroom on the behalf of students' career prospects and those arguing for computers in the classroom for broader reasons of radical educational reform.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 那些为了学生的职业前景而在课堂上争论计算机的人，和那些出于激进教育改革的更广泛原因而争论课堂上计算机的人，之间存在着一条无形的界限。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S2.text: Very few writers on the subject have explored this distinction—indeed, contradiction—which goes to the heart of what is wrong with the campaign to put computers in the classroom.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 很少有该主题的作者探讨过这种区别（实际上是矛盾），这触及了将计算机带入教室运动的问题的核心。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S3.text: An education that aims at getting a student a certain kind of job is a technical education, justified for reasons radically different from why education is universally required by law.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 旨在让学生获得某种工作的教育是技术教育，其合理性与法律普遍要求教育的原因截然不同。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S4.text: It is not simply to raise everyone's job prospects that all children are legally required to attend school into their teens.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 法律要求所有儿童到十几岁都必须上学，这不仅仅是为了提高每个人的就业前景。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S5.text: Rather, we have a certain conception of the American citizen, a character who is incomplete if he cannot competently assess how his livelihood and happiness are affected by things outside of himself.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S5.translation: 相反，我们对美国公民有一种特定的概念，如果他不能胜任地评估他的生计和幸福如何受到他自己之外的事物的影响，那么这个角色就是不完整的。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S6.text: But this was not always the case; before it was legally required for all children to attend school until a certain age, it was widely accepted that some were just not equipped by nature to pursue this kind of education.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P1-S6.translation: 但情况并非总是如此。在法律要求所有儿童到一定年龄之前必须上学之前，人们普遍认为有些人天生不具备接受这种教育的能力。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S1.text: With optimism characteristic of all industrialized countries, we came to accept that everyone is fit to be educated.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 带着所有工业化国家特有的乐观态度，我们开始接受每个人都适合接受教育的观点。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S2.text: Computer-education advocates forsake this optimistic notion for a pessimism that betrays their otherwise cheery outlook.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 计算机教育的倡导者放弃了这种乐观的观念，转而采取悲观的态度，这种悲观的态度背叛了他们原本乐观的前景。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S3.text: Banking on the confusion between educational and vocational reasons for bringing computers into schools, computer's advocates often emphasize the job prospects of graduates over their educational achievement.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 由于将计算机引入学校的教育和职业原因之间存在混淆，计算机的拥护者经常强调毕业生的就业前景而不是他们的教育成就。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S4.text: There are some good arguments for a technical education given the right kind of student.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 对于针对合适类型的学生进行技术教育有一些很好的论据。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S5.text: Many European schools introduce the concept of professional training early on in order to make sure children are properly equipped for the professions they want to join.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S5.translation: 许多欧洲学校很早就引入了专业培训的概念，以确保孩子们为他们想加入的职业做好适当的准备。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S6.text: It is, however, presumptuous to insist that there will only be so many jobs for so many scientists, so many businessmen, so many accountants.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P2-S6.translation: 然而，坚持认为只能为这么多的科学家、这么多的商人、这么多的会计师提供这么多的工作，这是自以为是的。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S1.text: Besides, this is unlikely to produce the needed number of every kind of professional in a country as large as ours and where the economy is spread over so many states and involves so many international corporations.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 此外，在我们这样一个幅员辽阔、经济分布在如此多的州、涉及如此多的跨国公司的国家里，这不太可能培养出所需数量的各类专业人员。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S2.text: But, for a small group of students, professional training might be the way to go since well-developed skills, all other factors being equal, can be the difference between having a job and not.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 但是，对于一小部分学生来说，专业培训可能是一条出路，因为在所有其他因素相同的情况下，良好的技能发展可能是找到工作与没有工作的区别。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S3.text: Of course, the basics of using any computer these days are very simple.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 当然，如今使用任何计算机的基础知识都非常简单。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S4.text: It does not take a lifelong acquaintance to pick up various software programs.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 不需要花一辈子的时间来熟悉各种软件程序。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S5.text: If one wanted to become a computer engineer, that is, of course, an entirely different story.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 如果一个人想成为一名计算机工程师，那当然是一个完全不同的故事。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S6.text: Basic computer skills take—at the very longest—a couple of months to learn.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S6.translation: 学习基本的计算机技能最长需要几个月的时间。

ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S7.text: In any case, basic computer skills are only complementary to the host of real skills that are necessary to becoming any kind of professional. It should be observed, of course, that no school, vocational or not, is helped by a confusion over its purpose.
ky-en1-1999-r-t3#P3-S7.translation: 无论如何，基本的计算机技能只是对成为任何专业人士所必需的大量实际技能的补充。当然，应该指出的是，任何一所学校，无论是职业学校还是非职业学校，都不会因其宗旨的混乱而有所帮助。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S1.text: When a Scottish research team startled the world by revealing 3 months ago that it had cloned an adult sheep, President Clinton moved swiftly.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 当苏格兰研究小组三个月前宣布克隆出一只成年绵羊时，震惊了世界，克林顿总统迅速采取了行动。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S2.text: Declaring that he was opposed to using this unusual animal husbandry technique to clone humans, he ordered that federal funds not be used for such an experiment—although no one had proposed to do so—and asked an independent panel of experts chaired by Princeton President Harold Shapiro to report back to the White House in 90 days with recommendations for a national policy on human cloning.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 他宣称反对使用这种不寻常的畜牧技术来克隆人类，并下令联邦资金不得用于此类实验（尽管没有人提议这样做），并要求由普林斯顿大学校长哈罗德·夏皮罗（Harold Shapiro）担任主席的独立专家小组在 90 天内向白宫报告，并提出有关人类克隆的国家政策的建议。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S3.text: That group—the National Bioethics Advisory Commission (NBAC)—has been working feverishly to put its wisdom on paper, and at a meeting on 17 May, members agreed on a near-final draft of their recommendations.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 该组织——国家生物伦理咨询委员会 (NBAC)——一直在积极努力将其智慧写在纸上，在 5 月 17 日的会议上，成员们就其建议的近乎最终草案达成了一致。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S4.text: NBAC will ask that Clinton's 90-day ban on federal funds for human cloning be extended indefinitely, and possibly that it be made law.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P1-S4.translation: NBAC 将要求无限期延长克林顿禁止联邦资金用于人类克隆的 90 天禁令，并可能将其立法。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S1.text: But NBAC members are planning to word the recommendation narrowly to avoid new restrictions on research that involves the cloning of human DNA or cells—routine in molecular biology.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 但 NBAC 成员计划对建议的措辞进行狭义化，以避免对涉及人类 DNA 或细胞克隆（分子生物学中的常规）的研究施加新的限制。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S2.text: The panel has not yet reached agreement on a crucial question, however, whether to recommend legislation that would make it a crime for private funding to be used for human cloning.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 然而，该小组尚未就一个关键问题达成一致，即是否建议立法将私人资金用于人类克隆定为犯罪行为。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S3.text: In a draft preface to the recommendations, discussed at the 17 May meeting, Shapiro suggested that the panel had found a broad consensus that it would be "morally unacceptable to attempt to create a human child by adult nuclear cloning." Shapiro explained during the meeting that the moral doubt stems mainly from fears about the risk to the health of the child.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: 在 5 月 17 日会议上讨论的建议序言草案中，夏皮罗表示，该小组已达成广泛共识，即“试图通过成人核克隆创造人类儿童在道德上是不可接受的”。夏皮罗在会议上解释说，道德怀疑主要源于对孩子健康风险的担忧。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S4.text: The panel then informally accepted several general conclusions, although some details have not been settled.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 随后，专家组非正式地接受了几项一般性结论，但一些细节尚未确定。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S1.text: NBAC plans to call for a continued ban on federal government funding for any attempt to clone body cell nuclei to create a child.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: NBAC 计划呼吁继续禁止联邦政府资助任何克隆体细胞核来创造孩子的尝试。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S2.text: Because current federal law already forbids the use of federal funds to create embryos (the earliest stage of human offspring before birth) for research or to knowingly endanger an embryo's life, NBAC will remain silent on embryo research.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 由于现行联邦法律已经禁止使用联邦资金来创造胚胎（人类后代出生前的最早阶段）用于研究或故意危及胚胎的生命，NBAC 将对胚胎研究保持沉默。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S3.text: NBAC members also indicated that they would appeal to privately funded researchers and clinics not to try to clone humans by body cell nuclear transfer.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S3.translation: NBAC成员还表示，他们将呼吁私人资助的研究人员和诊所不要试图通过体细胞核移植来克隆人类。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S4.text: But they were divided on whether to go further by calling for a federal law that would impose a complete ban on human cloning.
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S4.translation: 但他们对于是否进一步呼吁制定联邦法律全面禁止人类克隆存在分歧。

ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S5.text: Shapiro and most members favored an appeal for such legislation, but in a phone interview, he said this issue was still "up in the air".
ky-en1-1999-r-t4#P3-S5.translation: 夏皮罗和大多数成员赞成呼吁此类立法，但他在电话采访中表示，这个问题仍然“悬而未决”。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S1.text: Science, in practice, depends far less on the experiments it prepares than on the preparedness of the minds of the men who watch the experiments.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S1.translation: 在实践中，科学更多地取决于观察实验的人的思想准备，而不是它所准备的实验。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S2.text: Sir Isaac Newton supposedly discovered gravity through the fall of an apple.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S2.translation: 艾萨克·牛顿爵士据说是通过苹果下落发现了万有引力。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S3.text: Apples had been falling in many places for centuries and thousands of people had seen them fall.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S3.translation: 几个世纪以来，许多地方的苹果一直在掉落，成千上万的人亲眼目睹了苹果掉落的过程。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S4.text: But Newton for years had been curious about the cause of the orbital motion of the moon and planets.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S4.translation: 但牛顿多年来一直对月球和行星轨道运动的原因感到好奇。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S5.translation: 是什么让他们保持原状？

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S6.text: Why didn't they fall out of the sky?
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S6.translation: 为什么他们没有从天上掉下来？

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S7.text: The fact that the apple fell down toward the earth and not up into the tree answered the question he had been asking himself about those larger fruits of the heavens, the moon and the planets.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S7.translation: 苹果落向地面而不是落向树的事实回答了他一直在问自己的关于天空、月亮和行星上那些更大的果实的问题。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S8.text: How many men would have considered the possibility of an apple falling up into the tree?
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P1-S8.translation: 有多少人会考虑苹果掉到树上的可能性？

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S1.text: Newton did because he was not trying to predict anything.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S1.translation: 牛顿这样做是因为他并没有试图预测任何事情。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S3.text: His mind was ready for the unpredictable.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S3.translation: 他的头脑已做好应对不可预知的事情的准备。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S4.text: Unpredictability is part of the essential nature of research.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S4.translation: 不可预测性是研究本质的一部分。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S5.text: If you don't have unpredictable things, you don't have research.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S5.translation: 如果没有不可预测的事情，就没有研究。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S6.text: Scientists tend to forget this when writing their cut and dried reports for the technical journals, but history is filled with examples of it.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S6.translation: 科学家们在为技术期刊撰写简洁的报告时往往会忘记这一点，但历史上充满了这样的例子。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S7.text: In talking to some scientists, particularly younger ones, you might gather the impression that they find the "scientific method" a substitute for imaginative thought.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S7.translation: 在与一些科学家，尤其是年轻科学家交谈时，你可能会得到这样的印象：他们发现“科学方法”可以替代想象力。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S8.text: I've attended research conferences where a scientist has been asked what he thinks about the advisability of continuing a certain experiment.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P2-S8.translation: 我参加过一些研究会议，会上一位科学家被问到他对继续进行某项实验的建议有何看法。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S1.text: The scientist has frowned, looked at the graphs, and said, "the data are still inconclusive." "We know that," the men from the budget office have said, "but what do you think?
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S1.translation: 科学家皱起了眉头，看了看图表，说道：“数据还没有结论。” “我们知道这一点，”预算办公室的人说，“但是你觉得怎么样？

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S3.text: What do you think we might expect?" The scientist has been shocked at having even been asked to speculate.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S3.translation: 你认为我们会期待什么？”这位科学家甚至对被要求进行推测感到震惊。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S4.text: What this amounts to, of course, is that the scientist has become the victim of his own writings.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S4.translation: 当然，这意味着科学家已经成为他自己著作的受害者。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S5.text: He has put forward unquestioned claims so consistently that he not only believes them himself, but has convinced industrial and business management that they are true.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S5.translation: 他始终如一地提出毫无疑问的主张，以至于他不仅自己相信这些主张，而且还让工业和企业管理层相信这些主张是正确的。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S6.text: If experiments are planned and carried out according to plan as faithfully as the reports in the science journals indicate, then it is perfectly logical for management to expect research to produce results measurable in dollars and cents.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S6.translation: 如果实验像科学期刊上的报告那样忠实地按照计划进行计划和实施，那么管理层期望研究产生可以用美元和美分衡量的结果是完全合乎逻辑的。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S7.text: It is entirely reasonable for auditors to believe that scientists who know exactly where they are going and how they will get there should not be distracted by the necessity of keeping one eye on the cash register while the other eye is on the microscope.
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S7.translation: 审计人员完全有理由相信，那些确切知道自己要去哪里以及如何到达那里的科学家不应该因为一只眼睛盯着收银机而另一只眼睛盯着显微镜而分心。

ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S8.text: Nor, if regularity and conformity to a standard pattern are as desirable to the scientist as the writing of his papers would appear to reflect, is management to be blamed for discriminating against the "odd balls" among researchers in favor of more conventional thinkers who "work well with the team".
ky-en1-1999-r-t5#P3-S8.translation: 如果规律性和符合标准模式对科学家来说就像他的论文所反映的那样，那么管理层也不能被指责歧视研究人员中的“奇怪的球”，而偏爱“与团队合作良好”的更传统的思想家。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S1.text: A history of long and effortless success can be a dreadful handicap, but, if properly handled, it may become a driving force.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 长期不费吹灰之力取得成功的历史可能是一个可怕的障碍，但如果处理得当，它可能会成为一种推动力。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S2.text: When the United States entered just such a glowing period after the end of the Second World War, it had a market eight times larger than any competitor, giving its industries unparalleled economies of scale.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 当美国在第二次世界大战结束后进入如此辉煌​​的时期时，它的市场规模是任何竞争对手的八倍，使其产业具有无与伦比的规模经济。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S3.text: Its scientists were the world's best; its workers the most skilled.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 它的科学家是世界上最优秀的；它的工人是最熟练的。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S4.text: America and Americans were prosperous beyond the dreams of the Europeans and Asians whose economies the war had destroyed.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 美国和美国人的繁荣超出了欧洲人和亚洲人的梦想，他们的经济被战争摧毁了。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S5.text: It was inevitable that this primacy should have narrowed as other countries grew richer.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 随着其他国家变得更加富裕，这种主导地位不可避免地会缩小。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S6.text: Just as inevitably, the retreat from predominance proved painful.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S6.translation: 同样不可避免的是，从主导地位的退却也被证明是痛苦的。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S7.text: By the mid-1980s Americans had found themselves at a loss over their fading industrial competitiveness.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P1-S7.translation: 到 20 世纪 80 年代中期，美国人发现自己因工业竞争力下降而不知所措。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S1.text: Some huge American industries, such as consumer electronics, had shrunk or vanished in the face of foreign competition.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 美国一些大型产业，例如消费电子产品，在外国竞争面前已经萎缩或消失。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S2.text: By 1987 there was only one American television maker left, Zenith. (Now there is none: Zenith was bought by South Korea's LG Electronics in July.) Foreign-made cars and textiles were sweeping into the domestic market.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 到 1987 年，美国只剩下一家电视制造商：Zenith。 （现在已经没有了：Zenith 于 7 月份被韩国 LG 电子收购。） 外国制造的汽车和纺织品正在席卷国内市场。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S3.text: America's machine-tool industry was on the ropes.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S3.translation: 美国的机床工业陷入困境。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S4.text: For a while it looked as though the making of semiconductors, which America had invented and which sat at the heart of the new computer age, was going to be the next casualty.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S4.translation: 有一段时间，美国发明并处于新计算机时代核心地位的半导体制造似乎将成为下一个受害者。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S5.text: All of this caused a crisis of confidence.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: 所有这些都引发了信任危机。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S6.text: Americans stopped taking prosperity for granted.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S6.translation: 美国人不再认为繁荣是理所当然的。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S7.text: They began to believe that their way of doing business was failing, and that their incomes would therefore shortly begin to fall as well.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P2-S7.translation: 他们开始相信他们的经营方式正在失败，因此他们的收入很快也会开始下降。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S1.text: The mid-1980s brought one inquiry after another into the causes of America's industrial decline.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 20 世纪 80 年代中期，人们对美国工业衰退的原因进行了一次又一次的调查。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S2.text: Their sometimes sensational findings were filled with warnings about the growing competition from overseas.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 他们有时令人震惊的发现充满了对来自海外日益激烈的竞争的警告。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 事情发生了多么大的变化啊！

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S4.text: In 1995 the United States can look back on five years of solid growth while Japan has been struggling.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: 1995年，美国可以实现五年的稳健增长，而日本却一直在苦苦挣扎。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S5.text: Few Americans attribute this solely to such obvious causes as a devalued dollar or the turning of the business cycle.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: 很少有美国人将这仅仅归因于美元贬值或商业周期转变等明显原因。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S6.text: Self-doubt has yielded to blind pride.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 自我怀疑已经屈服于盲目的骄傲。

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S7.text: "American industry has changed its structure, has gone on a diet, and has learnt to be more quick-witted," according to Richard Cavanaugh, executive dean of Harvard's Kennedy School of Government.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S7.translation: 哈佛大学肯尼迪政府学院执行院长理查德·卡瓦诺表示：“美国工业已经改变了结构，开始节食，并学会了变得更加机智。”

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S8.text: "It makes me proud to be an American just to see how our businesses are improving their productivity," says Stephen Moore of the Cato Institute, a think-tank in Washington, DC.
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S8.translation: 华盛顿特区智库卡托研究所的史蒂芬·摩尔表示：“作为一名美国人，看到我们的企业如何提高生产力，我就感到很自豪。”

ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S9.text: And William Sahlman of the Harvard Business School believes that people will look back on this period as "a golden age of business management in the United States."
ky-en1-2000-r-t1#P3-S9.translation: 而哈佛商学院的威廉·萨尔曼则认为，人们回顾这一时期将是“美国企业管理的黄金时代”。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S1.text: Being a man has always been dangerous.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 作为一个男人一直都是危险的。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S2.text: There are about 105 males born for every 100 females, but this ratio drops to near balance at the age of maturity, and among 70-year-olds there are twice as many women as men.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 大约每 100 名女性出生就有 105 名男性，但这一比例在成熟时下降到接近平衡，并且在 70 岁的老年人中，女性数量是男性的两倍。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S3.text: But the great universal of male mortality is being changed.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 但男性死亡率的普遍现象正在发生改变。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S4.text: Now, boy babies survive almost as well as girls do.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 现在，男婴的生存率几乎和女婴一样好。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S5.text: This means that, for the first time, there will be an excess of boys in those crucial years when they are searching for a mate.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S5.translation: 这意味着，在寻找伴侣的关键年份，男孩数量将首次出现过剩。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S6.text: More importantly, another chance for natural selection has been removed.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S6.translation: 更重要的是，自然选择的另一个机会被消除了。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S7.text: Fifty years ago, the chance of a baby (particularly a boy baby) surviving depended on its weight.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S7.translation: 五十年前，婴儿（尤其是男婴）的生存机会取决于其体重。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S8.text: A kilogram too light or too heavy meant almost certain death.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P1-S8.translation: 太轻或太重一公斤几乎都意味着死亡。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S1.text: Today it makes almost no difference.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 今天，这几乎没有什么区别。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Since much of the variation is due to genes, one more agent of evolution has gone.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 由于大部分变异是由基因造成的，因此又一个进化的推动者消失了。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S3.text: There is another way to commit evolutionary suicide: stay alive, but have fewer children.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S3.translation: 进化自杀还有另一种方式：保持活力，但少生孩子。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S4.text: Few people are as fertile as in the past.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 很少有人像过去一样生育能力强。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S5.text: Except in some religious communities, very few women have 15 children.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S5.translation: 除了一些宗教团体外，很少有女性拥有 15 个孩子。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S6.text: Nowadays the number of births, like the age of death, has become average.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S6.translation: 如今，出生人数和死亡年龄一样，已趋于平均。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S7.text: Most of us have roughly the same number of offspring.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S7.translation: 我们大多数人的后代数量大致相同。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S8.text: Again, differences between people and the opportunity for natural selection to take advantage of it have diminished.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P2-S8.translation: 人与人之间的差异以及自然选择利用这种差异的机会再次减少。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 印度展示了正在发生的事情。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S2.text: The country offers wealth for a few in the great cities and poverty for the remaining tribal peoples.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 这个国家为大城市中的少数人提供了财富，却为剩下的部落人民提供了贫困。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S3.text: The grand mediocrity of today—everyone being the same in survival and number of offspring—means that natural selection has lost 80% of its power in upper-middle-class India compared to the tribes.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S3.translation: 今天的巨大平庸——每个人的生存和后代数量都一样——意味着与部落相比，自然选择在印度中上层阶级中失去了 80% 的力量。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S4.text: For us, this means that evolution is over; the biological Utopia has arrived.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S4.translation: 对我们来说，这意味着进化已经结束；生物乌托邦已经到来。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S5.text: Strangely, it has involved little physical change.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S5.translation: 奇怪的是，它几乎没有带来任何物理变化。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S6.text: No other species fills so many places in nature.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S6.translation: 没有其他物种占据了自然界如此多的地方。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S7.text: But in the past 100,000 years—even the past 100 years—our lives have been transformed but our bodies have not.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S7.translation: 但在过去的十万年里，甚至在过去的一百年里，我们的生活已经发生了改变，但我们的身体却没有。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S8.text: We did not evolve, because machines and society did it for us.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S8.translation: 我们没有进化，因为机器和社会为我们进化了。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S9.text: Darwin had a phrase to describe those ignorant of evolution: they "look at an organic being as a savage looks at a ship, as at something wholly beyond his comprehension." No doubt we will remember a 20th century way of life beyond comprehension for its ugliness.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S9.translation: 达尔文曾用一句话来描述那些对进化论一无所知的人：他们“看待有机生物就像野蛮人看待一艘船，就像看待完全超出他理解范围的事物”。毫无疑问，我们会记住20世纪的生活方式，因为它的丑陋是无法理解的。

ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S10.text: But however amazed our descendants may be at how far from Utopia we were, they will look just like us.
ky-en1-2000-r-t2#P3-S10.translation: 但是，无论我们的后代对我们离乌托邦有多远感到惊讶，他们看起来都会像我们一样。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S1.text: When a new movement in art attains a certain fashion, it is advisable to find out what its advocates are aiming at, for, however farfetched and unreasonable their principles may seem today, it is possible that in years to come they may be regarded as normal. With regard to Futurist poetry, however, the case is rather difficult, for whatever Futurist poetry may be—even admitting that the theory on which it is based may be right—it can hardly be classed as Literature.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 当一场新的艺术运动达到某种时尚时，最好找出它的倡导者的目标是什么，因为无论他们的原则在今天看起来多么牵强和不合理，在未来的岁月里它们可能会被认为是正常的。然而，就未来主义诗歌而言，情况就相当困难了，因为无论未来主义诗歌是什么——即使承认它所依据的理论可能是正确的——它也很难被归类为文学。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S2.text: This, in brief, is what the Futurist says: for a century, past conditions of life have been conditionally speeding up, till now we live in a world of noise and violence and speed.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 简而言之，这就是未来主义者所说的：一个世纪以来，过去的生活条件一直在有条件地加速，直到现在我们生活在一个充满噪音、暴力和速度的世界中。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S3.text: Consequently, our feelings, thoughts and emotions have undergone a corresponding change.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 因此，我们的感觉、思想和情绪也发生了相应的变化。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S4.text: This speeding up of life, says the Futurist, requires a new form of expression.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 未来主义者说，生活的加速需要一种新的表达形式。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S1.text: We must speed up our literature too, if we want to interpret modern stress.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 如果我们想解释现代压力，我们也必须加快我们的文学步伐。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S2.text: We must pour out a large stream of essential words, unhampered by stops, or qualifying adjectives, or finite verbs.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 我们必须倾注大量基本词汇，不受停顿、限定形容词或限定动词的阻碍。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S3.text: Instead of describing sounds we must make up words that imitate them; we must use many sizes of type and different colored inks on the same page, and shorten or lengthen words at will.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 我们必须创造模仿声音的词语，而不是描述声音。我们必须在同一页上使用多种尺寸的字体和不同颜色的墨水，并随意缩短或加长单词。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S4.text: Certainly their descriptions of battles are confusing.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 当然，他们对战斗的描述令人困惑。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S1.text: But it is a little upsetting to read in the explanatory notes that a certain line describes a fight between a Turkish and a Bulgarian officer on a bridge off which they both fall into the river—and then to find that the line consists of the noise of their falling and the weights of the officers: "Pluff!
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 但读到注释中的某句台词，描述了一名土耳其军官和一名保加利亚军官在一座桥上打斗，两人双双坠入河中，然后发现这句台词由他们坠落的噪音和军官的重量组成，这有点令人不安：“噗！

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S3.text: A hundred and eighty-five kilograms." This, though it fulfills the laws and requirements of Futurist poetry, can hardly be classed as Literature.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 一百八十五公斤。”这虽然符合未来主义诗歌的规律和要求，但很难被归类为文学。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S4.text: All the same, no thinking man can refuse to accept their first proposition: that a great change in our emotional life calls for a change of expression.
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 尽管如此，没有一个有思想的人不能拒绝接受他们的第一个命题：我们情感生活的巨大变化需要改变表达方式。

ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S5.text: The whole question is really this: have we essentially changed?
ky-en1-2000-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 整个问题实际上是这样的：我们本质上改变了吗？

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S1.text: Aimlessness has hardly been typical of postwar Japan whose productivity and social harmony are the envy of the United States and Europe.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 漫无目的并不是战后日本的典型特征，日本的生产力和社会和谐令美国和欧洲羡慕不已。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S2.text: But increasingly the Japanese are seeing a decline of the traditional work-moral values.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 但日本人越来越看到传统工作道德价值观的衰落。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S3.text: Ten years ago young people were hardworking and saw their jobs as their primary reason for being, but now Japan has largely fulfilled its economic needs, and young people don't know where they should go next.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 十年前，年轻人努力工作，把工作视为生存的首要原因，但现在日本已经基本满足了经济需求，年轻人不知道下一步该去哪里。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S4.text: The coming of age of the postwar baby boom and an entry of women into the male-dominated job market have limited the opportunities of teenagers who are already questioning the heavy personal sacrifices involved in climbing Japan's rigid social ladder to good schools and jobs.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P1-S4.translation: 战后婴儿潮的到来以及女性进入男性主导的就业市场限制了青少年的机会，他们已经开始质疑攀登日本严格的社会阶梯以获得好学校和工作所需的巨大个人牺牲。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S1.text: In a recent survey, it was found that only 24.5 percent of Japanese students were fully satisfied with school life, compared with 67.2 percent of students in the United States.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 最近的一项调查发现，只有 24.5% 的日本学生对学校生活完全满意，而美国学生的这一比例为 67.2%。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S2.text: In addition, far more Japanese workers expressed dissatisfaction with their jobs than did their counterparts in the 10 other countries surveyed.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 此外，对工作表示不满的日本工人比其他 10 个接受调查的国家的工人要多得多。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S3.text: While often praised by foreigners for its emphasis on the basics, Japanese education tends to stress test taking and mechanical learning over creativity and self-expression.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: 虽然日本教育因其对基础知识的重视而经常受到外国人的称赞，但日本教育往往强调应试和机械学习，而不是创造力和自我表达。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S4.text: "Those things that do not show up in the test scores—personality, ability, courage or humanity—are completely ignored," says Toshiki Kaifu, chairman of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's education committee.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 执政的自民党教育委员会主席海部俊树表示，“那些没有在考试成绩中体现出来的东西——个性、能力、勇气或人性——都被完全忽视了。”

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S1.text: "Frustration against this kind of thing leads kids to drop out and run wild." Last year Japan experienced 2,125 incidents of school violence, including 929 assaults on teachers.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: “对这种事情的沮丧会导致孩子们辍学并疯狂。”去年日本发生了2125起校园暴力事件，其中袭击教师事件929起。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S2.text: Amid the outcry, many conservative leaders are seeking a return to the pre-war emphasis on moral education.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 在强烈抗议中，许多保守派领导人正在寻求回归战前对道德教育的重视。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S3.text: Last year Mitsuo Setoyama, who was then education minister, raised eyebrows when he argued that liberal reforms introduced by the American occupation authorities after World War II had weakened the "Japanese morality of respect for parents." But that may have more to do with Japanese life-styles.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S3.translation: 去年，时任文部科学省大臣的濑户山光雄辩称，二战后美国占领当局推行的自由主义改革削弱了“日本尊重父母的道德”，这引起了人们的关注。但这可能与日本的生活方式有更多关系。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S4.text: "In Japan," says educator Yoko Muro, "it's never a question of whether you enjoy your job and your life, but only how much you can endure." With economic growth has come centralization; fully 76 percent of Japan's 119 million citizens live in cities where community and the extended family have been abandoned in favor of isolated, two-generation households.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S4.translation: “在日本，”教育家室罗洋子说，“问题从来不在于你是否喜欢你的工作和生活，而在于你能忍受多少。”随着经济的增长，集中化也随之而来。日本 1.19 亿公民中有 76% 生活在城市，社区和大家庭被抛弃，取而代之的是孤立的两代家庭。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S5.text: Urban Japanese have long endured lengthy commutes (travels to and from work) and crowded living conditions, but as the old group and family values weaken, the discomfort is beginning to tell.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S5.translation: 日本城市居民长期以来一直忍受着漫长的通勤（上下班）和拥挤的生活条件，但随着旧群体和家庭价值观的削弱，这种不适开始显现。

ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S6.text: In the past decade, the Japanese divorce rate, while still well below that of the United States, has increased by more than 50 percent, and suicides have increased by nearly one-quarter.
ky-en1-2000-r-t4#P3-S6.translation: 过去十年，日本离婚率虽然仍远低于美国，但已增加了 50% 以上，自杀率增加了近四分之一。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S1.text: If ambition is to be well regarded, the rewards of ambition—wealth, distinction, control over one's destiny—must be deemed worthy of the sacrifices made on ambition's behalf.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S1.translation: 如果要充分尊重野心，那么野心的回报——财富、声望、对自己命运的控制——就必须被认为值得为野心而做出的牺牲。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S2.text: If the tradition of ambition is to have vitality, it must be widely shared; and it especially must be highly regarded by people who are themselves admired, the educated not least among them.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S2.translation: 志向传统要具有生命力，就必须广泛传播；尤其是那些本身就受到钦佩的人，尤其是受过教育的人，必须高度重视它。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S3.text: In an odd way, however, it is the educated who have claimed to have given up on ambition as an ideal. What is odd is that they have perhaps most benefited from ambition—if not always their own then that of their parents and grandparents.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S3.translation: 然而，奇怪的是，正是那些受过教育的人声称已经放弃了将野心作为理想的目标。奇怪的是，他们或许从野心中获益最多——如果不是他们自己的野心，那么也是他们父母和祖父母的野心。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S4.text: There is a heavy note of hypocrisy in this, a case of closing the barn door after the horses have escaped—with the educated themselves riding on them.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P1-S4.translation: 这其中有浓浓的虚伪色彩，就像是在马匹逃走后关上谷仓门——受过教育的人自己骑在马匹上。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S1.text: Certainly people do not seem less interested in success and its signs now than formerly.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S1.translation: 当然，现在人们对成功及其标志的兴趣似乎并不比以前减弱。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S2.text: Summer homes, European travel, BMWs—the locations, place names and name brands may change, but such items do not seem less in demand today than a decade or two years ago.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S2.translation: 避暑别墅、欧洲旅行、宝马——地点、地名和品牌可能会改变，但今天对这些物品的需求似乎并不比十年前或两年前少。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S3.text: What has happened is that people cannot confess fully to their dreams, as easily and openly as once they could, lest they be thought pushing, acquisitive and vulgar.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S3.translation: 所发生的情况是，人们无法像以前那样轻松、公开地完全承认自己的梦想，以免被认为是咄咄逼人、贪婪且粗俗。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S4.text: Instead, we are treated to fine hypocritical spectacles, which now more than ever seem in ample supply: the critic of American materialism with a Southampton summer home; the publisher of radical books who takes his meals in three-star restaurants; the journalist advocating participatory democracy in all phases of life, whose own children are enrolled in private schools.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P2-S4.translation: 相反，我们看到的是精美的虚伪奇观，这些奇观现在似乎比以往任何时候都更加充足：对美国唯物主义的批评者拥有南安普敦的避暑别墅；在三星级餐厅用餐的激进书籍出版商；这位记者提倡人生各个阶段的参与式民主，他自己的孩子就读于私立学校。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S1.text: For such people and many more perhaps not so exceptional, the proper formulation is, "Succeed at all costs but avoid appearing ambitious." The attacks on ambition are many and come from various angles; its public defenders are few and unimpressive, where they are not extremely unattractive.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S1.translation: 对于这样的人以及更多可能不那么特殊的人来说，正确的表述是“不惜一切代价取得成功，但避免显得雄心勃勃”。对野心的攻击是多方面的，而且来自不同的角度。其公设辩护人数量很少且不起眼，但他们也并非毫无吸引力。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S2.text: As a result, the support for ambition as a healthy impulse, a quality to be admired and fixed in the mind of the young, is probably lower than it has ever been in the United States.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S2.translation: 因此，在年轻人心目中，对雄心作为一种健康的冲动、一种值得钦佩和固定的品质的支持可能比以往任何时候都低。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S3.text: This does not mean that ambition is at an end, that people no longer feel its stirrings and promptings, but only that, no longer openly honored, it is less openly professed.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S3.translation: 这并不意味着野心已经结束，人们不再感受到它的激动和推动，而只是意味着它不再被公开尊重，也不再那么公开宣称。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S4.text: Consequences follow from this, of course, some of which are that ambition is driven underground, or made sly.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S4.translation: 当然，随之而来的后果是，野心被驱入地下，或者变得狡猾。

ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S5.text: Such, then, is the way things stand: on the left angry critics, on the right stupid supporters, and in the middle, as usual, the majority of earnest people trying to get on in life.
ky-en1-2000-r-t5#P3-S5.translation: 那么，事情的现状就是这样：左边是愤怒的批评者，右边是愚蠢的支持者，而中间的是，像往常一样，大多数认真的人试图在生活中继续前进。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S1.text: Specialisation can be seen as a response to the problem of an increasing accumulation of scientific knowledge.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 专业化可以被视为对科学知识不断积累问题的回应。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S2.text: By splitting up the subject matter into smaller units, one man could continue to handle the information and use it as the basis for further research.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 通过将主题分解为更小的单元，一个人可以继续处理信息并将其用作进一步研究的基础。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S3.text: But specialisation was only one of a series of related developments in science affecting the process of communication.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 但专业化只是影响传播过程的一系列科学相关发展之一。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S4.text: Another was the growing professionalisation of scientific activity.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 另一个是科学活动日益专业化。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S5.text: No clear-cut distinction can be drawn between professionals and amateurs in science: exceptions can be found to any rule.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 科学领域的专业人士和业余爱好者之间没有明确的区别：任何规则都可以找到例外。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S1.text: Nevertheless, the word "amateur" does carry a connotation that the person concerned is not fully integrated into the scientific community and, in particular, may not fully share its values.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 然而，“业余爱好者”一词确实含有这样的含义：有关人员没有完全融入科学界，特别是可能不完全认同科学界的价值观。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S2.text: The growth of specialisation in the nineteenth century, with its consequent requirement of a longer, more complex training, implied greater problems for amateur participation in science.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 十九世纪专业化的发展，随之而来的是对更长、更复杂的训练的要求，这给业余参与科学带来了更大的问题。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S3.text: The trend was naturally most obvious in those areas of science based especially on mathematical or laboratory training, and can be illustrated in terms of the development of geology in the United Kingdom.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S3.translation: 这种趋势自然在那些基于数学或实验室培训的科学领域最为明显，并且可以用英国地质学的发展来说明。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S4.text: A comparison of British geological publications over the last century and a half reveals not simply an increasing emphasis on the primacy of research, but also a changing definition of what constitutes an acceptable research paper.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S4.translation: 对过去一个半世纪英国地质出版物的比较表明，不仅越来越强调研究的首要地位，而且对可接受的研究论文的定义也发生了变化。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S5.text: Thus, in the nineteenth century, local geological studies represented worthwhile research in their own right, but, in the twentieth century, local studies have increasingly become acceptable to professionals only if they incorporate, and reflect on, the wider geological picture.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: 因此，在十九世纪，地方地质研究本身就代表了有价值的研究，但在二十世纪，只有当地方研究纳入并反映更广泛的地质图景时，地方研究才越来越被专业人士所接受。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S1.text: Amateurs, on the other hand, have continued to pursue local studies in the old way.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 而业余爱好者则继续以旧方式进行地方研究。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S2.text: The overall result has been to make entrance to professional geological journals harder for amateurs, a result that has been reinforced by the widespread introduction of refereeing, first by national journals in the nineteenth century and then by several local geological journals in the twentieth century.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 总体结果是，业余爱好者进入专业地质期刊变得更加困难，这一结果由于审稿制度的广泛引入而得到加强，首先是十九世纪的国家期刊，然后是二十世纪的一些地方地质期刊。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S3.text: As a logical consequence of this development, separate journals have now appeared aimed mainly towards either professional or amateur readership.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 作为这种发展的必然结果，现在出现了主要针对专业或业余读者的独立期刊。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S4.text: A rather similar process of differentiation has led to professional geologists coming together nationally within one or two specific societies, whereas the amateurs have tended either to remain in local societies or to come together nationally in a different way.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: 一个相当相似的分化过程导致专业地质学家在全国范围内聚集在一两个特定的社团中，而业余爱好者则倾向于留在当地社团或以不同的方式在全国范围内聚集在一起。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S5.text: Although the process of professionalisation and specialisation was already well under way in British geology during the nineteenth century, its full consequences were thus delayed until the twentieth century.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: 尽管十九世纪英国地质学的专业化和专业化进程已经顺利进行，但其全面后果却被推迟到了二十世纪。

ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S6.text: In science generally, however, the nineteenth century must be reckoned as the crucial period for this change in the structure of science.
ky-en1-2001-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 然而，从一般科学的角度来看，十九世纪必须被视为科学结构发生这种变化的关键时期。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S1.text: A great deal of attention is being paid today to the so-called digital divide—the division of the world into the info (information) rich and the info poor.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 如今，人们对所谓的数字鸿沟给予了极大的关注——将世界划分为信息富国和信息贫国。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S2.text: And that divide does exist today.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 这种鸿沟今天确实存在。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S3.text: My wife and I lectured about this looming danger twenty years ago.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 二十年前，我和妻子就曾就这种迫在眉睫的危险进行过演讲。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S4.text: What was less visible then, however, were the new, positive forces that work against the digital divide.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 然而，当时不太明显的是消除数字鸿沟的新的积极力量。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S5.text: There are reasons to be optimistic.

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S6.text: There are technological reasons to hope the digital divide will narrow.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S6.translation: 有技术原因希望数字鸿沟能够缩小。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S7.text: As the Internet becomes more and more commercialized, it is in the interest of business to universalize access—after all, the more people online, the more potential customers there are.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S7.translation: 随着互联网变得越来越商业化，普及接入符合企业的利益——毕竟，上网的人越多，潜在客户就越多。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S8.text: More and more governments, afraid their countries will be left behind, want to spread Internet access.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P1-S8.translation: 越来越多的政府担心自己的国家会落后，希望普及互联网接入。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S1.text: Within the next decade or two, one to two billion people on the planet will be netted together.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 在未来的一两年内，地球上的一到二十亿人将被聚集在一起。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S2.text: As a result, I now believe the digital divide will narrow rather than widen in the years ahead.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 因此，我现在相信数字鸿沟在未来几年将会缩小而不是扩大。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S3.text: And that is very good news because the Internet may well be the most powerful tool for combating world poverty that we've ever had.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S3.translation: 这是一个非常好的消息，因为互联网很可能是我们有史以来消除世界贫困的最有力工具。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S4.text: Of course, the use of the Internet isn't the only way to defeat poverty.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 当然，使用互联网并不是消除贫困的唯一方法。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S5.text: And the Internet is not the only tool we have.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S5.translation: 互联网并不是我们拥有的唯一工具。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S6.text: But it has enormous potential. To take advantage of this tool, some impoverished countries will have to get over their outdated anti-colonial prejudices with respect to foreign investment.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S6.translation: 但它具有巨大的潜力。为了利用这一工具，一些贫困国家必须克服对外国投资过时的反殖民偏见。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S7.text: Countries that still think foreign investment is an invasion of their sovereignty might well study the history of infrastructure (the basic structural foundations of a society) in the United States.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S7.translation: 仍然认为外国投资是对其主权的侵犯的国家不妨研究一下美国基础设施（社会的基本结构基础）的历史。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S8.text: When the United States built its industrial infrastructure, it didn't have the capital to do so.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P2-S8.translation: 当美国建设工业基础设施时，它没有资金这样做。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S1.text: And that is why America's Second Wave infrastructure—including roads, harbors, highways, ports and so on—were built with foreign investment.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 这就是为什么美国的第二波基础设施——包括道路、港口、高速公路、港口等——都是由外国投资建造的。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S2.text: The English, the Germans, the Dutch and the French were investing in Britain's former colony.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 英国人、德国人、荷兰人和法国人都在英国的前殖民地投资。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S7.text: I believe the same thing would be true in places like Brazil or anywhere else for that matter.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S7.translation: 我相信在巴西或其他任何地方也会发生同样的情况。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S8.text: The more foreign capital you have helping you build your Third Wave infrastructure, which today is an electronic infrastructure, the better off you're going to be.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S8.translation: 你拥有越多的外国资本来帮助你建设你的第三次浪潮基础设施（今天是电子基础设施），你的生活就会越好。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S9.text: That doesn't mean lying down and becoming fooled, or letting foreign corporations run uncontrolled.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S9.translation: 这并不意味着袖手旁观、被愚弄，或者让外国公司不受控制地运营。

ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S10.text: But it does mean recognizing how important they can be in building the energy and telecom infrastructures needed to take full advantage of the Internet.
ky-en1-2001-r-t2#P3-S10.translation: 但这确实意味着认识到它们在建设充分利用互联网所需的能源和电信基础设施方面的重要性。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S1.text: Why do so many Americans distrust what they read in their newspapers?
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 为什么这么多美国人不相信他们在报纸上读到的内容？

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S2.text: The American Society of Newspaper Editors is trying to answer this painful question.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 美国报纸编辑协会正在试图回答这个令人痛苦的问题。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S3.text: The organization is deep into a long self-analysis known as the journalism credibility project.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 该组织正在进行一项名为“新闻可信度项目”的长期自我分析。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S4.text: Sad to say, this project has turned out to be mostly low-level findings about factual errors and spelling and grammar mistakes, combined with lots of headscratching puzzlement about what in the world those readers really want.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 遗憾的是，这个项目主要是关于事实错误、拼写和语法错误的低级发现，再加上对读者真正想要的东西的许多令人头疼的困惑。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S5.text: But the sources of distrust go way deeper.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S5.translation: 但不信任的根源更为深刻。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S6.text: Most journalists learn to see the world through a set of standard templates (patterns) into which they plug each day's events.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P1-S6.translation: 大多数记者学习通过一组标准模板（模式）来观察世界，并将每天发生的事件插入其中。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S1.text: In other words, there is a conventional story line in the newsroom culture that provides a backbone and a ready-made narrative structure for otherwise confusing news.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 换句话说，新闻编辑室文化中有一个传统的故事情节，为原本令人困惑的新闻提供了支柱和现成的叙事结构。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S2.text: There exists a social and cultural disconnect between journalists and their readers which helps explain why the "standard templates"of the newsroom seem alien to many readers.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 记者和读者之间存在社会和文化脱节，这有助于解释为什么新闻编辑室的“标准模板”对许多读者来说似乎很陌生。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S3.text: In a recent survey, questionnaires were sent to reporters in five middle size cities around the country, plus one large metropolitan area.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 在最近的一项调查中，向全国五个中等城市以及一个大城市地区的记者发送了调查问卷。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S4.text: Then residents in these communities were phoned at random and asked the same questions.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 然后随机给这些社区的居民打电话，问了同样的问题。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S5.text: Replies show that compared with other Americans, journalists are more likely to live in upscale neighborhoods, have maids, own Mercedeses, and trade stocks, and they're less likely to go to church, do volunteer work, or put down roots in community.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S5.translation: 答复显示，与其他美国人相比，记者更有可能住在高档社区、有女佣、拥有奔驰、交易股票，而且他们不太可能去教堂、做志愿者工作或扎根社区。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S6.text: Reporters tend to be part of a broadly defined social and cultural elite, so their work tends to reflect the conventional values of this elite.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P2-S6.translation: 记者往往是广泛定义的社会和文化精英的一部分，因此他们的工作往往反映该精英的传统价值观。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S1.text: The astonishing distrust of the news media isn't rooted in inaccuracy or poor reportorial skills but in the daily clash of world views between reporters and their readers.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 对新闻媒体的惊人不信任并非源于不准确或报道技巧不佳，而是源于记者与读者之间每天的世界观冲突。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S2.text: This is an explosive situation for any industry, particularly a declining one.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 对于任何行业，尤其​​是正在衰退的行业来说，这都是一种爆炸​​性的局面。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S3.text: Here is a troubled business that keeps hiring employees whose attitudes vastly annoy the customers.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 这是一家陷入困境的企业，不断雇用态度极大地惹恼顾客的员工。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S4.text: Then it sponsors lots of symposiums and a credibility project dedicated to wondering why customers are annoyed and fleeing in large numbers.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 然后，它赞助了许多研讨会和一个可信度项目，致力于了解为什么顾客会感到恼火并大量逃离。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S5.text: But it never seems to get around to noticing the cultural and class biases that so many former buyers are complaining about.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 但它似乎从来没有注意到许多前买家所抱怨的文化和阶级偏见。

ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S6.text: If it did, it would open up its diversity program, now focused narrowly on race and gender, and look for reporters who differ broadly by outlook, values, education, and class.
ky-en1-2001-r-t3#P3-S6.translation: 如果确实如此，它将开放其多元化计划，目前主要关注种族和性别，并寻找在观点、价值观、教育和阶级方面存在广泛差异的记者。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S1.text: The world is going through the biggest wave of mergers and acquisitions ever witnessed.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 世界正在经历有史以来最大规模的并购浪潮。
