ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S2.text: The process sweeps from hyperactive America to Europe and reaches the emerging countries with unsurpassed might.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 这一进程从极度活跃的美国席卷到欧洲，并以无与伦比的力量影响到新兴国家。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S3.text: Many in these countries are looking at this process and worrying: "Won't the wave of business concentration turn into an uncontrollable anti-competitive force?" There's no question that the big are getting bigger and more powerful.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 这些国家的许多人都在关注这一过程并担心：“企业集中化浪潮会不会变成一股无法控制的反竞争力量？”毫无疑问，大公司正在变得越来越大、越来越强大。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S4.text: Multinational corporations accounted for less than 20% of international trade in 1982.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S4.translation: 1982年，跨国公司占国际贸易的比例还不到20%。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S5.text: Today the figure is more than 25% and growing rapidly.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S5.translation: 如今，这一数字已超过 25%，并且还在快速增长。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S6.text: International affiliates account for a fast-growing segment of production in economies that open up and welcome foreign investment.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S6.translation: 在开放和欢迎外国投资的经济体中，国际子公司在生产中占据快速增长的部分。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S7.text: In Argentina, for instance, after the reforms of the early 1990s, multinationals went from 43% to almost 70% of the industrial production of the 200 largest firms.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P1-S7.translation: 例如，在阿根廷，经过 20 世纪 90 年代初的改革，跨国公司占 200 家最大企业工业生产的比例从 43% 增加到近 70%。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S1.text: This phenomenon has created serious concerns over the role of smaller economic firms, of national businessmen and over the ultimate stability of the world economy.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 这种现象引起了人们对小型经济公司、民族商人的作用以及世界经济最终稳定的严重担忧。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S2.text: I believe that the most important forces behind the massive M&A wave are the same that underlie the globalization process: falling transportation and communication costs, lower trade and investment barriers and enlarged markets that require enlarged operations capable of meeting customers' demands.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 我相信，大规模并购浪潮背后最重要的推动力与全球化进程的推动力是一样的：运输和通讯成本的下降、贸易和投资壁垒的降低以及市场的扩大，需要扩大经营规模来满足客户的需求。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S3.text: All these are beneficial, not detrimental, to consumers.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: 所有这些对于消费者来说都是有益的，而不是有害的。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S4.text: As productivity grows, the world's wealth increases.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 随着生产力的提高，世界财富也随之增加。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S5.text: Examples of benefits or costs of the current concentration wave are scanty.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S5.translation: 当前集中浪潮的好处或成本的例子很少。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S6.text: Yet it is hard to imagine that the merger of a few oil firms today could re-create the same threats to competition that were feared nearly a century ago in the U.S., when the Standard Oil trust was broken up.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S6.translation: 然而，很难想象今天几家石油公司的合并可能会重新造成近一个世纪前美国标准石油托拉斯解散时所担心的同样的竞争威胁。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S7.text: The mergers of telecom companies, such as WorldCom, hardly seem to bring higher prices for consumers or a reduction in the pace of technical progress.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P2-S7.translation: 世通等电信公司的合并似乎几乎没有给消费者带来更高的价格或减缓技术进步的步伐。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S1.text: On the contrary, the price of communications is coming down fast.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 相反，通信价格正在快速下降。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S2.text: In cars, too, concentration is increasing-witness Daimler and Chrysler, Renault and Nissan—but it does not appear that consumers are being hurt.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 在汽车领域，集中度也在不断提高——戴姆勒和克莱斯勒、雷诺和日产就是例证——但消费者似乎并未受到伤害。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S3.text: Yet the fact remains that the merger movement must be watched.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S3.translation: 但事实仍然是，合并动向必须受到关注。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S4.text: A few weeks ago, Alan Greenspan warned against the megamergers in the banking industry.
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S4.translation: 几周前，艾伦·格林斯潘对银行业的大型合并发出警告。

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S5.text: Who is going to supervise, regulate and operate as a lender of last resort with the gigantic banks that are being created?
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S5.translation: 谁将作为最后贷款人对正在创建的大型银行进行监督、监管和运营？

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S6.text: Won't multinationals shift production from one place to another when a nation gets too strict about infringements to fair competition?
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S6.translation: 当一个国家对公平竞争的侵权行为过于严格时，跨国公司是否会将生产从一个地方转移到另一个地方？

ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S7.text: And should one country take upon itself the role of "defending competition" on issues that affect many other nations, as in the U.S. vs. Microsoft case ?
ky-en1-2001-r-t4#P3-S7.translation: 一个国家是否应该在影响许多其他国家的问题上承担起“捍卫竞争”的角色，就像美国诉微软案一样？

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P1-S1.text: When I decided to quit my full time employment it never occurred to me that I might become a part of a new international trend.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P1-S1.translation: 当我决定辞去全职工作时，我从未想到我可能会成为新国际趋势的一部分。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P1-S2.text: A lateral move that hurt my pride and blocked my professional progress prompted me to abandon my relatively high profile career although, in the manner of a disgraced government minister, I covered my exit by claiming, "I wanted to spend more time with my family".
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P1-S2.translation: 一次横向调动伤害了我的自尊心并阻碍了我的职业进步，促使我放弃了我相对较高调的职业生涯，尽管我以一个丢脸的政府部长的方式掩盖了我的退出，声称“我想花更多的时间和我的家人在一起”。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P1-S3.text: Curiously, some two-and-a-half years and two novels later, my experiment in what the Americans term "downshifting" has turned my tired excuse into an absolute reality.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P1-S3.translation: 奇怪的是，大约两年半和两本小说之后，我对美国人所说的“降档”的实验将我疲惫的借口变成了绝对的现实。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P2-S1.text: I have been transformed from a passionate advocate of the philosophy of "having it all", preached by Linda Kelsey for the past seven years in the pages of She magazine, into a woman who is happy to settle for a bit of everything.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P2-S1.translation: 我已经从琳达·凯尔西过去七年在《She》杂志上宣扬的“拥有一切”哲学的热情倡导者，变成了一个乐于满足于一切的女人。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P2-S2.text: I have discovered, as perhaps Kelsey will after her much-publicized resignation from the editorship of She after a build-up of stress, that abandoning the doctrine of "juggling your life", and making the alternative move into "downshifting" brings with it far greater rewards than financial success and social status.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P2-S2.translation: 我发现，正如凯尔西因压力增大而广为人知地辞去《她》编辑一职后所发现的那样，放弃“兼顾生活”的信条，转而“放慢节奏”，会带来比经济成功和社会地位更大的回报。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P2-S3.text: Nothing could persuade me to return to the kind of life Kelsey used to advocate and I once enjoyed: 12-hour working days, pressured deadlines, the fearful strain of office politics and the limitations of being a parent on "quality time".
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P2-S3.translation: 没有什么能说服我回到凯尔西曾经提倡的、我曾经享受过的那种生活：12小时的工作日、紧迫的最后期限、办公室政治的可怕压力以及作为父母在“优质时间”上的限制。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S1.text: In America, the move away from juggling to a simpler, less materialistic lifestyle is a well-established trend.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S1.translation: 在美国，从杂耍转向更简单、更少物质主义的生活方式是一种既定的趋势。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S2.text: Downshifting, also known in America as "voluntary simplicity" has, ironically, even bred a new area of what might be termed anticonsumerism.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S2.translation: 具有讽刺意味的是，降档在美国也被称为“自愿简单”，甚至催生了一个可能被称为反消费主义的新领域。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S3.text: There are a number of bestselling downshifting self-help books for people who want to simplify their lives; there are newsletters, such as The Tightwad Gazette, that give hundreds of thousands of Americans useful tips on anything from recycling their cling-film to making their own soap; there are even support groups for those who want to achieve the mid- '90s equivalent of dropping out.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S3.translation: 有许多畅销的降档自助书籍适合那些想要简化生活的人。有一些时事通讯，例如《吝啬鬼公报》，为成千上万的美国人提供了各种有用的建议，从回收保鲜膜到制作自己的肥皂；甚至还有一些支持团体，为那些想要实现 90 年代中期退学的目标的人提供帮助。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S4.text: While in America the trend started as a reaction to the economic decline—after the mass redundancies caused by downsizing in the late '80s—and is still linked to the politics of thrift, in Britain, at least among the middle-class downshifters of my acquaintance, we have different reasons for seeking to simplify our lives.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S4.translation: 在美国，这种趋势始于对经济衰退的反应——在八十年代末因裁员而导致大规模裁员之后——并且仍然与节俭政治有关，而在英国，至少在我认识的中产阶级中，我们有不同的理由寻求简化我们的生活。

ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S5.text: For the women of my generation who were urged to keep juggling through the '80s, downshifting in the mid-'90s is not so much a search for the mythical good life—growing your own organic vegetables, and risking turning into one—as a personal recognition of your limitations.
ky-en1-2001-r-t5#P3-S5.translation: 对于我们这一代被敦促在 80 年代不断兼顾的女性来说，90 年代中期的放慢生活与其说是对神话般的美好生活的追求——自己种植有机蔬菜，并冒着变成有机蔬菜的风险——不如说是对自己局限性的个人认识。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S1.text: If you intend using humor in your talk to make people smile, you must know how to identify shared experiences and problems.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 如果你想在演讲中使用幽默让人们微笑，你必须知道如何识别共同的经历和问题。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S2.text: Your humor must be relevant to the audience and should help to show them that you are one of them or that you understand their situation and are in sympathy with their point of view.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 你的幽默必须与观众相关，并应有助于向他们表明你是他们中的一员，或者你了解他们的处境并同情他们的观点。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S3.text: Depending on whom you are addressing, the problems will be different.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 根据您要解决的对象不同，问题也会有所不同。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S4.text: If you are talking to a group of managers, you may refer to the disorganized methods of their secretaries; alternatively if you are addressing secretaries, you may want to comment on their disorganized bosses.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 如果你正在和一群经理交谈，你可以参考他们秘书的杂乱无章的方法；或者，如果你向秘书讲话，你可能想评论他们杂乱无章的老板。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S5.text: Here is an example, which I heard at a nurses' convention, of a story which works well because the audience all shared the same view of doctors.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 这是我在护士大会上听到的一个例子，这个故事很有效，因为观众都对医生有相同的看法。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S6.text: A man arrives in heaven and is being shown around by St.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P1-S6.translation: 一个人到达天堂，并在圣约翰的带领下四处参观。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S1.text: He sees wonderful accommodations, beautiful gardens, sunny weather, and so on.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 他看到了美妙的住宿、美丽的花园、阳光明媚的天气等等。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S2.text: Everyone is very peaceful, polite and friendly until, waiting in a line for lunch, the new arrival is suddenly pushed aside by a man in a white coat, who rushes to the head of the line, grabs his food and stomps over to a table by himself.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 每个人都非常平静、礼貌和友好，直到在排队等候午餐时，新来的人突然被一个穿白大褂的男人推到一边，他冲到队伍的最前面，抓起食物，自己跺脚走到一张桌子旁。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S3.text: "Who is that?" the new arrival asked St.

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S5.text: "Oh, that's God," came the reply, "but sometimes he thinks he's a doctor." If you are part of the group which you are addressing, you will be in a position to know the experiences and problems which are common to all of you and it'll be appropriate for you to make a passing remark about the inedible canteen food or the chairman's notorious bad taste in ties.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: “哦，那是上帝，”回答说，“但有时他认为自己是一名医生。”如果你是你正在讲话的群体中的一员，你将能够了解你们所有人共同的经历和问题，并且你可以顺便评论一下食堂的食物难吃或主席在领带方面臭名昭著的糟糕品味。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S6.text: With other audiences you mustn't attempt to cut in with humor as they will resent an outsider making disparaging remarks about their canteen or their chairman.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S6.translation: 对于其他观众，你不能试图以幽默的方式插话，因为他们会讨厌外人对他们的食堂或主席发表贬低性的言论。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S7.text: You will be on safer ground if you stick to scapegoats like the Post Office or the telephone system.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P2-S7.translation: 如果您坚持使用邮局或电话系统等替罪羊，您将处于更安全的境地。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S1.text: If you feel awkward being humorous, you must practice so that it becomes more natural. Include a few casual and apparently off-the-cuff remarks which you can deliver in a relaxed and unforced manner.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 如果你觉得幽默很尴尬，你必须练习，让它变得更自然。包括一些随意且明显即兴的言论，您可以以轻松且不强迫的方式发表这些言论。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S2.text: Often it's the delivery which causes the audience to smile, so speak slowly and remember that a raised eyebrow or an unbelieving look may help to show that you are making a light-hearted remark.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 通常，演讲会让听众微笑，所以要慢慢地说，并记住扬起眉毛或难以置信的表情可能有助于表明你正在发表轻松的言论。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S4.text: It often comes from the unexpected.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: 它常常来自于意想不到的事情。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S5.text: A twist on a familiar quote "If at first you don't succeed, give up" or a play on words or on a situation.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: 这是对一句熟悉的名言“如果一开始没有成功，就放弃”的扭曲，或者是文字游戏或情境游戏。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 寻找夸张和轻描淡写的内容。

ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S7.text: Look at your talk and pick out a few words or sentences which you can turn about and inject with humor.
ky-en1-2002-r-t1#P3-S7.translation: 看看你的演讲，挑出一些你可以翻转并注入幽默的单词或句子。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S1.text: Since the dawn of human ingenuity, people have devised ever more cunning tools to cope with work that is dangerous, boring, burdensome, or just plain nasty.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 自从人类的聪明才智诞生以来，人们发明了越来越狡猾的工具来应对危险、无聊、繁重或纯粹令人讨厌的工作。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S2.text: That compulsion has resulted in robotics—the science of conferring various human capabilities on machines.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 这种冲动催生了机器人技术——将人类的各种能力赋予机器的科学。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S3.text: And if scientists have yet to create the mechanical version of science fiction, they have begun to come close.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 如果科学家们还没有创造出科幻小说的机械版本，那么他们已经开始接近了。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S4.text: As a result, the modern world is increasingly populated by intelligent gizmos whose presence we barely notice but whose universal existence has removed much human labor.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 结果，现代世界中越来越多的智能小玩意儿出现，我们几乎没有注意到它们的存在，但它们的普遍存在却消除了许多人类劳动。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S5.text: Our factories hum to the rhythm of robot assembly arms.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P1-S5.translation: 我们的工厂随着机器人装配臂的节奏而嗡嗡作响。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S1.text: Our banking is done at automated teller terminals that thank us with mechanical politeness for the transaction.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 我们的银行业务是在自动柜员机上完成的，自动柜员机会以机械礼貌的方式感谢我们的交易。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Our subway trains are controlled by tireless robot-drivers.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 我们的地铁列车由不知疲倦的机器人司机控制。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S3.text: And thanks to the continual miniaturization of electronics and micro-mechanics, there are already robot systems that can perform some kinds of brain and bone surgery with submillimeter accuracy—far greater precision than highly skilled physicians can achieve with their hands alone.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S3.translation: 由于电子和微机械的不断小型化，已经有机器人系统可以以亚毫米精度执行某些类型的大脑和骨骼手术，其精度远远高于技术精湛的医生仅靠双手所能达到的精度。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S4.text: But if robots are to reach the next stage of laborsaving utility, they will have to operate with less human supervision and be able to make at least a few decisions for themselves—goals that pose a real challenge.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 但如果机器人要达到节省劳动力的下一阶段，它们将必须在更少的人类监督下运行，并且能够至少自己做出一些决定——这些目标构成了真正的挑战。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S5.text: "While we know how to tell a robot to handle a specific error," says Dave Lavery, manager of a robotics program at NASA, "we can't yet give a robot enough 'common sense' to reliably interact with a dynamic world." Indeed the quest for true artificial intelligence has produced very mixed results.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P2-S5.translation: NASA 机器人项目经理 Dave Lavery 表示：“虽然我们知道如何告诉机器人处理特定错误，但我们还无法赋予机器人足够的‘常识’来与动态世界可靠地交互。”事实上，对真正人工智能的追求已经产生了非常复杂的结果。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S1.text: Despite a spell of initial optimism in the 1960s and 1970s when it appeared that transistor circuits and microprocessors might be able to copy the action of the human brain by the year 2010, researchers lately have begun to extend that forecast by decades if not centuries.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 尽管在 20 世纪 60 年代和 1970 年代，晶体管电路和微处理器可能能够在 2010 年复制人脑的行为，人们对此抱有最初的乐观态度，但研究人员最近开始将这一预测延长了数十年甚至数百年。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S2.text: What they found, in attempting to model thought, is that the human brain's roughly one hundred billion nerve cells are much more talented—and human perception far more complicated—than previously imagined.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 他们在尝试建立思维模型时发现，人类大脑的大约 1000 亿个神经细胞比以前想象的要聪明得多，人类的感知也复杂得多。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S3.text: They have built robots that can recognize the error of a machine panel by a fraction of a millimeter in a controlled factory environment.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S3.translation: 他们制造的机器人可以在受控的工厂环境中识别机器面板的零点几毫米的误差。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S4.text: But the human mind can glimpse a rapidly changing scene and immediately disregard the 98 percent that is irrelevant, instantaneously focusing on the monkey at the side of a winding forest road or the single suspicious face in a big crowd.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S4.translation: 但人类的大脑可以瞥见快速变化的场景，并立即忽略98％的无关紧要的内容，立即将注意力集中在蜿蜒的林道旁的猴子或人群中的一张可疑的面孔上。

ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S5.text: The most advanced computer systems on Earth can't approach that kind of ability, and neuroscientists still don't know quite how we do it.
ky-en1-2002-r-t2#P3-S5.translation: 地球上最先进的计算机系统无法达到这种能力，神经科学家仍然不知道我们是如何做到这一点的。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S1.text: Could the bad old days of economic decline be about to return?
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 经济衰退的糟糕日子会再次出现吗？

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S2.text: Since OPEC agreed to supply-cuts in March, the price of crude oil has jumped to almost $26 a barrel, up from less than $10 last December.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 自 3 月份 OPEC 同意减产以来，原油价格已从去年 12 月的每桶不到 10 美元跃升至近 26 美元。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S3.text: This near-tripling of oil prices calls up scary memories of the 1973 oil shock, when prices quadrupled, and 1979-1980, when they also almost tripled.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 石油价格几乎翻了三倍，让人想起 1973 年石油危机，当时价格翻了两番，而 1979 年至 1980 年，石油价格也几乎翻了三倍。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S4.text: Both previous shocks resulted in double-digit inflation and global economic decline.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 之前的两次冲击都导致了两位数的通货膨胀和全球经济衰退。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S5.text: So where are the headlines warning of gloom and doom this time?
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S5.translation: 那么，这次警告悲观和厄运的头条新闻在哪里呢？

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S6.text: The oil price was given another push up this week when Iraq suspended oil exports.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S6.translation: 本周伊拉克暂停石油出口，油价再次上涨。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S7.text: Strengthening economic growth, at the same time as winter grips the northern hemisphere, could push the price higher still in the short term.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P1-S7.translation: 在北半球冬季来临的同时，经济增长的加强可能会在短期内推高价格。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S1.text: Yet there are good reasons to expect the economic consequences now to be less severe than in the 1970s.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 然而，我们有充分的理由预计现在的经济后果不会比 20 世纪 70 年代那么严重。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S2.text: In most countries the cost of crude oil now accounts for a smaller share of the price of petrol than it did in the 1970s.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 在大多数国家，原油成本目前在汽油价格中所占的比例比 20 世纪 70 年代要小。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S3.text: In Europe, taxes account for up to four-fifths of the retail price, so even quite big changes in the price of crude have a more muted effect on pump prices than in the past.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 在欧洲，税收占零售价格的五分之四，因此即使原油价格发生相当大的变化，对汽油价格的影响也比过去小。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S4.text: Rich economies are also less dependent on oil than they were, and so less sensitive to swings in the oil price.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 富裕经济体对石油的依赖也比以前减少了，因此对石油价格波动的敏感度也降低了。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S5.text: Energy conservation, a shift to other fuels and a decline in the importance of heavy, energy-intensive industries have reduced oil consumption.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S5.translation: 节约能源、转向其他燃料以及重工业、能源密集型工业重要性的下降减少了石油消耗。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S6.text: Software, consultancy and mobile telephones use far less oil than steel or car production.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S6.translation: 软件、咨询和移动电话使用的石油远少于钢铁或汽车生产。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S7.text: For each dollar of GDP (in constant prices) rich economies now use nearly 50% less oil than in 1973.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P2-S7.translation: 富裕经济体现在每增加一美元 GDP（按不变价格计算）的石油用量比 1973 年减少了近 50%。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S1.text: The OECD estimates in its latest Economic Outlook that, if oil prices averaged $22 a barrel for a full year, compared with $13 in 1998, this would increase the oil import bill in rich economies by only 0.25-0.5% of GDP.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 经合组织在其最新的《经济展望》中估计，如果全年油价平均为每桶 22 美元，而 1998 年为每桶 13 美元，那么富裕经济体的石油进口费用仅会增加 GDP 的 0.25-0.5%。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S2.text: That is less than one-quarter of the income loss in 1974 or 1980.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 这还不到 1974 年或 1980 年收入损失的四分之一。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S3.text: On the other hand, oil-importing emerging economies—to which heavy industry has shifted—have become more energy-intensive, and so could be more seriously squeezed.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 另一方面，重工业已转移到石油进口的新兴经济体已成为能源密集型国家，因此可能受到更严重的挤压。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S4.text: One more reason not to lose sleep over the rise in oil prices is that, unlike the rises in the 1970s, it has not occurred against the background of general commodity-price inflation and global excess demand.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 不要因油价上涨而失眠的另一个原因是，与 20 世纪 70 年代的上涨不同，这次上涨并不是在大宗商品价格普遍上涨和全球需求过剩的背景下发生的。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S5.text: A sizable portion of the world is only just emerging from economic decline.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 世界上相当大一部分地区刚刚摆脱经济衰退。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S6.text: The Economist's commodity price index is broadly unchanging from a year ago.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S6.translation: 《经济学人》的商品价格指数与一年前相比基本没有变化。

ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S7.text: In 1973 commodity prices jumped by 70%, and in 1979 by almost 30%.
ky-en1-2002-r-t3#P3-S7.translation: 1973 年，商品价格上涨了 70%，1979 年则上涨了近 30%。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S1.text: The Supreme Court's decisions on physician-assisted suicide carry important implications for how medicine seeks to relieve dying patients of pain and suffering.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 最高法院关于医生协助自杀的裁决对于医学如何寻求减轻垂死患者的痛苦和痛苦具有重要意义。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S2.text: Although it ruled that there is no constitutional right to physician-assisted suicide, the Court in effect supported the medical principle of "double effect", a centuries-old moral principle holding that an action having two effects—a good one that is intended and a harmful one that is foreseen—is permissible if the actor intends only the good effect.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 尽管法院裁定医生协助自杀不存在宪法权利，但法院实际上支持“双重效果”的医学原则，这是一项具有数百年历史的道德原则，认为具有两种效果的行为（一种是有意的好的效果，一种是可预见的有害的效果）是允许的，如果行为者只想获得好的效果。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S3.text: Doctors have used that principle in recent years to justify using high doses of morphine to control terminally ill patients' pain, even though increasing dosages will eventually kill the patient.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 近年来，医生们利用这一原则来证明使用高剂量吗啡来控制绝症患者的疼痛是合理的，尽管增加剂量最终会杀死患者。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S4.text: Nancy Dubler, director of Montefiore Medical Center, contends that the principle will shield doctors who "until now have very, very strongly insisted that they could not give patients sufficient medication to control their pain if that might hasten death".
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P1-S4.translation: 蒙蒂菲奥里医疗中心主任南希·杜布勒 (Nancy Dubler) 认为，这一原则将保护那些“到目前为止，他们非常非常强烈地坚持认为，他们不能给患者提供足够的药物来控制疼痛，如果这可能会加速死亡”的医生。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P2-S1.text: George Annas, chair of the health law department at Boston University, maintains that, as long as a doctor prescribes a drug for a legitimate medical purpose, the doctor has done nothing illegal even if the patient uses the drug to hasten death.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 波士顿大学卫生法系主任乔治·安纳斯认为，只要医生开出的药物是出于合法的医疗目的，即使患者使用药物加速死亡，医生也没有做任何违法的事情。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P2-S3.text: "We don't call those deaths homicides because the doctors didn't intend to kill their patients, although they risked their death.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: “我们不将这些死亡称为他杀，因为医生并没有打算杀死他们的病人，尽管他们冒着死亡的危险。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P2-S4.text: If you're a physician, you can risk your patient's suicide as long as you don't intend their suicide." On another level, many in the medical community acknowledge that the assisted-suicide debate has been fueled in part by the despair of patients for whom modern medicine has prolonged the physical agony of dying.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 如果你是一名医生，只要你不打算让病人自杀，你就可以冒自杀的风险。”在另一个层面上，医学界的许多人承认，辅助自杀的争论在一定程度上是由于病人的绝望而加剧的，现代医学延长了病人临终时的身体痛苦。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S1.text: Just three weeks before the Court's ruling on physician-assisted suicide, the National Academy of Science (NAS) released a two-volume report, Approaching Death: Improving Care at the End of Life.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 就在法院对医生协助自杀做出裁决的三周前，美国国家科学院 (NAS) 发布了一份两卷本的报告，《临近死亡：改善临终护理》。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S2.text: It identifies the undertreatment of pain and the aggressive use of "ineffectual and forced medical procedures that may prolong and even dishonor the period of dying" as the twin problems of end-of-life care.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 它将疼痛治疗不足和过度使用“可能延长甚至羞辱临终时间的无效和强制医疗程序”视为临终关怀的双重问题。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S3.text: The profession is taking steps to require young doctors to train in hospices, to test knowledge of aggressive pain management therapies, to develop a Medicare billing code for hospital-based care, and to develop new standards for assessing and treating pain at the end of life.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S3.translation: 该行业正在采取措施，要求年轻医生在临终关怀中心接受培训，测试积极的疼痛管理疗法的知识，为医院护理制定医疗保险计费代码，并制定评估和治疗临终疼痛的新标准。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S4.text: Annas says lawyers can play a key role in insisting that these well-meaning medical initiatives translate into better care.
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S4.translation: 安纳斯表示，律师可以发挥关键作用，坚持将这些善意的医疗举措转化为更好的护理。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S5.text: "Large numbers of physicians seem unconcerned with the pain their patients are needlessly and predictably suffering", to the extent that it constitutes "systematic patient abuse".
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S5.translation: “大量医生似乎并不关心患者不必要且可预见地遭受的痛苦”，以至于构成“系统性的患者虐待”。

ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S6.text: He says medical licensing boards "must make it clear...that painful deaths are presumptively ones that are incompetently managed and should result in license suspension".
ky-en1-2002-r-t4#P3-S6.translation: 他说，医疗许可委员会“必须明确……痛苦的死亡可能是管理不善造成的，应该导致执照被吊销”。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S1.text: Wild Bill Donovan would have loved the Internet.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 狂野的比尔·多诺万一定会喜欢互联网。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S2.text: The American spymaster who built the Office of Strategic Services in the World War Ⅱ and later laid the roots for the CIA was fascinated with information.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 这位在第二次世界大战期间建立战略情报局、后来为中央情报局奠定基础的美国间谍头子对信息非常着迷。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S3.text: Donovan believed in using whatever tools came to hand in the "great game" of espionage—spying as a "profession." These days the Net, which has already re-made such everyday pastimes as buying books and sending mail, is reshaping Donovan's vocation as well.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 多诺万相信在间谍活动的“伟大游戏”中使用任何可用的工具——间谍作为一种“职业”。如今，网络已经重新塑造了购买书籍和发送邮件等日常消遣方式，也正在重塑多诺万的职业。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S4.text: The latest revolution isn't simply a matter of gentlemen reading other gentlemen's e-mail.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 最新的革命不仅仅是绅士们阅读其他绅士的电子邮件的问题。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S5.text: That kind of electronic spying has been going on for decades.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 这种电子间谍活动已经持续了几十年。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S6.text: In the past three or four years, the World Wide Web has given birth to a whole industry of point-and-click spying.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P1-S6.translation: 在过去的三四年里，万维网催生了整个点击式间谍活动行业。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S1.text: The spooks call it "open source intelligence," and as the Net grows, it is becoming increasingly influential. In 1995 the CIA held a contest to see who could compile the most data about Burundi.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 间谍们称之为“开源情报”，随着网络的发展，它的影响力也越来越大。 1995年，中央情报局举办了一场竞赛，看谁能收集最多有关布隆迪的数据。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S2.text: The winner, by a large margin, was a tiny Virginia company called Open-Source Solutions, whose clear advantage was its mastery of the electronic world.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 以较大优势获胜的是弗吉尼亚州一家名为“开源解决方案”的小公司，该公司的明显优势是对电子世界的掌控。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S3.text: Among the firms making the biggest splash in the new world is Straitford, Inc., a private intelligence-analysis firm based in Austin, Texas.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S3.translation: 在新世界中引起最大关注的公司之一是 Straitford, Inc.，这是一家总部位于德克萨斯州奥斯汀的私人情报分析公司。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S4.text: Straitford makes money by selling the results of spying (covering nations from Chile to Russia) to corporations like energy-services firm McDermott International. Many of its predictions are available online at .
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S4.translation: 斯特雷特福德通过向能源服务公司麦克德莫特国际公司等公司出售间谍活动的结果（覆盖从智利到俄罗斯的国家）来赚钱。它的许多预测都可以在网上找到。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S5.text: Straiford president George Friedman says he sees the online world as a kind of mutually reinforcing tool for both information collection and distribution, a spymaster's dream.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: 斯特莱福德总裁乔治·弗里德曼表示，他将网络世界视为一种信息收集和分发的相辅相成的工具，这是间谍头子的梦想。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S6.text: Last week his firm was busy vacuuming up data bits from the far corners of the world and predicting a crisis in Ukraine.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P2-S6.translation: 上周，他的公司正忙于从世界遥远的角落收集数据并预测乌克兰的危机。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S1.text: "As soon as that report runs, we'll suddenly get 500 new internet sign-ups from Ukraine," says Friedman, a former political science professor.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 前政治学教授弗里德曼表示：“该报告一发布，我们就会突然从乌克兰获得 500 个新的互联网注册用户。”

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S2.text: "And we'll hear back from some of them." Open-source spying does have its risks, of course, since it can be difficult to tell good information from bad.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: “我们会收到其中一些人的回复。”当然，开源间谍活动确实有其风险，因为很难区分好信息和坏信息。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S3.text: That's where Straitford earns its keep.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 这就是斯特雷特福德赖以生存的地方。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S4.text: Friedman relies on a lean staff of 20 in Austin.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: Friedman 在奥斯汀拥有 20 名精干员工。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S5.text: Several of his staff members have military intelligence backgrounds.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: 他的几名幕僚拥有军事情报背景。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S6.text: He sees the firm's outsider status as the key to its success.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 他认为公司的局外人地位是其成功的关键。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S7.text: Straitford's briefs don't sound like the usual Washington back-and-forthing, whereby agencies avoid dramatic declarations on the chance they might be wrong.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S7.translation: 斯特雷特福德的简报听起来不像华盛顿通常的来来回回，各机构避免发表戏剧性的声明，以免自己可能出错。

ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S8.text: Straitford, says Friedman, takes pride in its independent voice.
ky-en1-2003-r-t1#P3-S8.translation: 弗里德曼说，斯特雷特福德为其独立的声音感到自豪。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S1.text: To paraphrase 18th-century statesman Edmund Burke, "all that is needed for the triumph of a misguided cause is that good people do nothing." One such cause now seeks to end biomedical research because of the theory that animals have rights ruling out their use in research.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 用 18 世纪政治家埃德蒙·伯克的话来说，“要让被误导的事业取得胜利，所需要的只是好人什么也不做。”现在，这样的原因之一就是寻求结束生物医学研究，因为动物有权排除其在研究中的使用。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S2.text: Scientists need to respond forcefully to animal rights advocates, whose arguments are confusing the public and thereby threatening advances in health knowledge and care.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 科学家需要对动物权利倡导者做出强有力的回应，他们的论点让公众感到困惑，从而威胁到健康知识和护理的进步。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S3.text: Leaders of the animal rights movement target biomedical research because it depends on public funding, and few people understand the process of health care research.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 动物权利运动的领导人瞄准生物医学研究，因为它依赖公共资金，而且很少有人了解医疗保健研究的过程。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S4.text: Hearing allegations of cruelty to animals in research settings, many are perplexed that anyone would deliberately harm an animal. For example, a grandmotherly woman staffing an animal rights booth at a recent street fair was distributing a brochure that encouraged readers not to use anything that comes from or is tested in animals—no meat, no fur, no medicines.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 听到有关在研究环境中虐待动物的指控，许多人对有人会故意伤害动物感到困惑。例如，在最近的街头集市上，一位在动物权利摊位工作的老奶奶正在分发一本小册子，鼓励读者不要使用任何来自动物或经过动物测试的东西——没有肉、没有皮毛、没有药物。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S5.text: Asked if she opposed immunizations, she wanted to know if vaccines come from animal research.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P1-S5.translation: 当被问及是否反对免疫接种时，她想知道疫苗是否来自动物研究。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S1.text: When assured that they do, she replied, "Then I would have to say yes." Asked what will happen when epidemics return, she said, "Don't worry, scientists will find some way of using computers." Such well-meaning people just don't understand.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 当确信他们会这样做时，她回答说：“那我就不得不答应了。”当被问及流行病卷土重来时会发生什么时，她说：“别担心，科学家会找到一些使用计算机的方法。”这么好心的人就是不明白。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Scientists must communicate their message to the public in a compassionate, understandable way—in human terms, not in the language of molecular biology.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 科学家必须以一种富有同情心、易于理解的方式向公众传达他们的信息——用人类的语言，而不是分子生物学的语言。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S3.text: We need to make clear the connection between animal research and a grandmother's hip replacement, a father's bypass operation, a baby's vaccinations, and even a pet's shots.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S3.translation: 我们需要弄清楚动物研究与祖母的髋关节置换术、父亲的搭桥手术、婴儿的疫苗接种，甚至宠物的注射之间的联系。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S4.text: To those who are unaware that animal research was needed to produce these treatments, as well as new treatments and vaccines, animal research seems wasteful at best and cruel at worst.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 对于那些不知道需要动物研究来生产这些治疗方法以及新疗法和疫苗的人来说，动物研究往好里说是浪费，往坏里说是残酷的。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S1.text: Scientists could "adopt" middle school classes and present their own research.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 科学家可以“采用”中学课程并展示他们自己的研究。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S2.text: They should be quick to respond to letters to the editor, lest animal rights misinformation go unchallenged and acquire a deceptive appearance of truth.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 他们应该迅速回复给编辑的信，以免动物权利的错误信息不受质疑，并获得具有欺骗性的真相。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S3.text: Research institutions could be opened to tours, to show that laboratory animals receive humane care.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S3.translation: 研究机构可以开放参观，以表明实验动物受到人道关怀。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S4.text: Finally, because the ultimate stakeholders are patients, the health research community should actively recruit to its cause not only well-known personalities such as Stephen Cooper, who has made courageous statements about the value of animal research, but all who receive medical treatment.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S4.translation: 最后，由于最终的利益相关者是患者，健康研究界不仅应该积极招募像斯蒂芬·库珀（Stephen Cooper）这样的知名人士来支持其事业，而且还应该招募所有接受治疗的人，斯蒂芬·库珀曾勇敢地阐述了动物研究的价值。

ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S5.text: If good people do nothing, there is a real possibility that an uninformed citizenry will extinguish the precious embers of medical progress.
ky-en1-2003-r-t2#P3-S5.translation: 如果好人不采取任何行动，不知情的公民很可能会扑灭医学进步的宝贵余烬。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S1.text: In recent years, railroads have been combining with each other, merging into supersystems, causing heightened concerns about monopoly.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 近年来，铁路相互结合，合并成超级系统，引发了人们对垄断的担忧。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S2.text: As recently as 1995, the top four railroads accounted for under 70 percent of the total ton-miles moved by rails.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 就在 1995 年，四大铁路的运输量还不到铁路运输总吨英里的 70%。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S3.text: Next year, after a series of mergers is completed, just four railroads will control well over 90 percent of all the freight moved by major rail carriers.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 明年，一系列合并完成后，仅四家铁路公司就将控制主要铁路运输公司运输量的 90% 以上。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S4.text: Supporters of the new supersystems argue that these mergers will allow for substantial cost reductions and better coordinated service.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 新超级系统的支持者认为，这些合并将大幅降低成本并提供更好的协调服务。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S5.text: Any threat of monopoly, they argue, is removed by fierce competition from trucks.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S5.translation: 他们认为，卡车的激烈竞争可以消除任何垄断威胁。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S6.text: But many shippers complain that for heavy bulk commodities traveling long distances, such as coal, chemicals, and grain, trucking is too costly and the railroads therefore have them by the throat.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P1-S6.translation: 但许多托运人抱怨说，对于长途运输的大宗商品，如煤炭、化学品和谷物，卡车运输成本太高，因此被铁路扼住了喉咙。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S1.text: The vast consolidation within the rail industry means that most shippers are served by only one rail company.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 铁路行业内的大规模整合意味着大多数托运人仅由一家铁路公司提供服务。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S2.text: Railroads typically charge such "captive" shippers 20 to 30 percent more than they do when another railroad is competing for the business.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 铁路公司向此类“专属”托运人收取的费用通常比其他铁路公司竞争该业务时高出 20% 至 30%。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S3.text: Shippers who feel they are being overcharged have the right to appeal to the federal government's Surface Transportation Board for rate relief, but the process is expensive, time consuming, and will work only in truly extreme cases.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 认为自己被多收费用的托运人有权向联邦政府的地面运输委员会请求减免费率，但这一过程既昂贵又耗时，而且只有在真正极端的情况下才有效。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S4.text: Railroads justify rate discrimination against captive shippers on the grounds that in the long run it reduces everyone's cost.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 铁路公司证明对自营托运人实行费率歧视是合理的，因为从长远来看，这会降低每个人的成本。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S5.text: If railroads charged all customers the same average rate, they argue, shippers who have the option of switching to trucks or other forms of transportation would do so, leaving remaining customers to shoulder the cost of keeping up the line.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S5.translation: 他们认为，如果铁路对所有客户收取相同的平均费率，那么可以选择改用卡车或其他运输方式的托运人就会这样做，而剩下的客户则需要承担维持线路的成本。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S6.text: It's a theory to which many economists subscribe, but in practice it often leaves railroads in the position of determining which companies will flourish and which will fail.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P2-S6.translation: 这是许多经济学家都认同的理论，但在实践中，它常常让铁路公司处于决定哪些公司将蓬勃发展、哪些公司将失败的位置。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S1.text: "Do we really want railroads to be the arbiters of who wins and who loses in the marketplace?" asks Martin Bercovici, a Washington lawyer who frequently represents shippers.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: “我们真的希望铁路成为市场上谁赢谁输的仲裁者吗？”经常代表托运人的华盛顿律师马丁·贝尔科维奇问道。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S2.text: Many captive shippers also worry they will soon be hit with a round of huge rate increases.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 许多自保托运人还担心他们很快就会受到一轮大幅费率上涨的打击。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S3.text: The railroad industry as a whole, despite its brightening fortunes, still does not earn enough to cover the cost of the capital it must invest to keep up with its surging traffic.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 整个铁路行业，尽管其财富不断增加，但收入仍然不足以支付其必须投资的资本成本，以跟上激增的运输量。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S4.text: Yet railroads continue to borrow billions to acquire one another, with Wall Street cheering them on.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 然而，铁路公司继续借贷数十亿美元相互收购，华尔街为它们喝彩。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S5.text: Consider the $10.2 billion bid by Norfolk Southern and CSX to acquire Conrail this year.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 考虑一下今年诺福克南方铁路公司和 CSX 出价 102 亿美元收购联合铁路公司的情况。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S6.text: Conrail's net railway operating income in 1996 was just $427 million, less than half of the carrying costs of the transaction.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S6.translation: 联合铁路公司 1996 年的铁路运营净收入仅为 4.27 亿美元，不到交易持有成本的一半。

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S7.text: Who's going to pay for the rest of the bill?
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S7.translation: 谁来支付账单的其余部分？

ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S8.text: Many captive shippers fear that they will, as Norfolk Southern and CSX increase their grip on the market.
ky-en1-2003-r-t3#P3-S8.translation: 随着诺福克南方航空和 CSX 加强对市场的控制，许多自保托运人担心他们会这么做。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S1.text: It is said that in England death is pressing, in Canada inevitable and in California optional. Small wonder.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 据说，死亡在英国是紧迫的，在加拿大是不可避免的，而在加利福尼亚是可选的。没什么奇怪的。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S2.text: Americans' life expectancy has nearly doubled over the past century.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 在过去的一个世纪里，美国人的预期寿命几乎翻了一番。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S3.text: Failing hips can be replaced, clinical depression controlled, cataracts removed in a 30-minute surgical procedure.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 在 30 分钟的手术过程中，可以更换失效的髋关节、控制临床抑郁症、去除白内障。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S4.text: Such advances offer the aging population a quality of life that was unimaginable when I entered medicine 50 years ago.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S4.translation: 这些进步为老龄化人口提供了50年前我进入医学界时难以想象的生活质量。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S5.text: But not even a great health-care system can cure death—and our failure to confront that reality now threatens this greatness of ours.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S5.translation: 但即使是一个伟大的医疗保健系统也无法治愈死亡——而我们未能面对这一现实，现在威胁着我们的伟大。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S6.text: Death is normal; we are genetically programmed to disintegrate and perish, even under ideal conditions.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S6.translation: 死亡是正常的；即使在理想的条件下，我们的基因也注定会瓦解和灭亡。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S7.text: We all understand that at some level, yet as medical consumers we treat death as a problem to be solved.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S7.translation: 我们都明白，在某种程度上，但作为医疗消费者，我们将死亡视为一个需要解决的问题。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S8.text: Shielded by third-party payers from the cost of our care, we demand everything that can possibly be done for us, even if it's useless.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P1-S8.translation: 由于第三方支付者保护我们免于支付护理费用，我们要求为我们做一切可能的事情，即使它是无用的。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S1.text: The most obvious example is late-stage cancer care.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 最明显的例子是晚期癌症护理。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S2.text: Physicians—frustrated by their inability to cure the disease and fearing loss of hope in the patient—too often offer aggressive treatment far beyond what is scientifically justified.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 医生们因无法治愈疾病而感到沮丧，并担心患者失去希望，常常提供远远超出科学合理范围的积极治疗。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S3.text: In 1950, the US spent $12.7 billion on health care.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: 1950年，美国在医疗保健上的支出为127亿美元。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S4.text: In 2002, the cost will be $1,540 billion.

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S5.text: Anyone can see this trend is unsustainable.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S5.translation: 任何人都可以看出这种趋势是不可持续的。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S6.text: Yet few seem willing to try to reverse it.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S6.translation: 然而似乎很少有人愿意尝试扭转这一局面。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S7.text: Some scholars conclude that a government with finite resources should simply stop paying for medical care that sustains life beyond a certain age—say 83 or so.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S7.translation: 一些学者的结论是，资源有限的政府应该停止支付维持生命超过一定年龄（例如 83 岁左右）的医疗费用。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S8.text: Former Colorado governor Richard Lamm has been quoted as saying that the old and infirm "have a duty to die and get out of the way", so that younger, healthier people can realize their potential. I would not go that far.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P2-S8.translation: 前科罗拉多州州长理查德·拉姆曾被引述说，年老体弱的人“有责任死去并离开”，以便更年轻、更健康的人能够发挥他们的潜力。我不会走那么远。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S1.text: Energetic people now routinely work through their 60s and beyond, and remain dazzlingly productive.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 现在，精力充沛的人们通常会工作到 60 多岁甚至更久，并且仍然保持着令人眼花缭乱的生产力。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S2.text: At 78, Viacom chairman Sumner Redstone jokingly claims to be 53.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 78 岁的维亚康姆董事长萨姆纳·雷石东开玩笑地声称自己 53 岁。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S3.text: Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O'Connor is in her 70s, and former surgeon general C.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S3.translation: 最高法院法官桑德拉·戴·奥康纳 (Sandra Day O'Connor) 已经 70 多岁了，前卫生局局长 C.

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S4.text: Everett Koop chairs an Internet start-up in his 80s.These leaders are living proof that prevention works and that we can manage the health problems that come naturally with age.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S4.translation: 80 多岁的埃弗雷特·库普 (Everett Koop) 是一家互联网初创公司的董事长。这些领导人是预防工作有效的活生生证明，也证明我们可以应对随着年龄增长而自然出现的健康问题。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S5.text: As a mere 68-year-old, I wish to age as productively as they have.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S5.translation: 作为一个年仅 68 岁的人，我希望能像他们一样富有成效地变老。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S6.text: Yet there are limits to what a society can spend in this pursuit.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S6.translation: 然而，社会在这一追求上的投入是有限的。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S7.text: As a physician, I know the most costly and dramatic measures may be ineffective and painful.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S7.translation: 作为一名医生，我知道最昂贵和最戏剧性的措施可能是无效和痛苦的。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S8.text: I also know that people in Japan and Sweden, countries that spend far less on medical care, have achieved longer, healthier lives than we have.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S8.translation: 我还知道，日本和瑞典的人们在医疗保健方面的支出要少得多，但他们的寿命却比我们更长、更健康。

ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S9.text: As a nation, we may be overfunding the quest for unlikely cures while underfunding research on humbler therapies that could improve people's lives.
ky-en1-2003-r-t4#P3-S9.translation: 作为一个国家，我们可能为寻求不太可能的治疗方法提供了过多的资金，而对可以改善人们生活的更简单的疗法的研究提供了不足的资金。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S1.text: Hunting for a job late last year, lawyer Gant Redmon stumbled across CareerBuilder, a job database on the Internet.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 去年年底，Gant Redmon 律师在寻找工作时偶然发现了 CareerBuilder，这是互联网上的一个工作数据库。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S2.text: He searched it with no success but was attracted by the site's "personal search agent".
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 他搜索没有成功，但被该网站的“个人搜索代理”所吸引。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S3.text: It's an interactive feature that lets visitors key in job criteria such as location, title, and salary, then E-mails them when a matching position is posted in the database.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 它是一种交互式功能，允许访问者输入工作条件，例如地点、职位和薪水，然后在数据库中发布匹配的职位时向他们发送电子邮件。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S4.text: Redmon chose the keywords legal, intellectual property and Washington, D.C.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 雷德蒙选择了关键词“法律”、“知识产权”和“华盛顿特区”。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S5.text: Three weeks later, he got his first notification of an opening.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 三周后，他收到了第一份空缺通知。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S6.text: "I struck gold," says Redmon, who E-mailed his resume to the employer and won a position as in-house counsel for a company.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S6.translation: “我找到了金子，”雷德蒙说，他通过电子邮件将简历发送给雇主，并赢得了一家公司内部法律顾问的职位。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S7.text: With thousands of career-related sites on the Internet, finding promising openings can be time-consuming and inefficient.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P1-S7.translation: 互联网上有数以千计的职业相关网站，寻找有前途的空缺职位可能既耗时又低效。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S1.text: Search agents reduce the need for repeated visits to the databases.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 搜索代理减少了重复访问数据库的需要。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S2.text: But although a search agent worked for Redmon, career experts see drawbacks.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 不过，尽管雷德蒙公司有一名猎头代理，但职业专家却看到了它的缺点。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S3.text: Narrowing your criteria, for example, may work against you: "Every time you answer a question you eliminate a possibility," says one expert.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S3.translation: 例如，缩小你的标准可能会对你不利：“每次你回答一个问题，你就消除了一种可能性，”一位专家说。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S4.text: For any job search, you should start with a narrow concept—what you think you want to do—then broaden it.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S4.translation: 对于任何求职，你都应该从一个狭隘的概念开始——你认为你想做的事情——然后扩大它。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S5.text: "None of these programs do that," says another expert.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: 另一位专家表示：“这些程序都没有做到这一点。”

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S6.text: "There's no career counseling implicit in all of this." Instead, the best strategy is to use the agent as a kind of tip service to keep abreast of jobs in a particular database; when you get E-mail, consider it a reminder to check the database again.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S6.translation: “这一切并不隐含职业咨询。”相反，最好的策略是使用代理作为一种小费服务，以随时了解特定数据库中的工作情况；当您收到电子邮件时，请将其视为再次检查数据库的提醒。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S7.text: "I would not rely on agents for finding everything that is added to a database that might interest me," says the author of a job-searching guide.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P2-S7.translation: “我不会依靠代理来查找数据库中添加的我可能感兴趣的所有内容，”求职指南的作者说。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S1.text: Some sites design their agents to tempt job hunters to return.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 一些网站设计其代理来吸引求职者回国。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S2.text: When CareerSite's agent sends out messages to those who have signed up for its service, for example, it includes only three potential jobs—those it considers the best matches.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 例如，当 CareerSite 的代理向那些注册其服务的人发送消息时，它只包含三个潜在的工作——它认为最匹配的工作。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S3.text: There may be more matches in the database; job hunters will have to visit the site again to find them—and they do.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 数据库中可能还有更多匹配项；求职者将不得不再次访问该网站才能找到他们——他们确实做到了。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S4.text: "On the day after we send our messages, we see a sharp increase in our traffic," says Seth Peets, vice president of marketing for CareerSite.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: CareerSite 营销副总裁 Seth Peets 表示：“发送消息后的第二天，我们发现流量急剧增加。”

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S5.text: Even those who aren't hunting for jobs may find search agents worthwhile.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: 即使那些不寻找工作的人也可能会发现搜索代理是值得的。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S6.text: Some use them to keep a close watch on the demand for their line of work or gather information on compensation to arm themselves when negotiating for a raise.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 有些人用它们来密切关注自己工作的需求，或者收集薪酬信息，以便在谈判加薪时武装自己。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S7.text: Although happily employed, Redmon maintains his agent at CareerBuilder.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S7.translation: 尽管雷德蒙的工作很愉快，但他的经纪人仍留在 CareerBuilder。

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S8.text: "You always keep your eyes open," he says.

ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S9.text: Working with a personal search agent means having another set of eyes looking out for you.
ky-en1-2004-r-t1#P3-S9.translation: 与个人搜索代理合作意味着有另一双眼睛在注视着您。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S1.text: Over the past century, all kinds of unfairness and discrimination have been condemned or made illegal. But one insidious form continues to thrive: alphabetism.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 一个世纪以来，各种不公平和歧视行为都受到谴责或被定为非法。但一种阴险的形式继续盛行：字母顺序。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S2.text: This, for those as yet unaware of such a disadvantage, refers to discrimination against those whose surnames begin with a letter in the lower half of the alphabet.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 对于那些尚未意识到这种劣势的人来说，这是指对姓氏以字母表下半部分字母开头的人的歧视。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S3.text: It has long been known that a taxi firm called AAAA cars has a big advantage over Zodiac cars when customers thumb through their phone directories.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 人们早就知道，当顾客翻阅电话簿时，一家名为 AAAA cars 的出租车公司比 Zodiac cars 有很大的优势。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S4.text: Less well known is the advantage that Adam Abbott has in life over Zoë Zysman.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 不太为人所知的是亚当·阿博特 (Adam Abbott) 在生活中相对于佐伊·齐斯曼 (Zoë Zysman) 的优势。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S5.text: English names are fairly evenly spread between the halves of the alphabet.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S5.translation: 英文名字相当均匀地分布在字母表的两半部分。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S6.text: Yet a suspiciously large number of top people have surnames beginning with letters between A and K.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P1-S6.translation: 然而，令人怀疑的是，大量高层人士的姓氏以 A 和 K 之间的字母开头。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S1.text: Thus the American president and vice-president have surnames starting with B and C respectively; and 26 of George Bush's predecessors (including his father) had surnames in the first half of the alphabet against just 16 in the second half.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 因此，美国总统和副总统的姓氏分别以B和C开头；乔治·布什的前任中有 26 位（包括他的父亲）的姓氏是字母表的前半部分，而后半部分的姓氏只有 16 个。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Even more striking, six of the seven heads of government of the G7 rich countries are alphabetically advantaged (Berlusconi, Blair, Bush, Chirac, Chrétien and Koizumi).
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 更引人注目的是，七国集团富裕国家的七位政府首脑中有六位按字母顺序排列占优势（贝卢斯科尼、布莱尔、布什、希拉克、克雷蒂安和小泉）。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S3.text: The world's three top central bankers (Greenspan, Duisenberg and Hayami) are all close to the top of the alphabet, even if one of them really uses Japanese characters.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S3.translation: 世界三大央行行长（格林斯潘、杜伊森贝格和速水）都接近字母表的顶端，即使其中一位真的使用日语字符。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S4.text: As are the world's five richest men (Gates, Buffett, Allen, Ellison and Albrecht).
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 世界上最富有的五位人士（盖茨、巴菲特、艾伦、埃里森和阿尔布雷希特）也是如此。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S6.text: One theory, dreamt up in all the spare time enjoyed by the alphabetically disadvantaged, is that the rot sets in early.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P2-S6.translation: 一种理论是，按字母顺序处于劣势的人在所有空闲时间里都梦想着，这种腐烂很早就开始了。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S1.text: At the start of the first year in infant school, teachers seat pupils alphabetically from the front, to make it easier to remember their names.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 在婴儿学校第一学年开始时，老师会按照字母顺序从前面安排学生就座，以便更容易记住他们的名字。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S2.text: So short-sighted Zysman junior gets stuck in the back row, and is rarely asked the improving questions posed by those insensitive teachers.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 因此，目光短浅的齐斯曼小学生被困在后排，很少被那些麻木不仁的老师提出改进的问题。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S3.text: At the time the alphabetically disadvantaged may think they have had a lucky escape.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S3.translation: 当时，按字母顺序处于劣势的人可能认为他们幸运地逃脱了。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S4.text: Yet the result may be worse qualifications, because they get less individual attention, as well as less confidence in speaking publicly.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S4.translation: 然而，结果可能是资质较差，因为他们受到的个人关注较少，公开演讲的信心也较低。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S6.text: At university graduation ceremonies, the ABCs proudly get their awards first; by the time they reach the Zysmans most people are literally having a ZZZ.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S6.translation: 在大学毕业典礼上，ABC 们自豪地第一个获得奖项；当他们到达 Zysmans 时，大多数人都已经感到 ZZZ 了。

ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S7.text: Shortlists for job interviews, election ballot papers, lists of conference speakers and attendees: all tend to be drawn up alphabetically, and their recipients lose interest as they plough through them.
ky-en1-2004-r-t2#P3-S7.translation: 工作面试的入围名单、选举选票、会议发言人和与会者名单：所有这些都往往是按字母顺序列出的，收件人在仔细阅读这些内容时就会失去兴趣。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S1.text: When it comes to the slowing economy, Ellen Spero isn't biting her nails just yet.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 谈到经济放缓，艾伦·斯佩罗 (Ellen Spero) 还没有咬指甲。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S2.text: But the 47-year-old manicurist isn't cutting, filing or polishing as many nails as she'd like to, either.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 但这位 47 岁的美甲师也没有按照自己的意愿剪、锉或抛光指甲。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S3.text: Most of her clients spend $12 to $50 weekly, but last month two longtime customers suddenly stopped showing up.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 她的大多数客户每周花费 12 至 50 美元，但上个月，两位长期客户突然不再出现。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 斯佩罗将此归咎于经济疲软。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S5.text: "I'm a good economic indicator," she says.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S5.translation: “我是一个很好的经济指标，”她说。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S6.text: "I provide a service that people can do without when they're concerned about saving some dollars." So Spero is downscaling, shopping at middle-brow Dillard's department store near her suburban Cleveland home, instead of Neiman Marcus.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S6.translation: “当人们担心节省一些钱时，我提供的服务是可以不需要的。”因此，斯佩罗正在缩小规模，在她位于克利夫兰郊区的家附近的中产阶级迪拉德百货公司购物，而不是在尼曼·马库斯 (Neiman Marcus)。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S7.text: "I don't know if other clients are going to abandon me, too," she says.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S7.translation: “我不知道其他客户是否也会抛弃我，”她说。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S8.text: Even before Alan Greenspan's admission that America's red-hot economy is cooling, lots of working folks had already seen signs of the slowdown themselves.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S8.translation: 甚至在艾伦·格林斯潘承认美国炙手可热的经济正在降温之前，许多工薪阶层就已经看到了经济放缓的迹象。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S9.text: From car dealerships to Gap outlets, sales have been lagging for months as shoppers temper their spending.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P1-S9.translation: 从汽车经销店到 Gap 专卖店，由于购物者减少支出，销售已经滞后数月。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S1.text: For retailers, who last year took in 24 percent of their revenue between Thanksgiving and Christmas, the cautious approach is coming at a crucial time.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 对于去年感恩节和圣诞节之间收入占总收入 24% 的零售商来说，他们在关键时刻采取了谨慎的态度。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S2.text: Already, experts say, holiday sales are off 7 percent from last year's pace.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 专家表示，假日销售已经比去年下降了 7%。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S3.text: But don't sound any alarms just yet.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 但暂时不要拉响任何警报。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S4.text: Consumers seem only mildly concerned, not panicked, and many say they remain optimistic about the economy's long-term prospects even as they do some modest belt-tightening.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 消费者似乎只是轻度担忧，并不惊慌，许多人表示，尽管他们适度勒紧裤腰带，但他们对经济的长期前景仍然持乐观态度。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S5.text: Consumers say they're not in despair because, despite the dreadful headlines, their own fortunes still feel pretty good.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S5.translation: 消费者表示，他们并不绝望，因为尽管有可怕的头条新闻，但他们自己的命运仍然不错。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S6.text: Home prices are holding steady in most regions.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S6.translation: 大多数地区的房价保持稳定。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S7.text: In Manhattan, "there's a new gold rush happening in the $4 million to $10 million range, predominantly fed by Wall Street bonuses," says broker Barbara Corcoran.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S7.translation: 经纪人芭芭拉·科克伦 (Barbara Corcoran) 表示，在曼哈顿，“新一轮淘金热正在兴起，价值 400 万至 1000 万美元，主要由华尔街奖金推动”。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S8.text: In San Francisco, prices are still rising even as frenzied overbidding quiets.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S8.translation: 在旧金山，尽管疯狂的竞价平静下来，但价格仍在上涨。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S9.text: "Instead of 20 to 30 offers, now maybe you only get two or three," says John Tealdi, a Bay Area real-estate broker.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P2-S9.translation: 湾区房地产经纪人约翰·蒂尔迪 (John Tealdi) 表示：“现在你可能只会收到两到三个报价，而不是 20 到 30 个。”

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S1.text: And most folks still feel pretty comfortable about their ability to find and keep a job.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 大多数人仍然对自己找到并保住工作的能力感到非常满意。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S2.text: Many folks see silver linings to this slowdown.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 许多人看到了经济放缓的一线希望。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S3.text: Potential home buyers would cheer for lower interest rates.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 潜在的购房者将为较低的利率欢呼。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S4.text: Employers wouldn't mind a little fewer bubbles in the job market.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 雇主不会介意就业市场的泡沫少一点。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S5.text: Many consumers seem to have been influenced by stock-market swings, which investors now view as a necessary ingredient to a sustained boom.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 许多消费者似乎受到股市波动的影响，投资者现在认为股市波动是持续繁荣的必要因素。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S6.text: Diners might see an upside, too.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S6.translation: 食客也可能会看到好处。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S7.text: Getting a table at Manhattan's hot new Alain Ducasse restaurant used to be impossible.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S7.translation: 过去，在曼哈顿新开的热门阿兰·杜卡斯餐厅 (Alain Ducasse) 订到一张桌子是不可能的。

ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S9.text: For that, Greenspan & Co. may still be worth toasting.
ky-en1-2004-r-t3#P3-S9.translation: 就这一点而言，格林斯潘公司可能仍然值得庆贺。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S1.text: Americans today don't place a very high value on intellect.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 今天的美国人并不十分看重智力。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S2.text: Our heroes are athletes, entertainers, and entrepreneurs, not scholars.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 我们的英雄是运动员、演艺人员和企业家，而不是学者。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S3.text: Even our schools are where we send our children to get a practical education—not to pursue knowledge for the sake of knowledge.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 甚至我们的学校也是我们送孩子接受实践教育的地方，而不是为了知识而追求知识。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S4.text: Symptoms of pervasive anti-intellectualism in our schools aren't difficult to find.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S4.translation: 我们学校中普遍存在的反智主义症状并不难发现。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S5.text: "Schools have always been in a society where practical is more important than intellectual," says education writer Diane Ravitch.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S5.translation: “学校一直处于一个实践比知识更重要的社会，”教育作家黛安·拉维奇说。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S6.text: "Schools could be a counterbalance." Ravitch's latest book.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S6.translation: “学校可以起到平衡作用。”拉维奇的最新书。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S7.text: Left Back: A Century of Failed School Reforms, traces the roots of anti-intellectualism in our schools, concluding they are anything but a counterbalance to the American distaste for intellectual pursuits.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P1-S7.translation: 《左后：一个世纪失败的学校改革》追溯了我们学校中反智主义的根源，得出的结论是它们根本无法平衡美国人对知识追求的厌恶。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S1.text: But they could and should be.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 但他们可以而且应该这样做。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S2.text: Encouraging kids to reject the life of the mind leaves them vulnerable to exploitation and control.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 鼓励孩子拒绝精神生活会让他们容易受到剥削和控制。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S3.text: Without the ability to think critically, to defend their ideas and understand the ideas of others, they cannot fully participate in our democracy.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: 如果没有批判性思考、捍卫自己的想法和理解他人的想法的能力，他们就无法充分参与我们的民主。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S4.text: Continuing along this path, says writer Earl Shorris, "We will become a second-rate country.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 作家厄尔·肖里斯说，继续沿着这条路走下去，“我们将成为二流国家。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S5.text: We will have a less civil society." "Intellect is resented as a form of power or privilege," writes historian and professor Richard Hofstadter in Anti-intellectualism in American Life, a Pulitzer-Prize winning book on the roots of anti-intellectualism in US politics, religion, and education.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S5.translation: 我们将拥有一个更少的公民社会。”历史学家兼教授理查德·霍夫施塔特（Richard Hofstadter）在《美国生活中的反智主义》一书中写道，“智力作为一种权力或特权形式而受到憎恨。”这本普利策奖得主著作探讨了美国政治、宗教和教育中反智主义的根源。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S6.text: From the beginning of our history, says Hofstadter, our democratic and populist urges have driven us to reject anything that smells of elitism.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S6.translation: 霍夫施塔特说，从我们的历史开始，我们的民主和民粹主义冲动就驱使我们拒绝任何带有精英主义味道的东西。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S7.text: Practicality, common sense, and native intelligence have been considered more noble qualities than anything you could learn from a book.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P2-S7.translation: 实用性、常识和天生的智慧被认为比从书本上学到的任何东西都更高尚。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S1.text: Ralph Waldo Emerson and other Transcendentalist philosophers thought schooling and rigorous book learning put unnatural restraints on children: "We are shut up in schools and college recitation rooms for 10 or 15 years and come out at last with a bellyful of words and do not know a thing." Mark Twain's Huckleberry Finn exemplified American anti-intellectualism.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生和其他超验主义哲学家认为学校教育和严格的书本学习对孩子们施加了不自然的限制：“我们被关在学校和大学的背诵室里10年或15年，最后出来时却满腹言语，一无所知。”马克·吐温的《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》是美国反智主义的典范。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S2.text: Its hero avoids being civilized—going to school and learning to read—so he can preserve his innate goodness.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 它的英雄避免文明——上学和学习阅读——这样他就可以保留他与生俱来的善良。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S3.text: Intellect, according to Hofstadter, is different from native intelligence, a quality we reluctantly admire.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S3.translation: 霍夫施塔特认为，智力不同于与生俱来的智力，后者是我们不情愿地钦佩的品质。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S4.text: Intellect is the critical, creative, and contemplative side of the mind.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S4.translation: 智力是心灵的批判性、创造性和沉思性的一面。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S5.text: Intelligence seeks to grasp, manipulate, re-order, and adjust, while intellect examines, ponders, wonders, theorizes, criticizes, and imagines.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S5.translation: 智力寻求把握、操纵、重新排序和调整，而智力则检查、思考、思考、理论、批评和想象。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S6.text: School remains a place where intellect is mistrusted.
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S6.translation: 学校仍然是一个智力不被信任的地方。

ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S7.text: Hofstadter says our country's educational system is in the grips of people who "joyfully and militantly proclaim their hostility to intellect and their eagerness to identify with children who show the least intellectual promise."
ky-en1-2004-r-t4#P3-S7.translation: 霍夫施塔特说，我们国家的教育体系掌握在那些“快乐而激进地宣称对智力怀有敌意并渴望认同最没有智力潜力的孩子”的人手中。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S1.text: Everybody loves a fat pay rise.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 每个人都喜欢大幅加薪。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S2.text: Yet pleasure at your own can vanish if you learn that a colleague has been given a bigger one.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 然而，如果你得知同事得到了更大的礼物，你自己的快乐就会消失。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S3.text: Indeed, if he has a reputation for slacking, you might even be outraged.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S3.translation: 事实上，如果他有偷懒的名声，你甚至可能会感到愤怒。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S4.text: Such behaviour is regarded as "all too human", with the underlying assumption that other animals would not be capable of this finely developed sense of grievance.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S4.translation: 这种行为被认为“太人性化了”，其基本假设是其他动物不具备这种精细发展的不满感。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S5.text: But a study by Sarah Brosnan and Frans de Waal of Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia, which has just been published in Nature, suggests that it is all too monkey, as well.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S5.translation: 但佐治亚州亚特兰大埃默里大学的莎拉·布罗斯南和弗兰斯·德瓦尔刚刚在《自然》杂志上发表的一项研究表明，这也太像猴子了。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S6.text: The researchers studied the behaviour of female brown capuchin monkeys.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P1-S6.translation: 研究人员研究了雌性棕色卷尾猴的行为。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S1.text: They are good-natured, co-operative creatures, and they share their food readily.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 它们是性情善良、善于合作的生物，并且乐于分享食物。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S2.text: Above all, like their female human counterparts, they tend to pay much closer attention to the value of "goods and services" than males.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: 最重要的是，与女性人类同行一样，她们往往比男性更关注“商品和服务”的价值。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S3.text: Such characteristics make them perfect candidates for Dr. Brosnan's and Dr. de Waal's study.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S3.translation: 这些特征使它们成为布罗斯南博士和德瓦尔博士研究的完美候选者。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S4.text: The researchers spent two years teaching their monkeys to exchange tokens for food.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S4.translation: 研究人员花了两年时间教猴子用代币交换食物。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S5.text: Normally, the monkeys were happy enough to exchange pieces of rock for slices of cucumber.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S5.translation: 通常情况下，猴子很乐意用石头换黄瓜片。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S6.text: However, when two monkeys were placed in separate but adjoining chambers, so that each could observe what the other was getting in return for its rock, their behaviour became markedly different.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S6.translation: 然而，当两只猴子被放置在单独但相邻的房间中，以便每只猴子都可以观察另一只猴子从石头中得到什么回报时，它们的行为变得明显不同。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S7.text: In the world of capuchins grapes are luxury goods (and much preferable to cucumbers).
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P2-S7.translation: 在卷尾猴的世界里，葡萄是奢侈品（而且比黄瓜更受欢迎）。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S1.text: So when one monkey was handed a grape in exchange for her token, the second was reluctant to hand hers over for a mere piece of cucumber.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 因此，当一只猴子被递上一颗葡萄来换取她的代币时，第二只猴子却不愿意仅仅为了一块黄瓜而交出她的葡萄。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S2.text: And if one received a grape without having to provide her token in exchange at all, the other either tossed her own token at the researcher or out of the chamber, or refused to accept the slice of cucumber.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 如果一个人在根本不需要提供代币作为交换的情况下收到了一颗葡萄，另一个人要么把自己的代币扔给研究人员，要么扔出房间，或者拒绝接受这片黄瓜。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S3.text: Indeed, the mere presence of a grape in the other chamber (without an actual monkey to eat it) was enough to induce resentment in a female capuchin.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 事实上，仅仅在另一个房间里出现一颗葡萄（没有真正的猴子来吃它）就足以引起雌性卷尾猴的不满。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S4.text: The researchers suggest that capuchin monkeys, like humans, are guided by social emotions.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S4.translation: 研究人员认为，卷尾猴和人类一样，受到社会情绪的引导。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S5.text: In the wild, they are a co-operative, group-living species.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S5.translation: 在野外，它们是一种合作、群体生活的物种。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S6.text: Such co-operation is likely to be stable only when each animal feels it is not being cheated.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S6.translation: 只有当每只动物都感觉自己没有被欺骗时，这种合作才可能是稳定的。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S7.text: Feelings of righteous indignation, it seems, are not the preserve of people alone.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S7.translation: 看来，义愤之情不只是人们的专利。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S8.text: Refusing a lesser reward completely makes these feelings abundantly clear to other members of the group.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S8.translation: 完全拒绝较少的奖励会让团队中的其他成员清楚地感受到这些感受。

ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S9.text: However, whether such a sense of fairness evolved independently in capuchins and humans, or whether it stems from the common ancestor that the species had 35 million years ago, is, as yet, an unanswered question.
ky-en1-2005-r-t1#P3-S9.translation: 然而，这种公平感是否是卷尾猴和人类独立进化出来的，还是源于该物种3500万年前的共同祖先，目前仍是一个悬而未决的问题。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S1.text: Do you remember all those years when scientists argued that smoking would kill us but the doubters insisted that we didn't know for sure?
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 你还记得那些年来科学家们认为吸烟会杀死我们，但怀疑者坚持认为我们并不确定吗？

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S2.text: That the evidence was inconclusive, the science uncertain?
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 证据尚无定论，科学也不确定？

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S3.text: That the antismoking lobby was out to destroy our way of life and the government should stay out of the way?
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S3.translation: 反吸烟游说团体的目的是破坏我们的生活方式，而政府应该袖手旁观？

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S4.text: Lots of Americans bought that nonsense, and over three decades, some 10 million smokers went to early graves.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S4.translation: 很多美国人都相信这种胡言乱语，三十年来，大约有 1000 万烟民早逝。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S5.text: There are upsetting parallels today, as scientists in one wave after another try to awaken us to the growing threat of global warming.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S5.translation: 今天，有一些令人不安的相似之处，科学家们一波又一波地试图唤醒我们认识到全球变暖日益严重的威胁。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S6.text: The latest was a panel from the National Academy of Sciences, enlisted by the White House, to tell us that the Earth's atmosphere is definitely warming and that the problem is largely man-made.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P1-S6.translation: 最新的消息是由白宫聘请的美国国家科学院的一个小组告诉我们，地球大气层肯定正在变暖，而这个问题很大程度上是人为造成的。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S1.text: The clear message is that we should get moving to protect ourselves.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 明确的信息是我们应该采取行动保护自己。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S2.text: The president of the National Academy, Bruce Alberts, added this key point in the preface to the panel's report: "Science never has all the answers.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 美国国家科学院院长布鲁斯·艾伯茨在专家组报告的序言中补充了这一要点：“科学永远无法给出所有答案。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S3.text: But science does provide us with the best available guide to the future, and it is critical that our nation and the world base important policies on the best judgments that science can provide concerning the future consequences of present actions." Just as on smoking, voices now come from many quarters insisting that the science about global warming is incomplete, that it's OK to keep pouring fumes into the air until we know for sure.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S3.translation: 但科学确实为我们提供了未来最好的指南，至关重要的是，我们的国家和世界的重要政策必须建立在科学能够对当前行动的未来后果提供的最佳判断的基础上。”就像吸烟一样，现在来自许多方面的声音坚持认为有关全球变暖的科学是不完整的，在我们确定之前可以继续向空气中排放烟雾。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S4.text: This is a dangerous game: by the time 100 percent of the evidence is in, it may be too late.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S4.translation: 这是一场危险的游戏：当 100% 的证据到位时，可能已经太晚了。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S5.text: With the risks obvious and growing, prudent people would take out an insurance policy now.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S5.translation: 随着风险的明显和不断增加，谨慎的人现在会购买保险。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S6.text: Fortunately, the White House is starting to pay attention.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P2-S6.translation: 幸运的是，白宫已经开始关注。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S1.text: But it's obvious that a majority of the president's advisers still don't take global warming seriously.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 但显然，大多数总统顾问仍然没有认真对待全球变暖问题。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S2.text: Instead of a plan of action, they continue to press for more research—a classic case of "paralysis by analysis".
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 他们没有制定行动计划，而是继续敦促进行更多研究——这是“分析瘫痪”的典型案例。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S3.text: To serve as responsible stewards of the planet, we must press forward on deeper atmospheric and oceanic research.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S3.translation: 为了成为地球的负责任的管理者，我们必须推进更深入的大气和海洋研究。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S5.text: If the Administration won't take the legislative initiative, Congress should help to begin fashioning conservation measures.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S5.translation: 如果政府不采取立法举措，国会应该帮助开始制定保护措施。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S6.text: A bill by Democratic Senator Robert Byrd of West Virginia, which would offer financial incentives for private industry, is a promising start.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S6.translation: 西弗吉尼亚州民主党参议员罗伯特·伯德提出的一项法案将为私营企业提供财政激励，这是一个充满希望的开始。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S7.text: Many see that the country is getting ready to build lots of new power plants to meet our energy needs.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S7.translation: 许多人看到该国正准备建造大量新发电厂以满足我们的能源需求。

ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S8.text: If we are ever going to protect the atmosphere, it is crucial that those new plants be environmentally sound.
ky-en1-2005-r-t2#P3-S8.translation: 如果我们想要保护大气层，那么这些新工厂必须对环境无害，这一点至关重要。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S1.text: Of all the components of a good night's sleep, dreams seem to be least within our control.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 在良好睡眠的所有组成部分中，梦似乎是我们最无法控制的。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S2.text: In dreams, a window opens into a world where logic is suspended and dead people speak.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 在梦中，一扇窗户打开，通向一个逻辑被悬置、死人说话的世界。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S3.text: A century ago, Freud formulated his revolutionary theory that dreams were the disguised shadows of our unconscious desires and fears; by the late 1970s, neurologists had switched to thinking of them as just "mental noise"—the random byproducts of the neural-repair work that goes on during sleep.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S3.translation: 一个世纪前，弗洛伊德提出了他的革命性理论，即梦是我们无意识欲望和恐惧的伪装阴影；梦是我们无意识欲望和恐惧的伪装阴影。到了 20 世纪 70 年代末，神经学家开始将它们视为“精神噪音”——睡眠期间进行的神经修复工作的随机副产品。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S4.text: Now researchers suspect that dreams are part of the mind's emotional thermostat, regulating moods while the brain is "off-line." And one leading authority says that these intensely powerful mental events can be not only harnessed but actually brought under conscious control, to help us sleep and feel better.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S4.translation: 现在，研究人员怀疑，梦是大脑情绪恒温器的一部分，可以在大脑“离线”时调节情绪。一位权威人士表示，这些极其强大的心理事件不仅可以被利用，而且实际上可以被置于有意识的控制之下，以帮助我们睡眠和感觉更好。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S5.text: "It's your dream," says Rosalind Cartwright, chair of psychology at Chicago's Medical Center.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S5.translation: “这是你的梦想，”芝加哥医学中心心理学主任罗莎琳德·卡特赖特说。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S6.text: "If you don't like it, change it." Evidence from brain imaging supports this view.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S6.translation: “如果你不喜欢它，就改变它。”来自大脑成像的证据支持了这一观点。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S7.text: The brain is as active during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep – when most vivid dreams occur—as it is when fully awake, says Dr. Eric Nofzinger at the University of Pittsburgh.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P1-S7.translation: 匹兹堡大学的埃里克·诺夫辛格博士说，在快速眼动睡眠期间（最生动的梦发生时），大脑与完全清醒时一样活跃。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S1.text: But not all parts of the brain are equally involved; the limbic system (the "emotional brain") is especially active, while the prefrontal cortex (the center of intellect and reasoning) is relatively quiet.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 但并非大脑的所有部分都同样参与其中。边缘系统（“情感脑”）特别活跃，而前额叶皮层（智力和推理中心）相对安静。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S2.text: "We wake up from dreams happy or depressed, and those feelings can stay with us all day." says Stanford sleep researcher Dr. William Dement.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: “我们从快乐或沮丧的梦中醒来，这些感觉会伴随我们一整天。”斯坦福大学睡眠研究员威廉·德门特博士说。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S3.text: The link between dreams and emotions shows up among the patients in Cartwright's clinic.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S3.translation: 梦和情绪之间的联系在卡特赖特诊所的病人身上显现出来。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S4.text: Most people seem to have more bad dreams early in the night, progressing toward happier ones before awakening, suggesting that they are working through negative feelings generated during the day.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S4.translation: 大多数人似乎在深夜会做更多的噩梦，在醒来之前会做一些更快乐的梦，这表明他们正在努力克服白天产生的负面情绪。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S5.text: Because our conscious mind is occupied with daily life we don't always think about the emotional significance of the day's events—until, it appears, we begin to dream.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S5.translation: 因为我们的意识思维被日常生活占据，所以我们并不总是思考当天事件的情感意义——直到我们开始做梦。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S6.text: And this process need not be left to the unconscious.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S6.translation: 这个过程不需要留给无意识。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S7.text: Cartwright believes one can exercise conscious control over recurring bad dreams.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P2-S7.translation: 卡特赖特相信，人们可以有意识地控制反复出现的噩梦。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S1.text: As soon as you awaken, identify what is upsetting about the dream.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 醒来后，立即找出梦中令人不安的原因。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S2.text: Visualize how you would like it to end instead; the next time it occurs, try to wake up just enough to control its course.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 想象一下你希望它如何结束；下次发生这种情况时，尝试醒来足以控制其进程。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S3.text: With much practice people can learn to, literally, do it in their sleep.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S3.translation: 通过大量练习，人们实际上可以学会在睡梦中做到这一点。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S4.text: At the end of the day, there's probably little reason to pay attention to our dreams at all unless they keep us from sleeping or "we wake up in a panic," Cartwright says.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S4.translation: 卡特赖特说，归根结底，我们可能根本没有理由去关注我们的梦，除非它们让我们无法入睡或“我们在惊慌中醒来”。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S5.text: Terrorism, economic uncertainties and general feelings of insecurity have increased people's anxiety.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S5.translation: 恐怖主义、经济不确定性和普遍的不安全感加剧了人们的焦虑。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S6.text: Those suffering from persistent nightmares should seek help from a therapist.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S6.translation: 那些经常做噩梦的人应该寻求治疗师的帮助。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S7.text: For the rest of us, the brain has its ways of working through bad feelings.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S7.translation: 对于我们其他人来说，大脑有其处理不良情绪的方式。

ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S8.text: Sleep—or rather dream—on it and you'll feel better in the morning.
ky-en1-2005-r-t3#P3-S8.translation: 睡觉——或者更确切地说做梦——早上你会感觉更好。

ky-en1-2005-r-t4#P1-S1.text: Americans no longer expect public figures, whether in speech or in writing, to command the English language with skill and gift.
ky-en1-2005-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 美国人不再期望公众人物，无论是在演讲还是写作中，都能以技巧和天赋掌握英语。

ky-en1-2005-r-t4#P1-S2.text: Nor do they aspire to such command themselves.
ky-en1-2005-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 他们自己也不渴望获得这样的命令。
