Van Oosten calls those chemicals "sunscreens" because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers. She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases.
ky-en1-2022-r-t1#P5-S1.translation: 于是，范奥斯滕及其同事竭尽全力抢救保护吉拉尔迪的这批雕塑。他们向部分展品中渗透注入了稳定固化化学制剂。范奥斯滕将这些制剂形象地称为“防晒剂”（sunscreens），因为其核心目标正是为了防止进一步的光照破坏并重新修复加固磨损的高分子纤维。令她由衷自豪的是，已有若干件雕塑得以重新面向公众公开展出，尽管有时必须陈列在坚固的透明保护罩之下。

ky-en1-2022-r-t1#P6-S1.text: Despite success stories like Van Oosten's, preservation of plastics will likely get harder. Old objects continue to deteriorate. Worse, biodegradable plastics, designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.
ky-en1-2022-r-t1#P6-S1.translation: 尽管有范奥斯滕这样振奋人心的成功案例，但塑料文物的保护工作在未来极可能会变得愈发艰难与充满严峻挑战（preservation of plastics will get harder / challenging）。老旧塑料藏品在持续不断地加速恶化；更糟糕的是，那些在设计初衷上就专门为了快速分解瓦解而生的“可生物降解塑料”，如今在日常生活中正变得越来越普遍普遍寻常。

ky-en1-2022-r-t1#P7-S1.text: And more is at stake here than individual objects. Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—after examining artifacts in museums.
ky-en1-2022-r-t1#P7-S1.translation: 而这里所关乎的利害，远远超越了单个具体的塑料器物本身。新里斯本大学科技学院文物保护与修复学助理教授乔安娜·利亚·费雷拉深刻指出：考古学家们当年正是通过细致检视博物馆中的各种出土文物，才首次确立定义了人类历史上的伟大物质时代——石器时代、铁器时代等等。

ky-en1-2022-r-t1#P7-S2.text: We now live in an age of plastic, she says, "and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve...will have a strong impact on how in the future we'll be seen."
ky-en1-2022-r-t1#P7-S2.translation: 我们如今正生活在一个崭新的‘塑料时代’，她表示，“而我们今天决定收集什么、决定妥善保护保存什么……必将对未来千百年后的后人如何看待审视我们这个时代，产生深远且决定性的历史影响（profound historical significance / how in the future we will be seen）。”

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P1-S1.text: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 随着最新一批年轻学子纷纷提笔填写本科入学申请表并权衡各自的人生抉择，当下的确非常值得深入思考：大学学位的真正意义、宗旨与价值究竟发生了何种深刻转变，以及 Z 世代（Generation Z）在开启其第三阶段求学生涯时究竟需要审慎考量些什么（reassess necessity of college education）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P1-S1.text: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 随着最新一批年轻学子纷纷提笔填写本科入学申请表并权衡各自的人生抉择，当下的确非常值得深入思考：大学学位的真正意义、宗旨与价值究竟发生了何种深刻转变，以及 Z 世代（Generation Z）在开启其第三阶段求学生涯时究竟需要审慎考量些什么（reassess necessity of college education）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P2-S1.text: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued. Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 千禧一代（Millennials）曾被长辈告知：只要在学校成绩优异、拿下一张体面的大学文凭，就能一生衣食无忧、立于不败之地。然而，这一美好的承诺如今已被证明大打折扣、漏洞百出。随着大学文凭走向普及化泛滥，其含金量也随之严重贬值（devalued）；高等教育再也不是一条稳妥通畅的社会阶层上升流动通道。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Today, 28 percent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 在当今英国，高达28%的大学毕业生在从事根本不需要本科学历的低阶岗位（non-graduate roles），这一比例甚至是经合组织（OECD）国家平均水平的整整两倍（reflects the shrinking value of a degree）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Today, 28 percent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 在当今英国，高达28%的大学毕业生在从事根本不需要本科学历的低阶岗位（non-graduate roles），这一比例甚至是经合组织（OECD）国家平均水平的整整两倍（reflects the shrinking value of a degree）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P3-S1.text: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 这绝不是说攻读大学学位毫无意义，而是强调大学学位并不适合所有人；从中学教室直接迈入大学阶梯讲堂绝非唯一不可避免的必然路径，人生完全还有其他切实可行的替代选择。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P4-S1.text: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P4-S1.translation: 令人欣慰的是，有诸多迹象表明这种务实转变已经悄然发生：Z 世代正主动从千禧一代前人的挫折中汲取深刻教训，哪怕许多家长和教师的思想观念依然顽固禁锢在非拿文凭不可的旧思维定式之中。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P4-S2.text: Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P4-S2.translation: 广大雇主早已敏锐洞察到了直接录用中学毕业生（school leavers）的显著优势——事实证明，他们往往比大学毕业生更具敬业投入度与企业忠诚度；许多雇主同样深刻体会到了对特定岗位彻底取消文凭硬性要求的巨大好处（employers taking realistic attitude to degrees）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P5-S1.text: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 percent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P5-S1.translation: 对于那些确实将攻读学位视作理想道路的人而言，请清醒意识到这很可能只是你未来众多学位的起点。在这个充斥着普通通才的时代，唯有掌握极其深度的专门知识或技能才能获得丰厚回报（further studies in a specific field）。如今研究生的平均收入比普通本科生高出整整40%；当身边的大学本科生越来越泛滥时，拥有两张文凭才真正合乎情理。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P6-S1.text: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly up-skilling throughout their career to stay employable. It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P6-S1.translation: Z 世代绝不可能在18岁或21岁大学毕业时就宣告教育的彻底终结；为了终身保持核心就业竞争力，他们将必须在整个职业生涯中持续不断地进行技能迭代升级（constantly up-skilling / lifelong learning）。据权威预测，出于科技变革重压、个人价值实现以及对多元体验的渴望，这一代人一生中平均将为17家不同的雇主效力，并跨界涉足5种完全不同的职业。贯穿一生的学习教育——而远非仅仅局限于校园内所习得的书本知识——将成为 Z 世代职业人生轨迹的绝对核心支柱（Lifelong learning will define them）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P7-S1.text: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: "I am a geographer" or "I am a classicist". Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.
ky-en1-2022-r-t2#P7-S1.translation: 老一辈人谈起自己的大学文凭时，往往喜欢使用第一人称现在时：“我是一名地理学者”或“我是一名古典学家”。然而他们的年轻儿女们绝不会再说出这般言语——仿佛他们早已深切洞悉：大学文凭再也无法以同样僵化的方式去定义他们绚烂广阔的人生轨迹。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P1-S1.text: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun. These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experiences of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 启迪心智、充满挑战、激发灵感、妙趣横生。这些词汇正是《自然》（Nature）杂志读者在关于艺术家与科研学者跨界合作的一系列文章中，用来形容他们亲身参与“艺术-科学跨界合作”体验时所给出的热烈评价。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P1-S2.text: Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists, and almost all said they would consider doing so in the future.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 在参与随附问卷调查的约350名受访者中，有近40%的人明确表示他们曾与艺术家展开过实质性跨界合作，且几乎所有受访者都坚决表示未来会继续考虑进行此类合作（received favourable responses）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P2-S1.text: Such an encouraging result is not surprising. Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences. "Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning," one respondent said.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 如此令人鼓舞的调查结果丝毫不足为奇。当今科学家正日益主动寻求视觉艺术家的跨界支持，以帮助他们将深奥晦涩的科研成果传播传递给全新的大众受众。“艺术家能够帮助科学家触达更加广阔的受众群体，并建立起深化理解认知的强烈情感共鸣连接，”一位受访者如是说。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P3-S1.text: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the senses came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 关于艺术家与科学家如何携手震撼人类感官的一个绝佳范例，便发生在上个月悉尼交响乐团对安东尼奥·韦瓦第经典名作《四季》所进行的震撼重构版演绎之中（reworked version of The Four Seasons）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P3-S1.text: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the senses came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 关于艺术家与科学家如何携手震撼人类感官的一个绝佳范例，便发生在上个月悉尼交响乐团对安东尼奥·韦瓦第经典名作《四季》所进行的震撼重构版演绎之中（reworked version of The Four Seasons）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P3-S2.text: They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University's Climate Change Communication Research Hub. The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P3-S2.translation: 他们通过向每个季节注入由莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的最新气候预测科研数据，重新解构并重塑了这部有着300年历史的经典乐谱。这场演出在英国格拉斯哥联合国气候变化大会召开前夕，发出了一记极富创造力与感染力的跨界行动号召（art offer audiences easy access to science）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P4-S1.text: But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street. Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll; however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements. Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P4-S1.translation: 然而，真正的跨界伙伴关系必须是一条互惠互利的“双向车道”（two-way street）。参与《自然》调查的艺术家数量少于科学家；然而若干受访者尖锐指出：艺术家的角色绝不能被狭隘地贬低为仅仅协助科学家满足其科研成果的大众传播需求（role may be underestimated），他们的艺术创作更不应仅仅被视作供科学家解剖研究的单向客体。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P4-S2.text: The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other's work. Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P4-S2.translation: 当科学家与艺术家在项目中拥有共同的利益关切、能够共同主导方案设计并能够相互审视批判彼此的工作时，这种跨界联盟才会爆发出最巨大的非凡价值。这种深度融合模式既能直接激发全新的前沿科学研究，又能孕育出震撼人心的伟大艺术力作。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P5-S1.text: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture. The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the "visual studies" in the name. Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P5-S1.translation: 半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院（MIT）正式创立了“高级视觉研究中心”（CAVS），以深入探索科技在人类文化中所扮演的角色。创始人们深谋远虑地将项目聚焦于“光”这一核心主题——这也正是其名称中“视觉研究”的由头。光线是艺术家与科学家共同怀有浓厚兴趣的交汇点，因而构成了跨界深度合作的坚实基石（exemplified valuable art-science alliances）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P5-S2.text: As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P5-S2.translation: 随着科学技术的飞速演进并细分为更多子学科，该中心同时也在满怀憧憬地眺望一个全新的未来：届时顶尖的科研学者能够同时身兼艺术家、作家与诗人，反之亦然。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P6-S1.text: Nature's poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P6-S1.translation: 《自然》杂志的民调结果表明，这种科艺融合的大趋势比以往任何时候都更加强劲；但要想让跨界合作真正取得实效，双方都必须投入充裕时间，并由衷拥抱过程中的意料之外与严峻挑战。

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P6-S1.text: Nature's poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge.

ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P6-S2.text: The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other. Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.
ky-en1-2022-r-t3#P6-S2.translation: 艺术与科学跨界联手的辐射范围，必须远远超越单纯作为科研成果传播辅助工具的狭隘功利目的（reach needs to go beyond research communication / should do more than communicating science），参与各方绝不能陷入对彼此贴标签、搞刻板印象的狭隘陷阱之中。无论是艺术家还是科学家，本质上都深深沉浸在探索发现与创造发明的崇高殿堂之中，而勇于挑战和相互批判审视，同样是双方共同拥有的核心灵魂所在！

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P1-S1.text: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause. Instead, dismissals must be justified. Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 新西兰《2000年雇佣关系法》（ERA）中的个人申诉条款，严禁雇主在缺乏正当充分理由的情况下擅自解雇员工。相反，一切解雇决定都必须证明具有正当合法性（justified），雇主必须同时出示正当解雇事由并严格遵循程序公正的法定流程。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P1-S1.text: The personal grievance provisions of New Zealand's Employment Relations Act 2000 (ERA) prevent an employer from firing an employee without good cause. Instead, dismissals must be justified. Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 新西兰《2000年雇佣关系法》（ERA）中的个人申诉条款，严禁雇主在缺乏正当充分理由的情况下擅自解雇员工。相反，一切解雇决定都必须证明具有正当合法性（justified），雇主必须同时出示正当解雇事由并严格遵循程序公正的法定流程。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P2-S1.text: "Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from unjustified dismissals". The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management. Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: “个人申诉程序的设立初衷，正是为了保护广大普通工人的饭碗工作免遭无理专断解雇的侵害（protect the rights of ordinary workers）。”其立法前提假设在于：传统的普通合同法在抵御管理层武断专横行径方面，严重缺乏对劳动者的充分制度保障。老板仅仅给出一份合同通知就能随意开除员工的时代早已一去不复返。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P3-S1.text: But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives. As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 然而，当这些保护性条款被无差别地适用于高薪管理人员与企业高管时，却给商业企业带来了难以承受的严重困境。正如无数董事会成员和企业主所痛切证明的那样：束缚限制企业解雇那些业绩拙劣却拿着高薪的管理人员，实乃掣肘提升企业生产力与整体经营业绩的致命“急刹车手刹”（hinder business development / handbrake on boosting performance）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P3-S2.text: The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure. Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them. Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: C级平庸经理人与A级卓越经理人之间的能力鸿沟，很可能直接决定了一家企业的商业成败，直接决定了广大普通员工是保住饭碗还是彻底失业。然而在现行法律下，管理者的平庸无能却再也不足以构成正当合法的解雇理由。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P4-S1.text: Consequently and paradoxically laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P4-S1.translation: 结果令人啼笑皆非且极其矛盾悖论的是：原本为了保护普通工人就业而制定的法律，如今却反过来将这些工人的饭碗置于巨大的失业风险之中。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P4-S1.text: Consequently and paradoxically laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P4-S1.translation: 结果令人啼笑皆非且极其矛盾悖论的是：原本为了保护普通工人就业而制定的法律，如今却反过来将这些工人的饭碗置于巨大的失业风险之中。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P4-S2.text: If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing underperforming managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages. Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P4-S2.translation: 即便不直接危及就业，只要雇佣保护法在客观上束缚了企业主解雇低效无能管理人员的权利，这些法律就会直接遏制企业生产力的提升，并进而直接压低压制广大工人的薪酬工资。事实上，在新西兰生产力委员会2014年发布的权威报告《新西兰生产力悖论之国际透视》中，该委员会明确将“管理人员能力素质低下”单列为导致该国长期生产力增长极其低迷疲软的罪魁祸首（supports dismissing poorly performing managers）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P5-S1.text: Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures. Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P5-S1.translation: 即便是高薪管理人员自身，也无法对 ERA 不当解雇程序所造成的附带伤害彻底免疫。因为雇佣保护法使得开除一名员工的法律经济成本变得极其昂贵，雇主在招聘新员工时因而变得空前谨慎保守。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P5-S2.text: This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment. And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.
ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P5-S2.translation: 这使得处于边缘水平的经理人更加难以找到工作；而且，由于企业必须全盘独自承担用人安排一旦出错所带来的沉重法律包袱，企业索性向全体员工支付更低的薪水（firms pay staff less / employees suffer from salary cuts）。

ky-en1-2022-r-t4#P5-S3.text: Society also suffers from excessive employment protections. Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being.

ky-en1-2023-r-t1#P5-S1.text: A study last year by the National Center for Science Education, a non-profit group of scientists and teachers, looking at how state public schools across the country address climate change in science classes, gave barely half of US states a grade B+ or higher.

ky-en1-2023-r-t1#P6-S1.translation: 该中心副主任格伦·布兰奇严肃告诫道：在一个将教育决策权深度下放至地方学区委员会的国家里，制定州一级的科学标准仅仅是一个影响力极其有限的参考基准（have limited influence）。即使某个州在其州级科学课程标准上被评为优秀生，“这也绝不意味着这些内容真正在一线课堂上得到了教授”，他表示。

ky-en1-2023-r-t2#P3-S2.text: Without enough affordable housing in southern New Hampshire towns, "employers are having a hard time attracting employees, and workers are having a hard time finding a place to live," Taylor said.

"A lot of workers are servicing the tourist industry, and the tourism industry is serviced by those people coming in short term," Castle said, "and so it's a cyclical effect."
ky-en1-2023-r-t2#P4-S1.translation: 然而，当地房地产经纪人协会首席执行官瑞安·卡斯尔针锋相对地指出，短租同样为大量外来游客提供了不可或缺的住宿支持。“大量本地劳工都在为蓬勃发展的旅游业服务，而旅游业本身又依赖于这些短期涌入的游客来支撑维系，”卡斯尔表示，“因此这完全是一个相互依存的良性循环效应。”

"I think individuals being able to rent out their second home is a good thing. If it's their vacation home anyway, and it's just empty, why can't you make money off it?" Horn said.
ky-en1-2023-r-t2#P5-S1.translation: 可负担住房政策权威专家凯伦·霍恩指出，短租本身并非问题的根本死结症结所在。“我认为普通个人能够把自己的第二套闲置住房出租完全是一件大好事。如果那本来就是他们的度假屋且常年空置，为什么不能借此赚点额外收入呢？”霍恩表示。

ky-en1-2023-r-t2#P5-S2.text: Issues arise, however, when developers attempt to create large-scale short-term rental facilities—de facto hotels—to bypass taxes and regulations. "I think the question is, shouldn't a developer who's really building a hotel, but disguising it as not a hotel, be treated and taxed and regulated like a hotel?" Horn said.
ky-en1-2023-r-t2#P5-S2.translation: 然而，真正的致命问题在于：当投机开发商企图通过打造大规模短租设施——即实质上的“事实酒店”（de facto hotels）——来肆意规避绕开合法税收与监管法规时，乱象便丛生而起（necessity to stop developers from evading taxes）。“我认为核心问题在于：一个明明在干着盖酒店勾当、却巧妙将其伪装成普通民宅以避税的开发商，难道不应当像正规酒店一样接受同等标准的严密监管和征税吗？”霍恩质问道。

ky-en1-2023-r-t2#P6-S1.text: At the end of 2018, Governor Charlie Baker of Massachusetts signed a bill to rein in those potential investor-buyers. The bill requires every rental host to register with the state, mandates they carry insurance, and opens the potential for local taxes on top of a new state levy. Boston took things even further, requiring renters to register with the city's Inspectional Services Department.
ky-en1-2023-r-t2#P6-S1.translation: 2018年底，马萨诸塞州州长查理·贝克正式签署了一项法案以遏制那些潜在的短租投资客买家。该法案强制要求每一位短租房东必须向州政府实名登记备案，强制要求其购买特定保险，并在全新州级税收之上为地方政府加征市政税打开了大门。波士顿市更是将监管推向极致，强制要求所有出租方必须向市检查服务局登记备案。

ky-en1-2023-r-t3#P2-S2.text: The trade magazine The Bookseller reported that Waterstones branch managers were being told to remove PRH books from prominent areas such as tables, display spaces and windows, and were "quietly retiring them to their relevant sections".

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P1-S2.text: The scientific community measures the quality of those papers in a number of ways, including the perceived quality of the journal (as reflected by the title's impact factor) and the number of citations a specific paper accumulates.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 科学共同体通过多种维度来衡量这些论文的学术质量，包括期刊自身的公认档次（具体体现为期刊影响因子）以及某篇具体论文所累积的被引用次数（citations）。

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P1-S3.text: The careers of scientists and the reputation of their institutions depend on the number and prestige of the papers they produce, but even more so on the citations attracted by these papers.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P1-S3.translation: 科学家的个人学术职业生涯（careers of scientists）以及其所属科研机构的声誉，不仅取决于他们所产出论文的数量与声望，更是极其深刻地取决于这些论文被同行引用的频繁程度与引用次数（how many times their papers are cited / citations attracted by papers）！

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P2-S1.text: Citation cartels, where journals, authors, and institutions conspire to inflate citation numbers, have existed for a long time. In 2016, researchers developed an algorithm to recognize suspicious citation patterns, including groups of authors that disproportionately cite one another and groups of journals that cite each other frequently to increase the impact factors of their publications.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 期刊、作者与机构三方暗中串通以恶意虚增引文数量的所谓“引用卡特尔”（Citation cartels），在学术界早已由来已久。早在2016年，科研人员就开发出了一种专门识别可疑引用模式的算法，包括不成比例相互引用的作者群伙，以及为了拉抬出版物影响因子而频繁互引的期刊集团联盟。

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P2-S2.text: Recently, another expression of this predatory behavior has emerged: so-called support service consultancies that provide language and other editorial support to individual authors and to journals sometimes advise contributors to add a number of citations to their articles.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 而最近，这种掠夺性学术不端行为又滋生出了全新的表现形式：那些表面上向独立作者和期刊提供语言润色及编辑支持的所谓“学术支持服务咨询机构”（support service consultancies），有时竟公然诱导或强行要求投稿作者在其文章中强行添加大量特定的额外引用文献（ask authors to include extra citations / advise contributors to add citations）！

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P3-S1.text: The advent of electronic publishing and authors' need to find outlets for their papers resulted in thousands of new journals. The birth of predatory journals wasn't far behind.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 电子数字出版时代的全面降临以及广大作者迫切寻找发文出路的现实需求，直接催生了数以千计的崭新学术期刊；而专门牟利的“掠夺性期刊”的诞生也紧随其后、应运而生。

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P3-S2.text: These journals can act as milk cows where every single article in an issue may cite a specific paper or a series of papers. In some instances, there is absolutely no relationship between the content of the article and the citations. The peculiar part is that the journal that the editor is supposedly working for is not profiting at all—it is just providing citations to other journals. Such practices can lead an article to accrue more than 150 citations in the same year that it was published.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 这些期刊充当着源源不断提供引用的“产奶母牛”（milk cows）——一期刊物中的每一篇论文可能全部都会强行引用某一篇特定论文或某一系列指定论文（boost citation counts for certain authors）。在某些极端荒谬案例中，文章本身的实际学术内容与强加的被引文献之间根本不存在哪怕半点逻辑关联。最诡异的地方在于，编辑名义上效力的这本期刊自身根本捞不到任何直接好处——它纯粹只是在单向为其他期刊或作者疯狂‘供奶式’输送引文！这种恶劣操纵甚至能让某篇特定论文在见刊当年就疯狂暴涨累积超过150次被引用！

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P4-S1.text: How insidious is this type of citation manipulation? In one example, an individual—acting as author, editor, and consultant—was able to use at least 15 journals as citation providers to articles published by five scientists at three universities.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P4-S1.translation: 这种引文操纵黑产究竟有多么隐蔽阴险猖獗？在一个触目惊心的真实案例中，某个集作者、编辑与咨询顾问于一身的操盘人，竟然成功利用至少15本学术期刊作为“引文供体”，专门为分布在三所高校的五位科学家所发表的论文疯狂注水刷引用！

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P4-S2.text: The problem is rampant in Scopus, a citation database, which includes a high number of the new "international" journals. In fact, a listing in Scopus seems to be a criterion to be targeted in this type of citation manipulation.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P4-S2.translation: 这一毒瘤现象在国际权威引文数据库 Scopus 中极其泛滥猖獗——该数据库收录了海量此类新型所谓“国际期刊”。事实上，只要被 Scopus 数据库收录索引，似乎就成为了被此类引文操纵集团精准锁定的目标衡量标准。

ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P5-S2.text: And for authors who wish to steer clear of citation cartel activities: when an editor, a reviewer, or a support service asks you to add inappropriate references, do not oblige and do report the request to the journal.
ky-en1-2023-r-t4#P5-S2.translation: 而对于那些渴望洁身自好、远离引文卡特尔泥潭的广大正直学者而言：一旦有任何期刊编辑、审稿人或润色服务机构要求你强行添加不恰当的无关参考文献，切切不可盲从顺从，并且必须坚决向期刊官方实名举报揭露其学术不端行径（do not oblige and do report / Reveal their misconduct）！

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P1-S1.text: Nearly 2000 years ago, as the Romans began to pull out of Scotland, they left behind a curious treasure: 10 tons of nails, nearly a million of the things.

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P1-S2.text: The nail hoard was discovered in 1960 in a four-metre-deep pit covered by two metres of gravel.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 这处浩大的铁钉窖藏于1960年被考古发现，深埋在一个深达四米、上方覆盖着整整两米厚砾石的隐秘深坑之中。

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P2-S1.text: Why had the Romans buried a million nails? The likely explanation is that the withdrawal was rushed, and they didn't want the local Caledonians getting their hands on 10 tons of weapons grade iron. The Romans buried the nails so deep that they would not be discovered for almost two millennia.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 罗马人究竟为何要深埋这一百万枚铁钉？最合情合理的解释是：当时撤退行动极其仓促紧急，而他们绝不希望当地的喀里多尼亚土著人染指获取这10吨宝贵的武器级优质铁原料（hiding them from locals / didn't want local Caledonians getting their hands on iron）。罗马人将铁钉埋得如此之深，以至于在长达近两千年的漫长岁月里都未曾被世人发觉。

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P3-S2.text: As Roma Agrawal explains in her new delightful book Nuts and Bolts, early 17th-century Virginians would sometimes burn down their homes if they were planning to relocate. This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes.

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 正如萝玛·阿格拉瓦尔在其令人赞叹的新作《螺母与螺栓》中所阐述的那样：17世纪初的弗吉尼亚早期殖民者在计划搬迁定居点时，有时甚至会故意纵火将自己的整座房屋付之一炬——这完全是为了回收那些价值连城的宝贵铁钉，在灰烬中筛出铁钉后便能重新循环利用。

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P3-S3.text: The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the simple-seeming technology was.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P3-S3.translation: 一个人竟然会仅仅为了回收铁钉而不惜烧毁一整栋房屋，这种不可思议的做法深刻印证了这项表面看似简单的制钉技术在当年是多么罕见稀缺、成本高昂且弥足珍贵（show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time）！

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P4-S1.text: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P4-S1.translation: 正如经济学家丹尼尔·西歇尔在一篇学术论文中所指出的那样，从18世纪末到20世纪中叶，铁钉的实际价格足足暴跌了整整90%。

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P4-S1.text: The price of nails fell by 90% between the late 1700s and mid-1900s, as economist Daniel Sichel points out in a research paper.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P4-S1.translation: 正如经济学家丹尼尔·西歇尔在一篇学术论文中所指出的那样，从18世纪末到20世纪中叶，铁钉的实际价格足足暴跌了整整90%。

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P4-S2.text: According to Sichel, although the falling price of nails was driven partly by cheaper iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P4-S2.translation: 根据西歇尔的深入分析，尽管铁钉价格暴跌部分得益于铁原料降价和能源成本下降，但绝大部分功劳都要归功于制钉制造商们——他们找到了将钢材高效加工转化为铁钉的更先进、更高效的生产工艺（more efficient ways / Increased productivity）。

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P5-S1.text: Nails themselves have changed over the years. But Sichel studied them because they haven't changed much. Roman lamps and Roman chariots are very different from LED strips and sports cars, but Roman nails are still clearly nails.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P5-S1.translation: 铁钉本身随岁月流逝当然发生过演变；但西歇尔之所以深入研究铁钉，恰恰是因为它们在本质上并没有发生太大的改变（haven't changed much / remained basically the same since Roman times）。罗马时代的油灯和双轮战车与当今的 LED 灯带和超级跑车天差地别，但两千年前的罗马铁钉却依然清晰可辨就是不折不扣的铁钉。

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P6-S1.text: I make no apology for being obsessed by a particular feature of everyday objects: their price. I am an economist, after all. After writing two books about the history of inventions, one thing I've learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it's the cheap technologies that change the world.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P6-S1.translation: 我毫不掩饰自己对日常物品一个极其特殊特征的由衷痴迷——那就是它们的价格。毕竟，我是一名经济学者。在撰写了两部关于人类发明史的专著之后，我所领悟到的最深刻真谛便是：尽管那些令人着迷的精密复杂高精尖技术（sophisticated technologies）独揽了世间所有的舆论炒作与光环；然而，真正带来翻天覆地革命性变革、深刻改变整个人类世界的，恰恰是那些成本极其低廉的廉价技术（cheap technologies change the world / bring about revolutionary change）！

ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P7-S1.text: The Gutenberg printing press transformed civilisation not by changing the nature of writing but by changing its cost—and it would have achieved little without a parallel collapse in the price of surfaces to write on, thanks to an often overlooked technology called paper.
ky-en1-2024-r-t1#P7-S1.translation: 古腾堡印刷机之所以彻底重塑了人类文明，绝非因为改变了文字书写的本质属性，而是由于根本性地大幅颠覆降低了书写知识的传播成本——而且，若非得益于一种常被忽视的‘造纸术’技术使得纸张承载成本同步发生断崖式暴跌，印刷机本不可能取得如此辉煌的伟业。

ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Dr. Annie Swanepoel, a child psychiatrist, believes that there are ways to incorporate them into western life. In Germany, one scheme has paired an old people's home with a nursery. The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting. Another measure could be encouraging friendships between children in different school years to mimic the supervised mixed-age play groups in hunter-gatherer communities.
ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 儿童精神病学家安妮·斯瓦内普尔博士深信，完全有多种可行途径将这些有益模式融入西方现代生活（an approach to integrating into western society）。在德国，一项创新试点方案成功将一家养老院与一家幼儿园结对配对：养老院的老年居民们协助照料幼儿，这一制度安排与部落的共同育儿如出一辙。另一项举措则是鼓励不同年级学龄儿童之间建立跨龄友谊，以模拟再现狩猎采集部落中在大人看护下的混龄游戏小组。

ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P5-S1.text: Chaudhary said that parents now had less child care support from family and social networks than during most of human evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and maternal depression, which could have a "knock-on" benefit to child's wellbeing.
ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P5-S1.translation: 乔杜里表示，现代父母从家族与社会网络中所能获得的育儿支持，比人类演化史上的绝大多数时期都要匮乏得多；然而，引入额外的辅助照料者能够显著减轻育儿压力与产后抑郁，从而对孩子的身心福祉产生极其显著的良性‘连锁反应’红利。

ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P5-S2.text: An infant born to a hunter-gatherer society could have more than ten caregivers—this contrasts starkly to nursery settings in the UK where regulations call for a ratio of one carer to four children aged two to three.
ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P5-S2.translation: 一个出生在狩猎采集社会的婴儿能够同时拥有十多位悉心呵护的照料者——这与英国现代托儿所的制度环境形成了触目惊心的强烈反差：英国法定法规竟然要求一名照料人员独自看管照看四名两至三岁的幼童（inferred that UK nurseries ought to improve their carer-to-child ratio）！

ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P6-S1.text: While hunter-gatherer children learn from observation and imitation in mixed-age playgroups, researchers said that western "instructive teaching", where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P6-S1.translation: 部落儿童是在混龄游戏小组中通过主动观察与模仿来自然学习；而研究学者指出，西方要求学生必须僵化端坐不动的“指令灌输式教学”，很可能正是诱发注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）等心理病症的重要诱因。

ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P6-S2.text: Chaudhary said that Britain should explore the possibility that older siblings helping their parents might also enhance their own social development.
ky-en1-2024-r-t2#P6-S2.translation: 乔杜里深刻呼吁：英国应当积极探索让年长兄姐协助父母照看弟妹的现实可能性，这不仅能减轻父母重负，更能极大促进年长孩子自身的社交心智成熟发展（For a happier family, learn from the hunter-gatherers）。

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 格雷格·鲁特科夫斯基是一位享誉业界的波兰知名数字艺术家，擅长运用西方古典油画绘画风格来创作如梦似幻的史诗级奇幻风景画作。

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P1-S2.text: He has made illustrations for games such as Sony's Horizon Forbidden West, Ubisoft's Anno, Dungeons & Dragons, and Magic: The Gathering. And he's become a sudden hit in the new world of text-to-image AI generation.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 他曾为索尼的《地平线：西之绝境》、育碧的《纪元》系列、《龙与地下城》以及《万智牌》等诸多顶级游戏大作绘制插画。而如今，他更是不可思议地在‘文本生成图像’（text-to-image）的全新人工智能生成领域中一夜爆红成为顶流现象级人物！

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P2-S1.text: His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new open-source AI art generator Stable Diffusion, which was launched late last month.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 在他那独树一帜的鲜明艺术画风引领下，他的名字如今已成为上个月底刚刚重磅发布的全新开源 AI 艺术生成器 Stable Diffusion 中使用最频繁的高频提示词（prompts）之一（popular with users of an AI art generator）。

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P2-S1.text: His distinctive style is now one of the most commonly used prompts in the new open-source AI art generator Stable Diffusion, which was launched late last month.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 在他那独树一帜的鲜明艺术画风引领下，他的名字如今已成为上个月底刚刚重磅发布的全新开源 AI 艺术生成器 Stable Diffusion 中使用最频繁的高频提示词（prompts）之一（popular with users of an AI art generator）。

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P2-S2.text: The tool, along with other popular image-generation AI models, allows anyone to create impressive images based on text prompts. For example, type in "Wizard with sword and a glowing orb of magic fire fights a fierce dragon Greg Rutkowski," and the system will produce something that looks not a million miles away from works in Rutkowski's style.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P2-S2.translation: 该工具与其他流行的图像生成 AI 模型一样，允许任何普通人仅凭简单的文本提示词就能生成令人惊叹的精美图像。例如，只要输入“手持宝剑与发光魔法火球的巫师与恶龙搏斗，格雷格·鲁特科夫斯基风格”，系统就会瞬间生成一副与鲁特科夫斯基本人原作风格几乎毫无二致的惊艳画作。

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P3-S1.text: But these open-source programs are built by scraping images from the Internet, often without permission and proper attribution to artists. As a result, they are raising tricky questions about ethics and copyright. And artists like Rutkowski have had enough.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 然而，这些开源 AI 程序的底层训练数据库，全部是通过从互联网络上大肆肆意抓取图片所构建起来的——而且往往根本没有获得原作者的许可，更没有给予艺术家应有的署名权（make unauthorized use of online images / scraping without permission）。因此，它们正在引发极其棘手的学术伦理与侵犯版权法律危机。而像鲁特科夫斯基这样的原创艺术家们，对此早已彻底忍无可忍（had enough）！

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P4-S1.text: According to the website Lexica, which tracks over 10 million images and prompts generated by Stable Diffusion, Rutkowski's name has been used as a prompt around 93,000 times.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P4-S1.translation: 据专门追踪 Stable Diffusion 所生成的超1000万张图像及提示词的专业网站 Lexica 统计显示，鲁特科夫斯基的名字已被作为生成提示词疯狂调用了大约整整9.3万次之多！

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P4-S2.text: Some of the world's most famous artists, such as Michelangelo, Pablo Picasso, and Leonardo da Vinci, brought up around 2,000 prompts each or less. Rutkowski's name also features as a prompt thousands of times in the Discord of another text-to-image generator, Midjourney.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P4-S2.translation: 相比之下，包括米开朗基罗、巴勃罗·毕加索以及列奥纳多·达·芬奇在内的若干全球最顶尖艺术大师，各自被调用的提示词次数却仅有2000次左右甚至更少。在另一款热门文生图 AI 工具 Midjourney 的官方社区中，鲁特科夫斯基的名字同样被作为提示词使用了数千次之多。

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P4-S3.text: Rutkowski was initially surprised but thought it might be a good way to reach new audiences. Then he tried searching for his name to see if a piece he had worked on had been published. The online search brought back work that had his name attached to it but wasn't his.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P4-S3.translation: 鲁特科夫斯基起初深感诧异，但一度天真地以为这或许是触达全新受众的良好契机。然而随后当他在搜索引擎中输入自己的名字、试图查看自己参与的一部作品是否已公开发表时，网络搜索结果却铺天盖地地返回了大量赫然冠以他本人的大名、但根本不是他本人所创作的劣质 AI 冒牌画作（AI-generated work bearing his name）！

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P5-S1.text: "It's been just a month. What about in a year? I probably won't be able to find my work out there because [the internet] will be flooded with AI art," Rutkowski says. "That's concerning."
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P5-S1.translation: “现在才刚刚过去短短一个月。那一年之后又会变成怎样？届时我恐怕在网上连自己的真实作品都根本搜寻不到了，因为整个互联网都将被泛滥成灾的 AI 仿造艺术画作彻底淹没，”鲁特科夫斯基心有余悸地表示，“这真是令人不寒而栗的严重担忧。”

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P6-S1.text: "There is a coalition growing within artist industries to figure out how to tackle or mitigate this," says Ortiz. The group is in its early days of mobilization, which could involve pushing for new policies or regulations.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P6-S1.translation: “艺术创意产业内部正在迅速组建起一个广泛的联合同盟，以共同探讨如何坚决应对或有效遏制这一侵权危机，”插画家奥尔蒂斯表示。该联盟目前正处于初期动员阶段，其核心行动将涵盖积极推动政府出台全新的版权监管政策或法律法规。

ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P6-S2.text: One suggestion is that AI models could be trained on images in the public domain, and AI companies could forge partnerships with museums and artists, Ortiz says.
ky-en1-2024-r-t3#P6-S2.translation: 奥尔蒂斯指出，一个极具建设性的合规建议是：AI 模型未来应当仅仅基于‘公有领域’（public domain，即无版权限制）的合法图像来进行训练学习，同时 AI 科技公司应当主动与各大博物馆以及原创艺术家们建立起正规授权的商业合作共赢伙伴关系（adopt a different strategy for AI model training）。

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P1-S1.text: The miracle of the Chesapeake Bay lies not in its depths, but in the complexity of its natural construction: the interaction of fresh and saline waters, and the mix of land and water.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 切萨皮克湾的伟大奇迹并不在于其深邃的海水深度，而在于其自然构造的极度错综复杂性：淡水与咸水的交融互动，以及陆地与水域的鬼斧神工般交错结合。

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P2-S1.text: All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 然而，这一切宝贵生态在上个月底均被置于巨大的毁灭性风险之中——当时美国联邦最高法院在涉及爱达荷州的一起诉讼案件（萨基特案）中作出一项判决，大幅削减剥夺了美国环境保护署（EPA）依法监管湿地与水道的法定权威（weakens the EPA's regulatory power / far less authority to regulate）。

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P2-S1.text: All this was put at great risk late last month, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in an Idaho case that provides the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) far less authority to regulate wetlands and waterways.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 然而，这一切宝贵生态在上个月底均被置于巨大的毁灭性风险之中——当时美国联邦最高法院在涉及爱达荷州的一起诉讼案件（萨基特案）中作出一项判决，大幅削减剥夺了美国环境保护署（EPA）依法监管湿地与水道的法定权威（weakens the EPA's regulatory power / far less authority to regulate）。

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P2-S2.text: Specifically, a 5-4 majority decided that wetlands protected by the EPA under its Clean Water Act authority must have a "continuous surface connection to bodies of water." This narrowing of the regulatory scope was a victory for builders, mining operators and other commercial interests that are often at odds with environmental rules. And it carries "significant repercussions for water quality and flood control throughout the United States," as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 具体而言，最高法院以5比4的微弱多数裁定：EPA 依据《清洁水法》管辖保护的湿地，必须与通航水体拥有“连续的地表水体连接”。这一监管范围的急剧大幅收窄，成为了房地产建筑商、采矿开发商以及其他长期与环保法规相抵触的商业利益集团的狂欢胜利；正如布雷特·卡瓦诺大法官所严肃指出的那样，该裁决将对“全美范围内的水质安全与防洪控制带来极其深远严重的灾难性恶果”。

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P3-S1.text: In Maryland, the good news is that there are many state laws in place that provide wetlands protections. But that's a very short-sighted view, particularly when it comes to the Chesapeake Bay.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 在马里兰州，看似利好的消息是该州自身拥有完备健全的州级法律来提供湿地保护。但这显然是一种极其短视狭隘的孤立视角，尤其在面对庞大的切萨皮克湾生态系统时更是如此。

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P3-S2.text: The reality is that water, and the pollutants that so often come with it, don't respect state boundaries. The Chesapeake draws from a 64,000-square-mile watershed that extends into Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia, the District of Columbia and Delaware. Will those jurisdictions extend the same protections now denied under Sackett v. EPA? Perhaps some, but all? That seems unlikely.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 残酷的客观现实在于：水流以及水中所携带的致命污染物，根本不会理会行政州界的人为阻隔。切萨皮克湾的水源汇集自一个横跨6.4万平方英里的庞大流域，延伸纵深至弗吉尼亚州、宾夕法尼亚州、纽约州、西弗吉尼亚州、华盛顿特区以及特拉华州。这些跨辖区地方政府难道会主动填补在萨基特案中被剥夺的同等严格保护吗？或许有个别州会，但指望所有州都照做？这几乎是痴人说梦（That seems unlikely / author feels worried about the future）！

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P4-S1.text: It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P4-S1.translation: 将此类最高法院判决轻描淡写地视为仅仅是在维护土地所有者的私有财产权，不仅极其幼稚简单，更是极其荒谬误导——因为该判决给其下游周边邻近地区所带来的恶果是如此毁灭性惨烈。

ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P4-S2.text: And it's a reminder that the EPA's involvement in the Chesapeake Bay Program has long been crucial as the means to transcend the influence of deep-pocketed special interests in neighboring states. Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren't thinking about next year's blue crab harvest in Maryland when they decide whether to spread animal waste on their fields, yet the runoff into nearby creeks can have enormous impact downstream.
ky-en1-2024-r-t4#P4-S2.translation: 这也再次深刻提醒世人：长期以来，EPA 深度介入切萨皮克湾综合治理计划，作为超越邻近各州财大气粗特殊利益集团地方保护主义干扰的核心手段，始终发挥着至关重要的统筹引领作用（crucial as means to transcend special interests / ensured the coordination of protection efforts）。举一个极其生动有力的例证：宾夕法尼亚州的农场主在决定是否往自家农田喷洒动物粪便肥料时，根本绝不会去替下游马里兰州明年的蓝蟹捕捞丰收着想；然而化肥农药径流流入附近溪流，却会对整个下游生态产生毁灭性的巨大冲击！

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P1-S1.text: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after ground-breaking research showed that Shakespeare does benefit children's literacy and emotional development. But only if you act him out.
ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 这位来自埃文河畔斯特拉特福德的昔日文法学校男孩（莎士比亚），在学术界结结实实地打出了一记漂亮的重拳——一项开创性的重磅研究表明：莎士比亚戏剧确实对儿童的读写能力与情感心智发育大有裨益（does benefit children's literacy and emotional development）。但这有一个绝对的前提：孩子们必须亲自将其搬上舞台演绎出来（play the roles in Shakespeare / act him out）！

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P2-S1.text: A study found that a "rehearsal room" approach to teaching Shakespeare broadened children's vocabulary and the complexity of their writing as well as their emotional literacy.
ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: 一项实证研究发现，采用戏剧“排练室”（rehearsal room）沉浸式方法来教授莎士比亚戏剧，不仅大幅拓宽了儿童的词汇量，显著提升了其书面写作的复杂程度，更极大增强了他们的情感共情素养（emotional literacy）。

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P2-S2.text: "The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.
ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P2-S2.translation: “这项研究雄辩地证明，专业演员的工作演绎方式，对孩子们如何运用语言以及他们如何审视看待自我，带来了极其深远重大的积极改变，”委托开展该项研究的皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC）教育总监 Jacqui O'Hanlon 表示。

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 这些学生被随机分成实验目标组与对照组（to find whether the change in instruction enhances learning outcomes）；两组学生被要求以《暴风雨》中遭遇海难后的斐迪南王子的第一人称角色，写下一封漂流瓶信件。其中，实验目标组在阅读文本的同时，被安排参与了整整30分钟的沉浸式戏剧表演角色扮演活动。

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P5-S1.text: The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on "desert island clichés" such as palm trees, target pupils were "more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions".
ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P5-S1.translation: 这项名为《行动之时》（Time to Act）的权威研究还发现：对照组学生通篇严重依赖诸如棕榈树等“荒岛陈词滥调”（desert island clichés），暴露出描写景物能力的严重匮乏薄弱（shows their weakness in description）；相比之下，实验目标组学生笔下的描写则显得“更具拓展张力，勾勒出了关于天空、海洋以及大气气象环境的更加广袤深邃的宏伟画卷”。

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P6-S1.text: O'Hanlon said she had been most surprised by the "emotional literacy that was evident in the [target] children's writing" and that they were "more resilient in their writing, more hopeful".
ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P6-S1.translation: O'Hanlon 女士坦言，最令她感到惊艳与震撼的，莫过于“实验组孩子书面表达中所展露出的极其惊人的情感共情素养（emotional literacy）”，他们在字里行间展现出了“更坚韧的内心力量与更满怀希望的情感光芒”。

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P6-S2.text: She added: "The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes." The study showed the importance of embedding the arts in education, she said.
ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P6-S2.translation: 她进一步补充道：“这种深刻的情感理解力极其清晰鲜明，它很可能正归功于排练室体验过程——在排练中你早已习惯了通过想象去体悟一切。孩子们能够极其自如地精准描绘各种不同的复杂情绪状态，而戏剧的核心本质正是让你设身处地穿上别人的鞋子换位思考（put yourself in different shoes / identifying with literary characters）。”她由衷感叹道，这项研究雄辩地证明了将艺术深度融入基础教育的极端重要性。

ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P7-S1.text: But could the results be replicated with any old dramatist? O'Hanlon said more research would be needed but suggested that Shakespeare's use of 20,000 words, compared with the everyday 2,000 words, gave a "massive expansion of language into children's lives", which was combined with children "using their whole bodies to bring words to life".
ky-en1-2025-r-t1#P7-S1.translation: 然而，这般辉煌的教学成果能否在任何其他古代剧作家的作品中轻易复制？O'Hanlon 表示虽然仍需更多对比实证研究，但她深刻指出：莎士比亚戏剧中庞大浩瀚的20,000个词汇量（相比之下现代人日常词汇仅有可怜的2,000个），给孩子们的语言世界带来了“空前巨大的语言暴涨式拓展扩张”，而这种浩瀚词汇又与孩子们“运用全身肢体去赋予词语鲜活生命（bring words to life）”的沉浸式表演完美结合在了一起（inferred that the new teaching method may work best with Shakespeare）。

ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P1-S2.text: The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling. At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.
ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 他们声称：气候危机迫在眉睫，我们必须立刻削减自身那些高能耗的计算机模型模拟运算；退一万步讲，我们也必须让自身的能源消耗变得远为更加绿色可持续。

ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P2-S1.text: It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites—the tools we scientists need to measure the planet's pulse—demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation.
ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 毋庸置疑，我们的前沿实验室、精密科研仪器、运载火箭与人造卫星——这些我们科学家用来把脉地球跳动节律所不可或缺的利器——在其建造制造与日常运转过程中确实都需要消耗海量的巨大能源（Energy-intensive research work is inevitable）。

ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P2-S2.text: And it is equally true that science's unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world. According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 per cent of the world's electricity.
ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 同样不可否认的是，科学界对数据的无尽渴求导致全球各地高能耗数据中心如雨后春笋般疯狂涌现。根据国际能源署（IEA）的权威统计，这些建筑设施目前消耗了全球整整约1%的总电力供应。

ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P3-S2.translation: 如果我们甚至无法精准追踪大气中二氧化碳的确切存量、来源路径以及排放责任方，我们又究竟如何向政策制定者提供关于减少碳排放的最佳施策建议？科技研发所产生的碳排放完全是物有所值的崇高投入（well spent）——从根本长远来看，这些科研成果将真正捍卫守护我们整个人类地球的未来命运（carbon emissions are justifiable in the long run）！

ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P5-S2.translation: 该奖项的往届得主之一、澳大利亚新南威尔士大学的马丁·格林教授，正是当今全球绝大多数太阳能电池板中广泛应用的“钝化发射极及背部接触”（PERC）太阳能技术的伟大发明者。正是得益于他的这项科学发明，我们今天才真正拥有了大幅降低全球碳排放的切实胜算与丰硕回报（the rewards of scientific endeavours）！

ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P6-S2.text: A great example of this is Europe's largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P6-S2.translation: 这其中最卓越的典范，莫过于坐落于芬兰的欧洲最大超级计算机 LUMI——它令人惊叹地实现了“负碳排放”（carbon negative）。该超算中心设于一座旧造纸厂内，全部依靠邻近河流的水力清洁能源驱动，而其散发的余热更是直接为周边卡亚尼小镇的居民提供市政供暖（LUMI is a model of sustainability efforts）！

ky-en1-2025-r-t2#P7-S1.text: If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.

ky-en1-2025-r-t3#P1-S1.text: Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns on Wall Street that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was.

ky-en1-2025-r-t3#P1-S2.text: But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.
ky-en1-2025-r-t3#P1-S2.translation: 然而，流媒体时代的全面降临却成为了一批意想不到的真正赢家的巨大横财摇钱树：数字盗版黑产犯罪分子利用破解软件在几秒钟内便能从正规在线视频平台抓取扒下整部电影或电视剧集，并将其架设在自己的非法盗播网站上——这些非法盗版平台每年单凭广告和会员订阅就能疯狂敛财吸金约20亿美元（legitimate streaming services are confronted with a real threat）！

ky-en1-2025-r-t3#P2-S1.text: With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that's working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.

ky-en1-2025-r-t3#P4-S2.text: Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy.

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P1-S1.text: Visit any antiques store and you'll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964-1965 World's Fair, the ephemera of history.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 走进任何一家古董旧货店，你都会邂逅无数来自过往岁月的珍贵历史器物遗存：泛黄的老照片、手写书信、详细介绍1964至1965年世博会辛克莱恐龙展览的折页宣传册——这些看似过眼云烟的“历史短暂遗存物”（ephemera of history）。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P1-S2.text: Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they are still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 然而，这些物件却并非真正如浮云般转瞬即逝，因为在历经数十年、乃至数个世纪的风霜洗礼之后，它们依然完好地留存于世。为什么？因为它们是实实在在、触手可及的“有形实体”（tangible / bring up the issue of preservation）！

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S1.text: Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation?
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 你是否曾深入思考过无形格式——即纯粹的数字信息——的生命周期？尤其是考虑到那些生产制造此类数字制品的创作者们，在创作时几乎极少会为其日后的长期留存保存做出任何周全预案？

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S2.text: For millennia, we've known what we've known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators' neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 数千年来，人类之所以能够通晓过往的历史认知，全赖那些历经劫难而幸存下来的古代文物——哪怕其最初的原作者当年对其疏于照料。实体器物本身就是直接承载并传递历史信息的物理介质（tangible artifacts convey information in a more direct way / thing itself is the medium）！

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S3.text: At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S3.translation: 在被创造之初，人们往往并未做出任何刻意保存的努力，但传统的模拟实体材料却天然拥有一线幸存生机，得以代代相传成为传记作家、历史学家和小说家所赖以考据的珍贵历史记录。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S4.text: Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information. One of S.R. Ranganathan's foundational Laws of Library Science is "Save the time of the reader." Thus, librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 图书馆与档案馆传统上一直默默肩负着信息组织整理、长期保存以及提供查阅的崇高神圣职责。图书情报学奠基人阮冈纳赞的基本法则之一便是“节省读者的时间”。因此，图书馆员们竭尽全力将有形实体文献全面数字化，使得全球各地的科研学者能够闪电般快速检索和调阅馆藏。其最终结果是造就了一座令人眼花缭乱的浩瀚历史文献宝库，但也随之带来了在浩如烟海中“大海捞针”的新难题。

Ranganathan's foundational Laws of Library Science is "Save the time of the reader." Thus, librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P2-S4.translation: 图书馆与档案馆传统上一直默默肩负着信息组织整理、长期保存以及提供查阅的崇高神圣职责。图书情报学奠基人阮冈纳赞的基本法则之一便是“节省读者的时间”。因此，图书馆员们竭尽全力将有形实体文献全面数字化，使得全球各地的科研学者能够闪电般快速检索和调阅馆藏。其最终结果是造就了一座令人眼花缭乱的浩瀚历史文献宝库，但也随之带来了在浩如烟海中“大海捞针”的新难题。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P3-S1.text: Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cellphone and saying, "it's all in here" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 然而，图书馆员们的无私奉献在客观上却反噬了我们自身——当终端用户高举着智能手机、指着随时随地可触达的海量信息炫耀说“所有资料都在手机里了”并以此作为证据宣称“当今图书馆对科研人员已不再那么至关重要”时，这种极度盲目短视的言论导致图书馆的核心价值遭到了严重低估与贬损（undervaluation of libraries / libraries are less vital）。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 然而，图书馆员们的无私奉献在客观上却反噬了我们自身——当终端用户高举着智能手机、指着随时随地可触达的海量信息炫耀说“所有资料都在手机里了”并以此作为证据宣称“当今图书馆对科研人员已不再那么至关重要”时，这种极度盲目短视的言论导致图书馆的核心价值遭到了严重低估与贬损（undervaluation of libraries / libraries are less vital）。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P3-S2.text: Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 然而，那种唾手可得的信息普适获取究竟是如何成为可能的？更重要的是，它又是靠谁在日复一日地严密维护？究竟是谁在精心筛选守护那些被留存的历史？当面对与生俱来的“原生数字信息”时，那令人不寒而栗的残酷答案只能是：如果没有图书馆员和档案管理学家的默默坚守，世上将再无任何人去拯救它们！数字信息实际上远比传统实体模拟信息需要多得多的悉心呵护与照料。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P3-S2.text: Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 然而，那种唾手可得的信息普适获取究竟是如何成为可能的？更重要的是，它又是靠谁在日复一日地严密维护？究竟是谁在精心筛选守护那些被留存的历史？当面对与生俱来的“原生数字信息”时，那令人不寒而栗的残酷答案只能是：如果没有图书馆员和档案管理学家的默默坚守，世上将再无任何人去拯救它们！数字信息实际上远比传统实体模拟信息需要多得多的悉心呵护与照料。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S1.text: Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that's saved, not the information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S1.translation: 即使某个数字物件侥幸被留存下来，最终被保存的往往也仅仅只是物理存储载体本身，而非内部承载的数据信息本身。随着科学技术的飞速迭代演进，一旦某种特定格式沦为过时淘汰（format becomes obsolete），该物件便彻底沦为了毫无用处的废品。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S1.text: Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that's saved, not the information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless.

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S2.text: Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this?
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S2.translation: 你是否曾无比无助绝望地凝视着一张古早的 ZIP 软盘（ZIP disk），心中抓狂暗想：我究竟该如何把里面的文件导出来（possibility of losing information in obsolete formats）？

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S2.text: Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this?
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S2.translation: 你是否曾无比无助绝望地凝视着一张古早的 ZIP 软盘（ZIP disk），心中抓狂暗想：我究竟该如何把里面的文件导出来（possibility of losing information in obsolete formats）？

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S3.text: Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S3.translation: 如果缺乏对数字资产持续不断的技术迁移迭代，在可预见的未来里，一场令所有历史学者彻夜难眠的终极噩梦就将不可避免地降临：当数字形态全面取代模拟实体的那一刻起，人类文明的全部历史记录竟然戛然而止、彻底中断！

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S3.text: Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P4-S3.translation: 如果缺乏对数字资产持续不断的技术迁移迭代，在可预见的未来里，一场令所有历史学者彻夜难眠的终极噩梦就将不可避免地降临：当数字形态全面取代模拟实体的那一刻起，人类文明的全部历史记录竟然戛然而止、彻底中断！

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P5-S1.text: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P5-S1.translation: 作为一名日常工作深度围绕特藏文献与数字资产展开的职业图书馆员，我完全感同身受历史学者们内心的深夜梦魇；如果我宣称当前世上已存在某种一劳永逸的全面数字保存解决方案，那绝对是在撒谎欺骗。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P5-S1.text: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P5-S1.translation: 作为一名日常工作深度围绕特藏文献与数字资产展开的职业图书馆员，我完全感同身受历史学者们内心的深夜梦魇；如果我宣称当前世上已存在某种一劳永逸的全面数字保存解决方案，那绝对是在撒谎欺骗。

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P5-S2.text: Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future. Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use information. Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won't find it an impossible one.
ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P5-S2.translation: 然而，广大科研学者尚可感到些许欣慰的是：世上仍有数以万计的图书馆员在全身心致力于为当今与未来的学者发掘、整理并守护保存宝贵的数字信息。图书馆员处于极其独特的枢纽地位，最懂得终端用户如何检索与使用信息。因此，我们在识别、保存并提供数字器物可获取性方面发挥着不可或缺的核心作用——从而确保，未来的科研人员在数字学术领域施展身手时，即便会发现这处领域充满重重艰巨挑战（Keeping digital historical records is a challenge），但也绝不至于绝望地发现这是一件彻底不可能完成的天方夜谭！

ky-en1-2025-r-t4#P5-S2.text: Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future. Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use information. Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won't find it an impossible one.

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P1-S1.text: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward. They've helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P1-S1.translation: 数千年来，驴在推动整个人类文明向前演进发展中始终发挥着绝对至关重要的关键作用（critical for human civilizations' development / propelling civilizations forward）。它们协助人类拉动轮式车辆、驮运往来旅者，并将海量货物运往世界各地。

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P1-S2.text: But where and when these animals first became intertwined with humans has been a mystery. Now, researchers have used genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa - about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses. The team published their findings in the journal Science this month.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P1-S2.translation: 然而，这些动物究竟是在何时何地最初与人类命运交织在一起的，长久以来一直是个未解之谜。如今，科研人员通过对200多头驴的基因组测序分析，成功将它们的驯化起源追溯至大约7000年前发生在东非的一起单一驯化事件——这比人类驯服马匹还要早整整约3000年。该研究团队于本月在《科学》（Science）期刊上正式发表了这一开创性发现。

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P2-S1.text: "Through their DNA, the animals are telling their history themselves," co-author Samantha Brooks, an equine researcher at the University of Florida, says in a statement. "We usually only get the human's side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened. Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived."
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P2-S1.translation: “通过自身的 DNA 密码，这些动物正在亲自向我们诉说它们自身的历史，”佛罗里达大学马科动物研究专家、该论文合著者萨曼莎·布鲁克斯在声明中表示，“我们通常只能通过人类留下的文字文献记载来了解人类单方面的历史视角，但显然书面历史并不总是能准确记录下事情究竟是如何发生的。通过深入观察这些 DNA 基因序列，我们获得了一份关于这些动物曾生活的生态环境及其所历经幸存历程的珍贵生物学实证见证（Genetic analysis offers insight into the history of donkeys）。”

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P3-S1.text: The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe. They also looked at genomes from 15 wild equids and 31 earlier donkeys that lived between about 4,000 and 100 years ago.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P3-S1.translation: 研究人员详尽检测了来自全球31个国家的207头现代驴的基因组，同时深入分析了15头野生马科动物以及31头生活在大约4000年至100年前的古代早期驴的基因组数据。

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P3-S2.text: The team reconstructed the animals' evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event: when herders in Kenya and the Horn of Africa tamed wild asses. They then traced how the animals spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia about 2,500 years later.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P3-S2.translation: 该科研团队成功重建了驴的生物演化树，并运用先进计算机模型精准锁定了驯化事件发生的具体节点：即肯尼亚和非洲之角的早期游牧牧民首次成功驯服非洲野驴的时刻。随后，他们深入追踪调查了这些动物如何在大约2500年后广泛扩散蔓延至非洲大陆其他地区以及欧亚大陆（investigated how donkeys dispersed widely in the world / spread across continent into Europe and Asia）。

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P4-S1.text: Though it's still unclear why the original domestication happened, Science News' Freda Kreier reports that the event coincided with the Sahara growing larger and drier.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P4-S1.translation: 尽管最初驯化发生的深层动机机制尚无定论，但《科学新闻》记者弗里达·克赖尔报道指出：该驯化事件在时间节点上恰好与撒哈拉地区面积不断扩大、气候急剧干旱化的地质时期高度吻合。

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P4-S2.text: "Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at navigating deserts," co-author Ludovic Orlando, an evolutionary biologist at Paul Sabatier University in France, tells the publication. Prehistoric humans may have tamed donkeys to help them navigate the expanding Sahara.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P4-S2.translation: “在负重驮物方面，驴是不折不扣的冠军王者，而且它们极其擅长在严酷荒漠环境中长途穿行，”该论文合著者、法国保罗·萨巴蒂尔大学演化生物学家卢多维克·奥兰多向媒体解释道。史前人类当初驯化驴，极可能正是为了借助其非凡耐力协助自身穿越日益干旱扩张的广袤撒哈拉沙漠（Orlando provides a possible explanation for why original domestication happened）。

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P5-S1.text: Researchers say these findings could help put donkeys in the spotlight. The animals could benefit from more research: Currently, there are no published genomes from donkeys located south of the Equator in Africa. But understanding where the animals were first domesticated could guide archaeologists to a narrow region to search for insights about the original tamed donkeys.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P5-S1.translation: 研究学者们表示，这些重大突破有助于让驴重新走进科研聚光灯的中心。这一物种理应得到更多学术研究的青睐：目前，非洲赤道以南地区尚未有已发表的驴基因组公开数据。然而，明确了解这些动物最初被驯化的具体发源地，能够精准指引考古学家聚焦于某个特定狭长区域，去深入发掘搜寻关于早期被驯化驴的珍贵实证线索。

ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P6-S1.text: Not only does human-understanding the equines' genetic makeup help reveal their contribution to human history, but it also might improve their management in the future, as climate change alters the planet's environment, write the authors.
ky-en1-2026-r-t1#P6-S1.translation: 论文作者在文末深刻总结指出：人类全面掌握并深刻理解马科动物的基因构成，不仅有助于系统揭示它们对整个人类历史所做出的不可磨灭的卓越贡献，而且在气候变化深刻重塑地球生态环境的当下，还极有可能有助于在未来大幅改善与提升对驴这一物种的科学繁育与管理保护水平（research could help with better management of donkeys）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P1-S1.text: There's no business like show business – but in Los Angeles, it feels like there's no business at all.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P1-S1.translation: 俗话说“没有任何行业能比得上演艺娱乐业”——然而在如今的洛杉矶，人们所感受到的却是整个文娱行业几乎彻底陷入了万马齐喑的全面停滞状态。

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P1-S2.text: If that sounds melodramatic, consider this: The Art Directors Guild, a labor union representing about 3,000 film workers, has suspended a training program and issued a statement explaining that "we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession." This is a reaction to Hollywood's decline, which is reaching a critical point for the industry and Southern California.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P1-S2.translation: 如果这听起来像是在耸人听闻大惊小怪，不妨看看这样一个铁打的事实：代表约3000名影视美术工作者的行业工会“美术指导工会”（Art Directors Guild）已正式叫停了其新人培训培养计划，并发布了一份令人心酸的公开声明解释称：“摸着良心，我们已无法再凭良知去鼓励诸位投身我们这一职业行当了。”这正是对好莱坞日趋衰落萧条所做出的本能应激反应——这场危机对整个影视产业及南加州地区而言，目前已赫然逼近了生死攸关的临界拐点（reveals the gloomy situation of Hollywood）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P2-S1.text: Production has been slipping away from Hollywood since the 1950s, but the effects have never been more apparent than at present.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P2-S1.translation: 自20世纪50年代以来，影视制作项目便一直在源源不断地逃离好莱坞，但这种流失带来的惨烈破坏性影响却从未像当今这般触目惊心显而易见。

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P2-S2.text: Other regions in the United States, Canada and Europe have steadily increased incentives to attract TV shows and movies, leaving California in the dust. Georgia offers up to 30% in transferable tax credits on film and TV production costs, plus an additional 10% increase on the base tax credit if the project includes a Georgia promotional logo.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P2-S2.translation: 美国其他州、加拿大以及欧洲等地区纷纷持续大幅加码税收激励措施以吸引电视剧和电影剧组前去拍摄，让加利福尼亚州被远远甩在身后。例如，乔治亚州针对影视制作成本提供了高达整整30%的可转让税收抵免优惠，如果作品中嵌入乔治亚州的宣传标识，还能在基础税收抵免上再额外追加10%的丰厚减免（illustrate efforts to lure production with tax incentives）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P3-S1.text: Even as California lost a huge volume of production to other locations, there was still plenty of film production taking place in Los Angeles before this year. We were kept afloat by "peak TV", the glut of content that was required by the explosion of streaming services.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P3-S1.translation: 即便加州已将海量制作业务拱手让给了其他地区，但在今年之前，洛杉矶本地依然保持着相当规模的影视拍摄体量。此前我们之所以能够勉强维持繁荣而不至于沉沦，全赖所谓的“电视巅峰期”（peak TV）——即各大流媒体平台的爆发式野蛮扩张所催生的过剩内容狂潮；然而随着流媒体平台战略优先级的急剧调整转向（Streamers changed their strategic priorities），这一泡沫期已戛然而止。

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P4-S1.text: If productions in Southern California dip below a critical level for too long, the industry's essential talent will drift away along with enormous sums of revenue.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P4-S1.translation: 如果南加州的影视制作量在危险的临界水平之下持续低迷徘徊过久，整个行业的核心骨干专业人才就将伴随着巨额的商业收入一同远走高飞、大量流失到外地（entertainment industry might face a brain drain to other places / essential talent will drift away）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P4-S2.text: Persuading studios to film here would become much more challenging if we couldn't offer a deep bench of local film workers, on-screen talent and local businesses that support the entertainment industry.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P4-S2.translation: 如果我们自身无法再提供由庞大本地影视幕后技工、台前优秀演员以及配套文娱支持企业所构筑的雄厚专业人才储备梯队，那么日后要想说服各大影视制片厂重返这里拍摄，将会变得空前艰难。

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P5-S1.text: That's why the California Film Commission and its Los Angeles counterpart, Film LA, should act now, before it's too late. These agencies and other government bodies should dramatically improve incentives to keep our current shows and attract new productions to Los Angeles.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P5-S1.translation: 这正是为什么加州电影委员会及其洛杉矶对口机构 Film LA 必须立刻果断采取行动、切莫坐失良机的原因所在。这些主管机构及其他各级政府部门应当大刀阔斧地显著提升税收政策激励力度，以全力保住我们现有的影视剧组，并吸引更多全新的影视项目落户洛杉矶。

ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P5-S2.text: Let's go on with the show... and make sure the show doesn't go on without us.
ky-en1-2026-r-t2#P5-S2.translation: 让我们继续唱好这场时代大戏……并务必全力确保这场全球娱乐盛宴在未来绝对不能抛下我们独自上演（California should strive to maintain its position in the industry）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P1-S1.text: The pioneers of wireless saw it as a gift to all the people. Sir John Reith said that it would end "isolation of the spirit" and rejoiced: "It does not matter how many thousands may be listening, there is always enough for others… the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously."
ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P1-S1.translation: 早期无线电广播的先驱们将其由衷视为一项馈赠给全人类所有人的崇高礼物。约翰·里斯爵士（Sir John Reith）曾满怀激情地断言，无线电广播将彻底终结“人类心灵的孤独隔绝”，并欣喜若狂地赞叹道：“无论此刻已有成千上万人在同时收听，它所蕴含的信息养分对于其他人来说永远充裕丰盛……无论是绝顶天才还是懵懂愚人，无论是豪门巨富还是赤贫寒士，都能在同一时刻毫无门槛地平等收听（wireless was accessible to everyone）！”

ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P2-S1.text: Between two great wars this technological innovation built a new kind of national consciousness. Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beatty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939. She draws on letters, diaries and fiction, and a 1939 field notebook of verbatim audience research by Winifred Gill.
ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P2-S1.translation: 在两次世界大战之间的风云岁月里，这项伟大的技术创新成功铸就了一种全新的国民共同体意识。本周在牛津大学博德利图书馆（Bodleian in Oxford）正式开展的一场由贝蒂·鲁本斯精心策划的专著出版与历史文献展览，翔实记录了无线电广播在1922年至1939年期间如何深刻颠覆改变了早期公众的日常生活（theme is the impact of radio on its early audience）。她广泛调阅了当年的书信、私人日记、文学小说，以及由威妮弗雷德·吉尔于1939年开展的一线受众逐字逐句田野调研笔记。

ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P3-S1.text: There's fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness. A cartoon mocks a group failing to converse because they're all in headphones. People report that broad music made workmen whistle new tunes. A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and "talking on the brush handle".
ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P3-S1.translation: 在当年普通人尽情享受这一纯粹新奇体验的鲜活证言中充满了无尽乐趣：一幅讽刺漫画幽默嘲弄了一群人因为各自戴着笨重耳机而无法彼此交流；有记录显示，广播音乐让流水线工人们随口吹出各种全新的动听口哨曲调；一位家庭主妇甚至反映，自从无线电广播走进千家万户之后，街头的争吵斗殴明显减少了，但邻里之间停下脚步“靠在扫帚把上闲聊家常”（talking on the brush handle / having a casual chat）的温馨场景也同样变少了。

ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P4-S1.text: By and large the wireless was welcome. I loved the man from the Thirties research who found that wireless suddenly offered "a lot of variety… things I thought I'd never be interested in… ice hockey, perhaps".
ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P4-S1.translation: 总体而言，无线电广播在当年受到了全社会最热烈的欢迎。我由衷喜爱30年代受众调研中那位普通男子的生动感言——他惊喜地发现广播突然为他展现了“极其纷繁多样的广阔世界……许多我曾以为自己这辈子绝不会感兴趣的事物，比如冰球比赛，如今竟然听得津津有味”。

ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P4-S2.text: True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task. In my own book about radio I recorded how, on one drive: "I caught up with the news, learnt some 17th-century history, and was startlingly educated by an unpretentious programme on the history of the stethoscope."
ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P4-S2.translation: 确实如此：在数字化时代降临前长达80多年的漫长岁月里，传统的“线性语言广播”为世人带来了不可多得的“意外收获与偶得惊喜之礼”（gift of serendipity / radio listeners could make unexpected gains）——它能够随机点亮枯燥乏味的驾车旅途或单调繁重的手工劳作。在我自己撰写的关于广播历史的专著中，我就曾深情记录下自己在一次驱车途中的真实奇遇：“我不仅顺畅跟进了时事新闻，意外学到了17世纪的历史知识，更被一档关于听诊器发明史的质朴无华节目深深启迪，获得了令人惊叹的意外新知！”

ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P5-S1.text: But radio's enriching serendipity is ebbing. With multiple networks and countless podcasts, a smartphone user selects what to hear and when. And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs.
ky-en1-2026-r-t3#P5-S1.translation: 然而令人唏嘘的是，广播曾赋予人类的那种丰盈充沛的“意外惊喜”（serendipity），如今却在悄然退潮消逝。面对层出不穷的网络流媒体与数不胜数的个性化播客，智能手机用户只按个人偏好精准筛选何时收听何种特定内容。诚然，戴着耳机漫步收听自己所爱固然美妙；但这种看似无限的自由选择，却在无形中诱导促使我们将自己紧紧蜷缩退缩到狭隘的小众利基兴趣以及单一同温层的固有偏见信念之中（people should adopt a sensible attitude to innovations / shrink into niche beliefs）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P1-S1.text: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to "put everything out," he recalled. But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona's Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P1-S1.translation: 当汤姆·斯威特纳姆在20世纪70年代加入美国国家森林局工作时，他回忆道当时上级赋予他的唯一铁律指令便是“扑灭眼前的一切林火”。然而，当斯威特纳姆后来进入亚利桑那大学著名的树木年轮研究实验室攻读研究生时，他却极其震惊地发现：在欧洲殖民者最初踏上北美大陆之前的数百年间，这片土地上竟然密集存在着反复发生的大量野火历史记录（surprised by the number of wildfires in precolonial times）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P1-S2.text: Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P1-S2.translation: 在他所深入检测分析的若干古树年轮中，有的古树在不同圈层的年轮间竟然触目惊心地留下了整整20多道历经大火洗礼的深重“火疤”（fire scars）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P2-S1.text: The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn't have been severe enough to kill most trees. Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P2-S1.translation: 火灾发生得如此频繁这一客观事实本身就证明：这些野火的烈度绝不可能严重到足以烧死绝大多数树木的程度。恰恰相反，越来越多的前沿科研成果雄辩地表明：频繁发生的“低强度低烈度火灾”（frequent, low-severity fires），反而让许多森林生态系统变得远为更加健康强韧（Paragraph 2 focuses on the benefits of low-severity fires）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P2-S2.text: They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease. Because flammable material couldn't build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P2-S2.translation: 这些低烈度小火能够及时清除森林中枯死及患病的残木，大幅减少树种间的恶性养分竞争，并有效遏制树木病虫害的肆意蔓延。而且正因为地表易燃枯枝落叶等可燃物没有机会长期大量堆积，野火的蔓延速度往往十分缓慢，并在烧到此前曾过火的隔离区域边界时便会自然而然地逐渐自行熄灭。

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P3-S1.text: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent. Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P3-S1.translation: 2022年，斯威特纳姆与其他科学家携手组建团队，系统汇总构建了覆盖全北美大陆的树木火疤数据库。他们建立的“北美树木年轮火疤网络”（NAFSN），为上个月重磅发表的一篇权威学术论文奠定了坚实的数据基石。

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P3-S2.text: In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall. The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P3-S2.translation: 在该项研究中，科研人员将历史上的野火发生节律与过去几十年所记录到的实际野火数据进行了跨时空对比，赫然发现了一个触目惊心的巨大“火灾短缺/赤字”（striking shortfall）。在数据库所涵盖的监测样点中，过去几十年实际经历的野火频次，竟然还不到如果没有人为灭火干预情况下预期发生自然火灾数量的四分之一（wildfires' frequency has markedly decreased）！

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P4-S1.text: This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire. "Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions."
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P4-S1.translation: 国际荒野火灾协会前主席凯利·马丁表示，这种火灾频次的骤减确实是现代消防灭火高效力的有力佐证。“然而，一味灭火压制与气候变化两者叠加造成的恶果，却反而严重削弱侵蚀了人类压制扑灭森林大火的能力——尤其是那些在最为危险致命的极端恶劣气象条件下所引爆引燃的特大暴烈火灾（modern firefighting may make severe fires harder to put out）！”

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P5-S1.text: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it. At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P5-S1.translation: 为了防止整个森林生态系统在特大火灾中化为灰烬，马丁深刻指出：人类必须主动将有益健康的良性火灾重新引回那些需要火的林区。在优胜美地国家公园（Yosemite National Park），马丁亲自统筹主导了所谓的“受控引火/规定烧除”（prescribed burns），以极大提升整片森林景观的生态韧性。

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P5-S2.text: These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park's facilities. Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P5-S2.translation: 这些引火行动均经过极其周密的科学规划，并在气象条件确保火势极易受控的安全窗口期内被有意点燃；它们成功清除了公园重点设施周围长期积聚的大量易燃燃料载量。科学研究表明，这些受控引火即便在后来遭遇最极端危险的气象条件时，也能显著大幅降低后续突发野火的破坏烈度！

ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P6-S1.text: Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said. "It's a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging," said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.
ky-en1-2026-r-t4#P6-S1.translation: 然而专家们指出，尽管广大科学家与政府官员如今越来越高度一致地认同在我们的森林中需要引入更多良性火灾，但气候变化却正在让这一策略的执行变得愈发艰难。“这是一把名副其实的双刃剑——因为在气候变化下野火正变得愈发猛烈和庞大，我们因而比以往任何时候都更加迫切需要这项受控引火工作；但与此同时，开展该项工作的窗口期与难度也随之变得极具挑战，”华盛顿大学火灾生态学家苏珊·普里查德深刻总结道（Both Martin and Prichard agree that it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns）。
